  • If the PCs free the names and expose Nocturne, the Duke's claim weakens. Caelum can stand up to his father openly, and the PCs gain advantage on all saves against fey on Night 7.
  • If Caelum is befriended and Nocturne exposed, he can renounce the Dusk Court, and his marriage-loophole (Part 2) becomes a fourth path to saving the city.
  • If Amaranth's loopholes are found, names are struck from the Book one by one, a wonderful scene of tension as the clock ticks toward midnight.

scenes.title: Fey Encounter & Temptation Table (d12)
scenes.html:
Roll once per night in the city's gardens and canals, or whenever the PCs travel through the Lanternwood, Thicketmoor, or Duskvine at dusk. Solo: roll for the hero; the companion may make one save with them or warn them of a trap (Wisdom DC 13). Group: roll once, and the temptation targets the PC with the lowest passive Insight (or a PC the fey is already fond of). Every entry gives a clear way to resist, a consequence for yielding, and usually a trick for clever players.

d12 Temptation Resist If you yield Clever trick
1 Pipwhistle lands on your nose and asks for a kiss "for luck." Politely decline thrice, or offer a button. Pocket Bargain: owe her a song (comic curse if unpaid). Pay her in gossip; she'll tell you who in the city is glimmer-sick.
2 A banquet on a moonlit lawn, laid for exactly your party, with no host in sight. Refuse to eat (Wis DC 13 if hungry). +1 Enthrallment (Hedgefolk) and you lose 1d4 hours. Offer bread and salt of your own: the hosts appear, charmed, and answer three questions.
3 Ondine invites you to rest by her pool, braiding lilies into your hair. Wis DC 13; cold water to the face. Fall asleep and roll on Dreaming Waters. Bring news of Sallowmere's humiliation and she'll trade your shoes for a secret.
4 Rillo plays your song at a canal-side revel and holds out his hand. Wis DC 14 (advantage with wax in your ears). Dance until dawn (+1 Enthrallment, 1 exhaustion); risk being led to the Lanternwood. Out-play him (Performance DC 14) and he owes you a dance and a guide.
5 A lover's voice (someone you miss, from home or here) calls from a fountain. Insight DC 15 sees through the glamour. +1 Enthrallment (Thornwake) and Nocturne learns one of your secrets. Answer with something only the real person would know; the glamour shatters, and you glimpse the Thornwake stair.
6 A gift on your pillow: a black rose and a mask of spider-silk lace, with an invitation to Nocturne's Masquerade. Refuse the gift or burn it with cold iron nearby. +1 Enthrallment (Nocturne); she can find you anywhere for 3 days. Wear the mask inside out: it shows you her true face and the way in.
7 The Sorrowkiss finds you grieving and offers to take the pain away. Wis DC 15; refuse his blown kiss. Glimmer: +1 Enthrallment, poisoned, and possibly Glimmer Craving. Weep openly and talk to him honestly: Sorrow's Mercy, and he may tell you about the glimmer vats.
8 Amaranth offers to "simplify" your debts if you'll sign just your first name. Refuse; or read the fine print (Investigation DC 17). Your name enters the Book of Forfeit Names (a claim on you on Night 7). Spot the loophole and sign "with the Accord's permission": Amaranth, delighted, owes you a favor instead.
9 A sprite sweetheart offers to "help": they'll make one suspect fall madly in love with you. Refuse. (A love charm on someone else is fey control; the Accord would void any vow that came of it.) The suspect is enthralled; any testimony they give is tainted and inadmissible, and the Veiled Sisters are furious. Ask instead for "a moment when they'll tell the truth": a free Allure box with no strings, if you can phrase it right.
10 Caelum appears at your elbow with two glasses of rose wine and a warning about Nocturne. Drink nothing from his hand without fair exchange. +1 Enthrallment (Caelum); he'll release it if he's on your side. Trade him a true secret for his: he reveals Nocturne holds Aurel Fenn's name.
11 A moth-winged courtier whispers that your dreams are the most beautiful in Vesperine. Would you share one? Wis DC 14. A happy memory is taken to the Moth Court (Side Adventure 2 can retrieve it). Offer a nightmare instead: the Moth Court is fascinated, and you gain a guide into the Cocoon Palace.
12 The roses bloom black: the Fae Duke himself speaks from a hedge and offers you anything you desire for one kiss-sealed promise. Wis DC 18, or refuse outright (Inspiration for a perfect refusal). A vow to the Duke himself (+2 Enthrallment, Dusk Court). Only the Night 7 resolution can break it. Ask him a question he can't answer. The roses wilt, and the Duke owes you a single truthful answer before Night 7.

sessions.title: Branching Structure & Endings
sessions.summary: The web of threads, wrong accusations, the Seventh Bell and Endings A–D.

scenes.title: The Shape of the Campaign
scenes.html:
The mystery is a web, not a line. After the opening scene, the PCs choose where to go each night. Think of the campaign in three movements.

                         ACT I: THE BLACK KISS (Night 1)
              Murder at the Opera -> Warrant -> Question suspects at the scene
                                       |
        +------------------------------+-------------------------------+
        |                              |                               |
  THE CITY THREAD                THE COUNTRY THREAD            THE UNDERWORLD THREAD
  Sable Palazzo, Perfumery,      Side adventures 1-5           Drowned Market, Varo,
  Atelier, Crypt, Hall of Vows   (each = 1 night, 1 Keystone)  Hale, Saltgrave (Syndicate)
        |                              |                               |
        +---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
                        |                              |
              ACT II: THE UNRAVELLING (Nights 2-5)     |
          3+ Keystones -> confront Thessaly  <---------+
          Wrong accusation -> complications (see below)
                        |
              ACT III: THE SEVENTH BELL (Night 6-7)
          Council vote, Fae Duke's heralds, the choice of endings

Approach Orders (Three Sample Playthroughs)

  • The Detective's Road (city-first). Opera → Sable Palazzo (Riddle 1, journal) → Vos Perfumery (Riddle 3) → Atelier (suspicion) → Crypt (Riddle 4) → confront Thessaly on Night 4. Fast, cerebral, leaves time for one side adventure as the city burns.
  • The Rogue's Road (underworld-first). Flirt Varo into cooperating → Drowned Market (Riddle 5) → Saltgrave (blackmail archive) → Hale flips → Hall of Vows with Varo's key (Riddle 2). The PCs end up owing the Syndicate — or owning it.
  • The Wanderer's Road (country-first). Chase the vanished carpenter into the Thicketmoor → follow moth-dust to the Lanternwood → visit the Countess. The PCs arrive back in the city with allies, a witness, and two Keystones, but only two or three nights left.

If the PCs Accuse the Wrong Person

Accusation is a public act — made before the Opera Council and sealed with a kiss-oath by the accuser. A false accusation has consequences, but it doesn't end the game:

  • Seraphine is arrested; the Syndicate, fearing she'll talk, tries to assassinate her in her cell (Night +1). Saving her makes her a loyal ally.
  • Celestine is arrested; House Morrow withdraws its guard from the city and the Unravelling advances one extra step.
  • Hale is arrested; the Lantern Watch collapses and Lanternside riots (combat encounter).
  • Varo is arrested; he breaks out within a night and leaves the PCs a rude note — and the vault key.
  • In every case, Thessaly sends the PCs a gift: a beautiful mask, and a card reading "Well done, darlings." (She overplays her hand: the card smells of bloodrose — the false accusation itself becomes a clue.)

The Climax: The Seventh Bell

On the final night, the Opera Council convenes in the Velvet Opera to name a new Oathwarden before midnight. The Fae Duke's heralds attend, smiling. Candidates may include:

  • Thessaly / Isaveth — if her identity is proven, she is the rightful heir of founding blood.
  • Lady Celestine Morrow — House Morrow is also of founding blood (her ascension is legal but loveless; she'd do it to save the city).
  • The Syndicate's puppet — a minor noble bought by Mother Brine (or Lucan Vey, if he survived).
  • A PC — the Ledger can accept anyone who is freely kissed into office by a founding heir — a loophole the Veiled Sisters will reveal if asked (History DC 16 or a gift to the Hall).

Allies earned in side adventures show up here: ogres stomp in, sirens sing, a dragon lands on the Opera roof, the Countess casts her vote.

scenes.title: Possible Endings
scenes.html:
Ending A — The Unmasking (Justice)

The PCs expose Thessaly before the Council with three or more Keystones. She does not deny it. The Ledger, sensing the truth, writes her true name across its blank pages in shining ink. She is arrested for murder — and in the same breath, legally recognized as Lady Isaveth Sable. Celestine (or another founding heir) is sworn in as Oathwarden. The city is saved, the law is upheld, and the PCs leave knowing that justice and fairness are not quite the same thing. Epilogue: Isaveth asks the PCs to visit her in the Tower of Penitence. She has made them each a mask.

Ending B — The Restored Name (Mercy)

The PCs gather the proof — and choose to present it not as a murder case, but as Aurelian's crime: the theft of a woman's identity through a corrupted oath. Under the Accord, a stolen vow voids everything built on it. With the Council's support (requires at least two allied votes: Countess Dusk, the blackmail archive, or Dame Ottoline), Isaveth is sworn in as Oathwarden. Her first act is to rewrite the Ledger so that no kiss-oath can ever take a person's self. Her second act, she insists, is to confess the murder publicly and accept exile to the Lanternwood once a successor is trained. Epilogue: the city wears no masks for one day each year: "Isaveth's Day."

Ending C — The Velvet Throne (Ambition)

The PCs seize the moment. With the vault key, the vow-page, and Thessaly's secret, they can force a bargain: a PC is kissed into the office of Oathwarden by a founding heir (Isaveth, Celestine, or — via blackmail — someone more reluctant who agrees to the deal; the kiss must still be freely given or the Ledger rejects it). The PC now controls every promise in Carnelia. Thessaly may be pardoned, exposed, or quietly sent away — the PC's choice. The Syndicate approaches with offers. The Fae Duke's heralds bow low and say, "We look forward to doing business with you." This ending opens a whole second campaign: ruling a city of secrets.

Ending D — The Seventh Bell Tolls (Failure)

If no Oathwarden is sworn by midnight on Night 7, the Accord fails. The Fae Duke arrives in a rain of rose petals and claims the founding bloodlines. Vesperine is drawn halfway into the Feywild — a city of eternal masquerade, where nobody can remove their mask. Not a game over: a dark new campaign begins, in which the PCs must journey into the Duke's court to win the city back.

sessions.title: Running Intrigue & Seduction
sessions.summary: The Allure track, the Flirt Gambit and the Fade to Black table rule.

scenes.title: Introduction
scenes.html: These optional mechanics make charm and flirtation a full pillar of play, as important as combat.

scenes.title: The Allure Track
scenes.html:
Every major NPC has an Allure track of 4 boxes. Each successful social move fills a box; each insult, clumsy lie, or misread fills nothing and may erase one.

Boxes Status Effect
0 Guarded Standard answers only; lies freely.
1 Intrigued Answers one "softened" question honestly.
2 Charmed Reveals their secret if asked directly; advantage on further Persuasion.
3 Smitten Volunteers an "under pressure" reveal without coercion; may offer help.
4 Devoted Becomes an ally; will take a risk for the PC. Romance possible if both are willing — fade to black.

Ways to fill a box: Persuasion against the NPC's flirt-angle DC; a gift that fits their taste; doing something brave in their presence; winning a game, dance, or duel; a genuinely good line at the table (GM awards one box, no roll).

The Flirt Gambit. Once per scene, a PC can try a bold flirtation to throw an NPC off balance: opposed Charisma (Persuasion or Performance) vs. the NPC's Wisdom (Insight). Success: the NPC has disadvantage on their next Deception check. Failure: the NPC laughs it off and has advantage on reading you.

Two-Way Seduction. NPCs flirt back — with agendas. When an NPC tries to charm information out of a PC, call for a Wisdom (Insight) check against the NPC's DC. On a failure, the player decides what slips out (a true fact about the investigation). This creates delicious tension without taking away player agency.

scenes.title: Fade to Black — the Table Rule
scenes.html: When two consenting adult characters head somewhere private, the GM narrates the door closing, the candle guttering, or the camera panning to the canal. Resume with "The next morning…" — and perhaps a mechanical reward: the PC gains Inspiration, and the partner moves one box up on the Allure track. Romance is never with captives, never coerced, never with anyone under the influence of mind-affecting magic, and never with minors. In Carnelia, this is also in-world law: the Accord rejects any unwilling kiss.

sessions.title: Solo Play & Group Scaling
sessions.summary: Oracle, plot twists, companions, solo scaling and scaling for 3–5 players.

scenes.title: Playing Solo (One Adventurer, With or Without a GM)
scenes.html:
Vesperine works beautifully for a single investigator — the genre of the lone detective in a decadent city. Use these rules whether a GM is running a one-on-one game or the player is running it themselves.

The Oracle (Yes/No Questions)

When you don't know the answer to a question ("Is the guard asleep?", "Does Varo know more than he's telling?"), decide how likely it is and roll a d20:

Likelihood No, and… No No, but… Yes, but… Yes Yes, and…
Unlikely 1–4 5–10 11–13 14–16 17–19 20
Even odds 1–2 3–7 8–10 11–13 14–18 19–20
Likely 1 2–4 5–7 8–10 11–16 17–20
  • And = an extra twist in the same direction (a bonus or complication).
  • But = a partial or complicated answer.
  • Doubles (if you roll a second d20 for something else and it matches) = a Plot Twist: roll on the table below.

Plot Twist Table (d8)

d8 Twist
1 A suspect is attacked — they survive, barely, and blame you.
2 Thessaly arrives with tea and pastries and an "innocent" question.
3 The Unravelling advances one step early.
4 A masked stranger slips a note into your pocket: a clue, or a trap.
5 An NPC on your Allure track confesses something they shouldn't.
6 The Thorn Syndicate sends someone to "persuade" you to drop the case.
7 A Fae herald appears and offers you a bargain.
8 Someone you trusted has been lying — reveal a lie from an ally.

NPC Reaction (d6, for when an NPC's mood isn't obvious)

1 Hostile · 2 Suspicious · 3 Busy/distracted · 4 Curious · 5 Friendly · 6 Flirtatious (fill one Allure box for free)

Companion NPCs

A solo hero may recruit one companion (two for a fragile character, e.g., a level-3 wizard). Companions are run by the GM or by the solo player, act on the hero's initiative, use a simplified stat block, and have their own opinions — and Allure tracks.

Companion Role Stat block Personality & hook
Varo Kestrel Rogue / face / lockpick spy (+10 HP; gains +1 HP Die per hero level above 3) Cheerful, unreliable, flirts with your enemies; secretly knows about the vow-page. Will betray you once — then come back.
Captain Dorian Hale Tank / law veteran Gruff, protective, ashamed of his debts. Redemption arc: helping you is his way back.
Ezren Vos Support / alchemy mage with healing word swapped for magic missile Identifies poisons, brews potions (1 potion of healing per long rest). Reads people by scent.
Little Gretch (after Side Adventure 1) Muscle ogre (reduce to 45 HP) Shy, romantic, carries you across rivers. Cannot fit through most doors.
Pipwhistle Dewlace (after befriending her, Part 6) Scout / thief pixie Invisible, nosy, steals small items and gossip. Warns you when fey are near (advantage on saves against the first fey temptation each night). Demands sweets.

Companion Rule — "Have My Back." Once per short rest, the solo hero may call on the companion to turn a failed check into a success, or absorb one hit that would have dropped the hero to 0 HP. The cost: the companion gets a demand (a favor, a confession, a risky errand) that must be addressed before the next long rest.

Scaling Encounters for Solo Play

  • Hit points: Halve the HP of all non-boss enemies; reduce bosses to 2/3 HP.
  • Action economy: A solo hero fighting a boss gains Hero's Surge: once per combat, take an extra action at the start of your turn.
  • Numbers: Replace groups of enemies with one enemy of the same type per hero + companion, plus a hazard.
  • Death's Door: When reduced to 0 HP, a solo hero may instead choose to drop to 1 HP and suffer a Scar (a lasting complication: a lost item, a broken promise, an enemy who's now aware of you). Once per adventure.
  • Rest: Allow one free short rest between each night's scenes (the city provides inns, salons, and bathhouses).
  • Clues: Lower the Keystone requirement to two for a solo hero, or let the companion supply one hint per night.
  • Social encounters: Solo play shines here. Use the Allure track as written; the solo hero is the center of every flirtation.

Running It Fully GM-less

Treat each location as a scene. On arrival, read the description, then ask the oracle about the situation ("Is the suspect here?"), roll NPC reactions, and roll for clues as written. Track the Unravelling clock in a notebook. Let the riddles be real — solve them yourself before checking the answers (they're in Part 4, so read that part only as needed or ask a friend to cover it).

scenes.title: Solo Entry Adventures (Companion Book)
scenes.html:
The companion book Through the Oathless Glass (solo-entry-adventures.pdf / .docx / .md) holds five solo gamebook adventures, one per gateway character, for a single 1st- to 3rd-level adventurer. Each one covers the PC's life on their own side of the mirror, a Mirror-Promise prompt, the pull-through read-aloud, and the gateway character's charm, offer, and secret. Each includes a 7–8-scene numbered mission with a riddle, a 🌹 resist-or-yield scene on the Allure/Enthrallment tracks, a chase or fight, and a moral choice, then ends in 2–3 hand-offs into this guide.

# Adventure Gateway Landing point Hands off into
1 The Glass Remembers Lysander Rosewater Gallery, seconds after the murder The Black Kiss (eyewitness testimony about Thessaly)
2 The Blue Hour Sabine Velour The Blue Hour's back room Underworld thread: the Queen's Shard, Hale's marker, Mother Brine
3 A Rose Before Midnight Prince Caelum Edge of the Lanternwood Side Adventure 2 and the Fae endgame (the wedding-dream Keystone)
4 Hold Your Breath Marisol Tidewhisper A Saltgrave sea cave at rising tide Side Adventure 3 (the Pearl Heart, Varo's report)
5 May I Come In? Sir Valentin Dusk Château Dusk's Harvest Masquerade Side Adventure 4 (Lucan's letter, Morwenna's vote, the Isaveth lead)

Every entry adventure arrives on Night 1, and its ending states exactly which clue, ally, Anchor, or Scar you carry into the campaign. They work just as well as one-on-one prologues for a group: run each player's entry solo, then reunite the party at the Velvet Opera by first dawn.

scenes.title: Scaling for 3–5 Players
scenes.html:
Party size Adjustments
3 players Use encounters as written for the low end of each level range. Allow one companion NPC if the party lacks a healer or face.
4 players The default assumption. Use levels as written.
5 players Add one enemy of the most common type to each fight, or +50% HP to bosses; add a Legendary Resistance (1/day) to Hulga, Ilysse, Kray, and Lucan. Increase the clock pressure: require four Keystones for a convincing accusation.

Spotlight in groups. Give each player a personal tie to one suspect (Seraphine is a PC's old flame; Hale once arrested a PC; Ezren made a PC's signature perfume; Varo owes a PC money; Celestine challenged a PC to a duel years ago; Thessaly is the PC's favorite "aunt" figure in the city). These ties make interrogations personal and the final reveal hurt.

Splitting the party. Vesperine encourages it — one group at the Opera, another at the Drowned Market. Cut between scenes every 15–20 minutes; end each cut on a cliffhanger.

sessions.title: Appendices — Opening Scene, Session Zero, Names & Rumors
sessions.summary: Player-facing extras (also in the player guide window; the rumor truths stay here).

scenes.title: Appendix A — Opening Scene (Read-Aloud)
scenes.html:
The Velvet Opera is a furnace of candlelight and perfume. A thousand masks turn toward the Rosewater balcony as the great clock above it — oddly silent tonight — is ignored in favor of the hand-bells. Midnight. The Oathwarden, Lord Aurelian Sable, sweeps the diva Seraphine Lark into his arms, and the whole house roars as their lips meet.

Then he staggers. His fingers claw at his golden mask. Black — black as spilled ink — spreads from beneath its edges, down his cheeks, across his lips. He falls. Someone screams "Poison!" and a hundred masked faces scatter like startled birds.

In the chaos, a tiny woman in crimson with a jeweled lorgnette taps your shoulder. "You," says Dame Ottoline Graves, "have no oaths in this city. How wonderfully useful. Come with me."

scenes.title: Appendix B — Session Zero Checklist
scenes.html:
• Confirm the content compass: suggestive, never explicit; fade to black; no captives, coercion, or minors in any romantic context.
  • Agree on Lines (never appears) and Veils (happens off-screen). Typical Veils for this campaign: graphic gore, torture.
  • Pick personal ties to suspects (Part 9).
  • Explain the fey etiquette rules to players (Part 6): never say "thank you," never give your full name, and refuse gifts graciously. Agree that enthralled characters cannot consent to romance.
  • If using the mirror prologue: each player writes the promise their character once made to their own reflection (Part 2), and you roll for the gateway character.
  • Decide: group, solo with GM, or GM-less solo.
  • Choose whether the Allure track is in use.

scenes.title: Appendix C — Quick Vesperine Names & Rumors
scenes.html:
Names: Benedetto Fiore (tenor), Allegra Vane (card-salon owner), Pim Gallowglass (gondolier), Sister Corvina (Veiled Sister), Teodor Graves (sleeping heir), Old Mother Brine (fence), Lorcan the Poet, Bel Okafor (first mate), Marta Ilic (innkeeper), Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand.

Rumors (d8): 1. "Aurelian was never really a Sable — I heard his grandmother sold eels." (True-ish.) 2. "The diva poisoned him on the Syndicate's orders." (False.) 3. "The Countess of the Duskvine drinks the blood of virgins." (False — she drinks wine and the blood of enthusiastic volunteers.) 4. "Men are vanishing in the Thicketmoor and coming back fat and happy." (True — the ones who escape.) 5. "Madame Rook has made Aurelian's mask every year for thirty years, and never charged him a coin." (True. Think about it.) 6. "The Ledger is bleeding." (True.) 7. "A dragon is reading our mail." (True.) 8. "Captain Hale lost his own house in a card game." (True, and his horse.)

End of guide. May all your oaths be kept — and all your masks come off at the right moment.

npcs.name: Lysander of the Silvered Glass

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Tall and slender, with skin that carries a faint quicksilver sheen and hair like poured white silver tied back with a black ribbon. His eyes are polished steel that reflect you rather than having a color of their own. He wears a five-hundred-year-old doublet of silver brocade with a high lace collar, and he chimes faintly, like a wineglass, when he moves.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Courtly, wistful, playful, and very lonely. He has watched every masquerade for five centuries and can describe each one, but he has not touched anyone in five hundred years.

blocks.label: Seduction / flirt angle
blocks.html: He mirrors. He adopts your posture, your accent, your favorite turn of phrase, and tells you exactly what you most need to hear with uncanny accuracy ("You always stand like that when you're pretending not to be hurt"). To charm him, surprise him by doing something he couldn't have predicted (Persuasion DC 15, advantage for genuine spontaneity). He finds that irresistible.

blocks.label: Secret agenda
blocks.html: Lysander was Oriane Sable's lover and Mirelle's apprentice. He sealed a promise to Oriane by kissing the Glass ("I will watch over your house forever"), and the Glass took him at his word. He can leave only if someone freely agrees to trade places with him, or if he passes through when the Glass opens home. He fishes for that agreement with carefully ambiguous wording ("Would you let me walk beside you, just once?"). A PC who agrees without understanding hasn't really agreed, and the Glass will refuse the trade, so he must eventually ask honestly. He also watched the murder from inside the mirror at 11:47. He saw Thessaly come through the secret door, and he knows by her eyes that she is Oriane's blood. He is torn between justice and protecting the last of "his" house.

blocks.label: How he appears
blocks.html: Your reflection smiles before you do. Then it steps aside, and he is standing behind you in the glass, bowing. He offers a silvered hand through the surface: "Forgive the intrusion. Your city is about to need you more than you can imagine. Mine already does."

blocks.label: Where he leads
blocks.html: Straight into the main plot. The PCs tumble out of the mirror wall into the Rosewater Gallery seconds after Aurelian falls, making them instant witnesses (and instant suspects).

blocks.label: What he wants from the PCs
blocks.html: Freedom, warmth, a single real touch, and for House Sable to survive. He trades his eyewitness testimony (a Keystone clue) only for a promise to help him out of the Glass. He will offer his testimony freely if a PC earns Smitten (3 boxes) on his Allure track.

npcs.name: Sabine Velour

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A strikingly glamorous woman in her mid-fifties with warm brown skin, finger-waved black hair streaked with silver, and a long midnight-blue gown of beaded sequins with opera gloves to the elbow. She carries a jeweled cigarette holder she never lights and wears a single playing card, the Queen of Hearts, tucked into her beaded clutch. Her voice is smoke and honey.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Worldly, warm, funny, and deeply homesick. She calls everyone "sugar" or "kid." Underneath the sparkle she carries thirty years of guilt.

blocks.label: Seduction / flirt angle
blocks.html: Old-world glamour. She sings to you, dances you around her salon, and asks greedily about your world, its songs, its slang, how the coffee tastes. Charm her with stories of home (Persuasion DC 13; automatic success if a PC sings or recites something from the "real" world at the table). She flirts most dangerously at the card table, where she cheats beautifully.

blocks.label: Secret agenda
blocks.html: Sabine was the last oathless judge. Thirty years ago she was summoned, swept off her feet by a charming young Aurelian Sable, and endorsed him as Oathwarden with a kiss. That kiss became her Anchor, and with Aurelian dead it is finally released. She has long suspected he stole something terrible to get his name. She now runs The Blue Hour, a card salon in the Velvet Quarter bankrolled by Old Mother Brine, and she owes the Thorn Syndicate a fortune. She owns a shard of the Glass (a hand-mirror), which is how she reached the PCs. The Syndicate wants that shard, because whoever holds a shard when the Glass opens can choose who goes through. Her deal with Brine: deliver the new oathless judges and steer them toward the Syndicate's candidate in exchange for her debts and a ticket home. She is ashamed of this and may break it.

blocks.label: How she appears
blocks.html: In a bar mirror, a dark window, or a phone screen. First comes a faint trumpet and a woman singing a song from your world that she shouldn't know. Then her gloved hand slides out of the glass holding the Queen of Hearts: "Pick a card, sugar. Any card. They all go to the same place."

blocks.label: Where she leads
blocks.html: The Velvet Quarter and the underworld thread. The PCs land in The Blue Hour's back room, a short walk from the Drowned Market, Varo Kestrel, and Captain Hale's gambling debts.

blocks.label: What she wants from the PCs
blocks.html: News of home, a way back, and absolution. She wants them to finish what she got wrong. If they earn her trust (Allure 3+) she confesses the Syndicate deal and gives them the shard, a powerful tool for the endgame and the way home.

npcs.name: Prince Caelum of the Dusk

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Unearthly tall, with skin the soft violet of twilight, golden eyes, and graceful antlers twined with climbing red roses. He wears a long high-collared coat of rose-petal-red velvet stitched with thorns, a crown of briar, and an expression of permanent private amusement. He smells of summer nights.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Languid, charming, mischievous, and very old. He is bored by almost everything and fascinated by mortals because they end.

blocks.label: Seduction / flirt angle
blocks.html: He makes bargains sound like love poems ("Give me only a dance at the seventh bell, and I will give you anything that fits in your two hands"). Every gift he offers has a string, and he is delighted when you notice it. Charm him by refusing a gift wittily, or by out-bargaining him (opposed Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) vs. his +8). Accept his gifts uncritically and he loses respect for you.

blocks.label: Secret agenda
blocks.html: Caelum is the Fae Duke's youngest son, sent to make sure the Accord fails on Night 7 so his father can claim Vesperine. Secretly, he wants the city for himself, and he has fallen half in love with its music, its masquerades, and its mortals. His plan is to let the Accord fail and then claim Vesperine from his father as his domain, a beautiful fey-touched city of eternal revels ruled by a (mostly) kind prince. A second, deeper secret: if a PC becomes Oathwarden and freely chooses to marry him, the Accord would make him a citizen, free of his father forever. He will court a PC toward that end, honestly, if they ever ask him the right question (Insight DC 18 to sense there is something he isn't saying).

blocks.label: How he appears
blocks.html: Rose petals drift out of the mirror before he does, then the glass fogs as if breathed on from the other side. A long hand, thorned rings on every finger, offers a single rose through the surface: "Come and see something beautiful before it ends."

blocks.label: Where he leads
blocks.html: The PCs land at the edge of the Lanternwood, beneath glowing trees, close to the Moth Court (Side Adventure 2). Queen Ilysse is his former paramour and still furious with him, which makes for a very awkward introduction. He also opens the Fae endgame thread (see Part 6 for his rivalry with Lady Nocturne Vesh).

blocks.label: What he wants from the PCs
blocks.html: A promise sealed with a kiss: "one dance at the seventh bell." It sounds innocent, but it binds the PC to be wherever he is at midnight on Night 7 (an Anchor that could pull them into the Feywild if Ending D happens). What he truly wants is a way to stay in the mortal world.

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Cael Rosier
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: A dashing, red-coated rose merchant who supplies every ballroom in the Gilded Crescent and loses fortunes at Sabine's card tables with a grin. Everyone knows Cael; no one knows where he lives. His roses are famous for never wilting.
  • Tells:
  • He never says "thank you," and he deftly sidesteps it when others say it to him ("Don't thank me, darling, it's bad luck").
  • Roses near him bloom; cut flowers in a room open as he enters.
  • Perception DC 15 in candlelight: the shadow of his head has antlers.
  • He flinches from iron coins and pays only in silver and gold.
  • Insight DC 17: he speaks in carefully true sentences and never tells a plain lie.
  • Mirror reflection: Twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, rose-twined antlers, and a briar crown. In the glass he looks at the viewer directly and puts a finger to his lips.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. He seals a kiss-bound bargain. Roses burst from the air as the vow takes. 2. Nocturne threatens a PC he has grown fond of, and he reveals himself to stand in her way. 3. A PC reaches Allure 3 with him and asks the right question (Insight DC 18, Part 6). He chooses to show them. 4. Sunset in the Lanternwood, where his glamour simply will not hold. 5. A cold-iron blade at his throat.

Read-aloud: The Rose Merchant's True Face. Cael sighs, the way a man sighs when a card game has gone on too long, and sets down his glass. "I did so enjoy being ordinary," he says. Every rose in the room opens at once. The red coat lengthens into rose-petal velvet stitched with thorns; his skin deepens to the violet of the last minute before night; and from his dark curls rise antlers twined with climbing roses, brushing the chandelier, which chimes. His eyes are molten gold. "Prince Caelum of the Dusk," he says, bowing, "and still, I promise, your friend. I simply wasn't allowed to say so until now."

npcs.public: Unearthly tall, with skin the soft violet of twilight, golden eyes, and graceful antlers twined with climbing red roses. He wears a long high-collared coat of rose-petal-red velvet stitched with thorns, a crown of briar, and an expression of permanent private amusement. He smells of summer nights. Languid, charming, mischievous, and very old.

npcs.name: Marisol Tidewhisper

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A merfolk siren who can take a two-legged shape on land. Sea-green scales shimmer along her cheekbones, collarbones, and forearms. Her long black hair is braided with sea-glass and tiny bells, and her eyes are the color of moonlit surf. She wears a fitted bodice of pearl and abalone shell, a sweeping wrap-skirt of sea-silk, and a gauzy sea-silk shawl. She is always slightly damp and grinning.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Wild, reckless, gleefully rule-breaking, with a laugh like a breaking wave. She is impatient with old traditions and with her elders.

blocks.label: Seduction / flirt angle
blocks.html: Dares. She splashes, teases, challenges you to cliff-dive, holds your gaze a beat too long, and asks openly: "Kiss me for luck before the storm?" She is transparent that a kiss here is a promise, though she phrases it so it sounds like nothing. Charm her by matching her recklessness (Athletics or Acrobatics stunt + Persuasion DC 14). Turning her down with a better dare earns her respect.

blocks.label: Secret agenda
blocks.html: Marisol is the one who gave the Pearl Heart to Captain Kray. She wanted to break Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa's centuries-old rule over the Choir, and Kray promised to help. He betrayed her and enslaved her sisters. She stole a shard of the Glass from a shipwreck to recruit outsiders no one in Carnelia could buy. Now she wants the PCs to recover the Pearl Heart and hand it to her rather than Nerissa, which would make her the new Mother of the Choir.

blocks.label: How she appears
blocks.html: Through water: a bath, a puddle, a glass of wine, the sink. First a song you feel in your teeth, then a laughing face beneath the surface. Then a cool, wet, webbed hand closes around your wrist: "Hold your breath, darling."

blocks.label: Where she leads
blocks.html: The PCs come up gasping in a moonlit sea cave on the Saltgrave Coast (Side Adventure 3), directly beneath the Smugglers' Grotto, with the tide rising.

blocks.label: What she wants from the PCs
blocks.html: The Pearl Heart, a crew of champions, and, if a PC is interested, a sweetheart who will race her to the bottom of the sea. Exposing her betrayal to Nerissa (Insight DC 16 or the testimony of Kray's first mate Bel Okafor) forces a dramatic choice between justice for the Choir and loyalty to the one who brought them.

npcs.name: Sir Valentin Dusk

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Pale as candle wax, with tousled raven hair, a small beauty mark beneath one heavy-lidded dark eye, and a rakish half-smile. He dresses in a black velvet coat with garnet buttons, a ruffled cravat, and gloves of oxblood leather. He is a vampire, so in mirrors he is invisible except for his clothes.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Decadent, sardonic, romantic, and very tired of eternity. He is witty to the point of self-mockery and kinder than he pretends.

blocks.label: Seduction / flirt angle
blocks.html: He notices your pulse ("It quickened. I'm flattered."), describes warmth like poetry, and asks permission for everything, from a dance to a seat beside you to a lock of your hair, and he turns asking into the most seductive thing in the room. Charm him with candor (Persuasion DC 14) or by offering him something he hasn't felt in centuries: a sunrise described, a shared laugh, a hand held without fear. He never feeds on anyone who has not enthusiastically agreed, and he finds the question tedious only when people assume otherwise.

blocks.label: Secret agenda
blocks.html: Valentin was Countess Morwenna Dusk's consort for a hundred years, until her steward Lucan Vey framed him for a murder Lucan committed. Morwenna exiled him. He wants Lucan destroyed and Morwenna's forgiveness. He has a deeper, more selfish hope too: an old fey legend says a vampire who passes through the Oathless Glass into a world without the Accord might walk in sunlight again. He means to go through when it opens, with or without the PCs' blessing.

blocks.label: How he appears
blocks.html: The mirror shows the room behind you, perfectly ordinary, except that the empty armchair in the reflection is no longer empty. An elegant coat and cravat sit there with no one in them, and a wineglass lifts itself in a toast. A voice says: "Please don't scream. I've had a very long century. May I come in? You do have to say yes."

blocks.label: Where he leads
blocks.html: The PCs step out of a tall gilded mirror into a dim side gallery of Château Dusk in the Duskvine Valley, in the middle of the Harvest Masquerade (Side Adventure 4).

blocks.label: What he wants from the PCs
blocks.html: Proof of Lucan's crimes, an introduction to Morwenna that won't end with her setting him on fire, and a place beside them when the Glass opens home.

npcs.name: Seraphine Lark

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Human, early 30s, a cascade of copper hair, emerald silk gown, a voice that could melt candle wax. Black-stained lips she refuses to wash ("Let them look").

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Dramatic, quick-witted, exhausted by her own legend. Funny when she forgets to perform.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: Flirts with everyone as a performance — it's armor. Charm her by ignoring the act and talking to the real woman (DC 15; DC 10 if a PC compliments something other than her beauty). She will also try to seduce information out of the PCs about the investigation, on behalf of her Syndicate handlers.

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: She's been spying on Aurelian for the Thorn Syndicate — passing on his pillow-talk for two years. And she is in love with Lady Celestine Morrow, his fiancée.

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: On stage until 11:50, then went up to the Rosewater balcony and waited with the crowd until the midnight kiss. True — forty witnesses.

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: She literally kissed him and he died. Her lips are black.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: Aurelian had been frightened for weeks. Someone sent him a porcelain mask with no face and he kept murmuring, "The masks remember." And at about quarter to midnight, while waiting on the balcony, she glimpsed in the mirror wall "Madame Rook's silver braid, fussing with his ribbon — then gone."

npcs.name: Lady Celestine Morrow

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Half-elf, 28, platinum hair in a severe crown braid, ice-blue gown with a high collar, a single sapphire at her throat. Moves like a duelist.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Cold, cutting, brilliant. Treats conversation as fencing and keeps score.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: A challenge. She despises flattery and is fascinated by audacity. Charm her with wit, a bold dare, or by beating her at something (DC 17; advantage on the check if a PC wins a game of cards, a duel of words, or an actual duel). If charmed, she becomes a sharp, sardonic ally.

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: She is in love with Seraphine and was desperate to escape her engagement oath. A month ago she bought oath-breaking salts from Ezren Vos. They didn't work (they were fakes).

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: "Alone on the balcony, enjoying the view." False. She was in the Morrow family box, writing a love letter to Seraphine, which she then burned.

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: Strong motive (a hated marriage), a vial of suspicious white crystals in her vanity, and a lie in her alibi.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: The salts and the letter (she'll show the ashes in her grate — a mending spell restores a scorched fragment: "…we'll be free by the end of the festival, my lark…" — damning-looking but innocent). She also saw Captain Hale take a fat purse from a masked man in a thorn-green domino at 11:30.

npcs.name: Captain Dorian Hale

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Human, mid-40s, broad shoulders, a scar along his jaw, Lantern Watch coat with the top buttons perpetually undone. Smells of pipe smoke and rain.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Tired, gruff, decent at heart, ashamed of what he's become. Dry humor.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: Classic smolder; he respects courage and plain speaking and is disarmed by genuine kindness (DC 14). If charmed, he offers a "nightcap" at the Tilted House — where, drink in hand, he tells the truth.

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: He owes the Thorn Syndicate 2,000 ducats in gambling debts. He took a bribe from Varo Kestrel to pull his guards away from the Dressing Gallery corridor between 11:30 and midnight.

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: "Walking the perimeter." Partly true — he stayed far from the corridor on purpose.

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: He's obstructing the investigation, has a Syndicate purse in his strongbox, and quietly ordered the body moved before the PCs arrived.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: The bribe, and Varo's name. Crucially: "The dressing corridor was empty for half an hour. Anyone could have come and gone through those rooms — and the mirror wall's got a door. Everyone backstage knows it."

npcs.name: Ezren Vos

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Tiefling, 30s, lavender skin, gold rings on curling horns, a loose silk robe over an embroidered vest. Speaks softly and leans in close to smell you.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Sensual, curious, theatrical, a little amoral, genuinely brilliant.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: He describes people by their scent — "You smell like a secret and saddle leather" — and is charmed by those who play along or let him create a signature perfume for them (DC 13). Appeal to his vanity about his craft and he'll show off.

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: He sells illegal "oath-breaking salts" — mostly fakes made of sea salt and crushed pearl. Selling them is a crime that would close his shop.

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: At the party all night, running the perfume fountain on the ground floor. True.

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: He made the bloodrose perfume on Seraphine's lips. He knows poisons. He's nervous.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: Examining the body or the stain (or a sample), he identifies Widow's Sigh: "The poison wasn't on her lips. Widow's Sigh is inert until it breathes bloodrose. It was on his face — inside the mask." And his order ledger (coded, see Riddle 3) shows that "Madame R." bought a vial of bloodrose a month ago — odd, since Thessaly famously wears only lavender.

npcs.name: Varo Kestrel

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Half-elf, late 20s, dark curls, crooked grin, a rose-thorn earring, a thorn-green domino mask. Dresses better than he can afford.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Shameless, charming, cheerful even when caught. Loyal to his friends, nobody else.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: He flirts with everyone, constantly and outrageously, including the PCs, the Watch, and a statue. Charm him by flirting back better — he respects a worthy rival (DC 12). He can become a recurring rogue companion (see Solo Rules).

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: Six months ago he stole a page from Aurelian's desk for a Syndicate blackmail scheme. Tonight he bribed Hale so he could lift Aurelian's Ledger-vault key from his coat in the cloakroom. He succeeded — he has the key on him right now.

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: "Dancing." With whom? "Everyone."

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: He was caught on a balcony with the victim's key ring; he's Syndicate; he bribed the Watch.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: The theft of the page: "Some old wedding vow — 'Aurel Fenn' and 'Isaveth Sable.' Thought it was leverage. Mother Brine sold it before I could use it. Some lady in a grey veil. Paid in masks — beautiful masks." He can lead the PCs to Mother Brine in the Drowned Market, and he'll trade the vault key for immunity.

npcs.name: Madame Thessaly Rook

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Human, about 60, a long silver braid pinned with gold, laugh lines, magnificent dark eyes, fingertips flecked with gold leaf. Always a lavender shawl. Never wears a mask herself.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Warm, wicked, hilarious, everybody's favorite aunt who has stories. Underneath: steel, grief, and thirty years of patience.

blocks.label: Flirt / seduction angle
blocks.html: Outrageously, theatrically flirtatious ("If I were thirty years younger, darling, you'd need a bodyguard"). She charms the PCs rather than the reverse — and she gives each PC a free, beautiful mask "for the investigation — you'll need to blend in." One of these masks (or all, in a small group) is a listening mask: Thessaly can hear whatever its wearer hears by holding its twin to her ear. A detect magic reveals faint divination magic; Ezren Vos or a DC 16 Arcana check identifies it.

blocks.label: Secret
blocks.html: She is Lady Isaveth Sable, and she murdered her husband.

blocks.label: Alibi
blocks.html: "In the Dressing Gallery all evening, fitting masks." Technically true — the Dressing Gallery connects to the murder scene through the mirror door. Several actors confirm she was there, "though she stepped out once, around quarter to."

blocks.label: Looks guilty because
blocks.html: Very little at first. That's the point.

blocks.label: Under pressure reveals
blocks.html: First, she deflects toward Celestine ("That poor girl was desperate, darling — ask her about the salts"). Confronted with two or more hard clues, she grows quiet and still. Confronted with the vow-page or the empty crypt, she removes her shawl, straightens, and speaks in the cultured accent of the Gilded Crescent: "My name is Isaveth Sable. He took it from me with a kiss. I took it back the same way." Then she makes the PCs an offer (see Endings).

npcs.name: Lord Aurelian Sable

blocks.label: The victim
blocks.html:
Age 58. Silver at the temples, a dimpled smile that has ended three marriages (none of them his), always in midnight-blue velvet. Aurelian was beloved in public — generous, witty, the best dancer at any ball — and feared in private, because the man who keeps the Ledger knows every promise everyone has ever broken. He was engaged to Lady Celestine Morrow, kept the diva Seraphine Lark as his "muse," and had held the office of Oathwarden for thirty years.

How he was found. At the stroke of midnight on the Night of Unmasking, by tradition, the Oathwarden kisses the reigning star of the Opera on the Rosewater balcony as the whole house unmasks. Aurelian kissed Seraphine Lark, staggered, clawed at his mask, and fell dead by the chaise. His lips and the skin beneath his mask were stained black as Ledger ink. The crowd screamed one word: poison kiss.

npcs.name: Dame Ottoline Graves

blocks.label: The Investigator's Warrant
blocks.html: The Opera Council's spokesperson, Dame Ottoline Graves (an elderly, terrifyingly polite patron with a lorgnette), hires the PCs because they are outsiders with no oaths sworn in the city — "the only people in Vesperine with nothing to hide." (If the PCs came through the Oathless Glass, this is literal: the Council's charter requires an oathless judge to confirm the next Oathwarden. See Part 2.) The Red Ribbon Warrant grants entry to any house and the right to question anyone once. Reward: 500 ducats each, plus a favor of the Council (a kiss-oath — naturally).

blocks.label: In The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court
blocks.html: Wings of dusky violet and gold, eyes like wet ink, a gown that seems spun of moonlight. Speaks in a near-whisper so you must lean close. Seductive in the manner of something ancient and amused. Collects compliments, dances, and truths.

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Madame Ilse Hush
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: A veiled, soft-voiced dream-reader who opened the Hush House in the Velvet Quarter this season. She reads dreams for a silver kiss and sells little blue bottles of sleep-tonic that give the sweetest dreams in Carnelia. Her clients sleep wonderfully, and some of them don't wake up for days.
  • Tells:
  • A powder like crushed moonlight on her fingertips and on the rim of every tonic bottle.
  • Candle flames lean toward her, and moths gather at her windows.
  • She speaks only in whispers, so clients must lean close.
  • She has iron candleholders replaced with glass.
  • Insight DC 16: she seems hungry when a client describes a beautiful dream.
  • Mirror reflection: Great wings of dusky violet and gold patterned like eyes, ink-dark eyes, and a gown spun from moonlight.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Someone falls asleep in her presence. She cannot resist feeding, and the wings unfold. 2. A sudden gust of wind or a lantern thrust at her face. Moth instinct takes over. 3. Pipwhistle's dream-sugar trade is exposed in front of her. 4. A PC wins the Moth Waltz, or calls her by her true name and title.

Read-aloud: The Dream-Reader's Wings. Madame Hush leans across the little table, her veil stirring with each whispered word. "Tell me," she breathes, "what did you dream of last night?" Behind you, someone in the waiting room has nodded off, and the dream-reader's head turns toward them like a flower toward the sun. Her veil falls away. Behind her, two great shapes unfold and fill the room, wings of dusky violet and gold, each patterned with a staring eye. Every candle bends toward her. Silver dust drifts down like snow. "Forgive me," whispers Queen Ilysse of the Hush, and her eyes are pools of ink. "It has been such a long time since I had something sweet."

npcs.name: Pipwhistle Dewlace

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A pixie the size of a hand, with dandelion-fluff hair, freckles of pollen, iridescent dragonfly wings, and a dress of overlapping rose petals with a thimble for a hat. She glows faintly pink when pleased and faintly green when plotting.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Giddy, nosy, sentimental, and a compulsive collector of shiny buttons, gossip, and tiny promises.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: She kisses noses "for luck." She hides in a PC's collar and whispers compliments. Each nose-kiss comes with a tiny, cheerful demand ("Now you owe me a song, sweet thing!"). Charm her with sweets, buttons, or a lullaby (Persuasion DC 11, or automatic with an offering).

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: She trades the tiny promises she collects to the Moth Court for dream-sugar, which is how the Court tracks who in Vesperine dreams the sweetest (and whom to harvest next). She has no idea it's hurting anyone, and she is horrified if shown.

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: Use the pixie stat block (or sprite, swapping the bow for Pixie Dust: one creature, DC 12 Wisdom save or confused for 1 round). Pocket Bargain: a creature who accepts her nose-kiss gains a trivial obligation. Ignoring it for a day gives a comic curse (hiccups, a perpetual sneeze, shoelaces knotting themselves) until paid. These do not add Enthrallment. As an ally (Allure 3+), she can scout invisibly and steal small items. She makes a perfect solo-play companion (see Part 9).

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Pip Dewley
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: The bubbly, curly-haired, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble, a cozy tavern on Needle Row. She's everyone's favorite: quick with a tray, quicker with gossip, and always asking for "a little something for luck." Buttons go missing whenever she's near.
  • Tells:
  • Buttons vanish from coats wherever she's been, and her apron pockets jingle.
  • She serves everything in pewter and never touches the iron tankards on the top shelf.
  • Startle her and, for a blink, she seems much smaller (Perception DC 12).
  • Faint pink sparkles cling to anyone she kisses on the nose "for luck."
  • Insight DC 12: she trades favors for favors and remembers every promise down to the word.
  • Mirror reflection: A hand-sized pixie with dragonfly wings, standing on the bar where Pip's tray should be, waving cheerfully.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. She sneezes, especially at pepper or dust. Pop. 2. Someone pays her in buttons. She can't help it: she shrinks with glee. 3. A PC refuses one of her tiny promises, or breaks one she's owed. 4. Someone offers her a whole cake. 5. Cold iron in her hand. She drops to pixie size with a squeak and hides in a teacup.

Read-aloud: The Barmaid Goes Pop. Pip leans across the bar, beaming, a tray of steaming teacups balanced on one hand. "Now, sweet thing, a little kiss on the nose for luck, and you'll owe me just one teensy song—" Someone drops a pouch of shiny brass buttons on the counter. Pip's eyes go enormous. There is a sound like a cork leaving a bottle, a puff of pink glitter, and the teacups crash down onto an empty floor. Something the size of your hand zips up out of the wreckage on dragonfly wings, clutching a button like a shield, glowing bright, delighted pink. "Ohhh, those are lovely," squeaks Pipwhistle Dewlace. "Oops. Um. Surprise?"

npcs.name: Ondine Mirewillow

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A river nymph with green-gold skin, long hair the color of wet willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, and dark eyes that ripple. She wears a flowing gown of layered green silk that seems to drip without ever soaking anything, plus a necklace of river-pearls. Frogs sing when she laughs.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Teasing, sunny, petty, and timeless. She forgets that mortals age.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: She invites travelers to "rest a moment" by her pool on the Bog Causeway, braids flowers into their hair, and asks for something small: a boot, a ribbon, a lock of hair. Each yes deepens the lure. Charm her by out-teasing her or by bringing gossip about her enemy, Auntie Sallowmere the bog hag (Persuasion DC 13).

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: Ondine's lure is lost time. Travelers who "rest a moment" wake hours, sometimes a year, later, and she keeps their shoes as trophies. She has nothing against anyone; she is simply bored. She is also feuding with Sallowmere and would love the PCs to humiliate the hag (Part 5, Side Adventure 1).

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: Use the dryad stat block, replacing Tree Stride with Water Stride (between any two bodies of water within 60 ft). Fey Charm works as the dryad's (DC 14, adds 1 Enthrallment on a failure). Dreaming Waters: a creature that sits by her pool must make a DC 13 Wisdom save or fall asleep. On waking, roll 1d6: 1–3 one hour has passed, 4–5 one night (advance the Unravelling clock!), 6 she lets you choose, but only if you've made her laugh. Cold water to the face wakes a sleeper (an ironic counter, since she hates it).

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Dina Mire
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: The giggling, sun-freckled bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside, the city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse. She scrubs backs, braids hair, and gossips about everyone. Patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.
  • Tells:
  • Her hems are always damp, though she never seems to get wet.
  • Frogs sing in the drains when she laughs.
  • The baths' lost-and-found holds a suspicious mountain of single shoes.
  • She has worked at the Lilywater "for years," but the oldest regulars swear she hasn't aged in forty.
  • Insight DC 14: she asks every customer for "just a little something," such as a ribbon or a lock of hair.
  • Mirror reflection: She ripples any water near her, so the PCs have disadvantage on the Perception check in water. In a mirror she has green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair, and eyes that ripple like a pond.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Cold water splashed in her face. She shrieks and the glamour slips away with the water. 2. Someone mentions Auntie Sallowmere: a flash of fury, and frogs everywhere. 3. She is caught red-handed with a sleeping customer's shoes. 4. She uses Water Stride to escape, vanishing into one pool and laughing out of another.

Read-aloud: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles. Dina is mid-giggle, a braid of somebody's hair half-finished in her fingers, when the bucket of cold water hits her. She shrieks, and the shriek turns into a laugh like a brook in spring. The freckles slide off her like wet paint. Her skin is green-gold now, her hair a cascade of willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, her eyes dark and rippling. Every frog in the drains begins to sing. "Well, that was rude," says Ondine Mirewillow, wringing out a lily. "And I was being so good. Mostly. Does anyone want their shoes back?"

npcs.name: Rillo Fennamint

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A handsome satyr with curling ram's horns gilded at the tips, chestnut curls, a goatee, and twinkling amber eyes. He wears an open-throated poet's shirt under a waistcoat of patchwork velvet and carries panpipes on a ribbon. He has goat legs, of course, and he dances on them as if they were a happy accident.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Joyful, shameless, generous, a born party, and secretly sentimental.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: He plays a tune that is yours, a melody the listener has never heard but feels they've always known, then asks them to dance. He flirts with absolutely everyone, including Captain Hale (who is not amused) and Madame Rook (who is). Charm him by dancing with abandon or outplaying him in a music duel (Performance DC 14).

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: Rillo is a talent scout for the Moth Court. He leads the best dreamers from Vesperine's revels out into the Lanternwood "for an after-party," and they wake in Ilysse's cocoons. He tells himself it's harmless fun. He has a soft spot for the PCs and can be turned, becoming a guide into the Cocoon Palace (with advantage on the Dimming stealth path in Side Adventure 2).

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: Use the satyr stat block with 45 HP and Revel Pipes as an action: a charming melody (DC 14 Wisdom save or charmed for 1 minute, +1 Enthrallment), a frightening strain, or a gentle lullaby (DC 14 or fall asleep). Creatures who have danced with him willingly have disadvantage on the save. Cotton or wax in the ears grants advantage, as does a loud and terrible counter-song.

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Master Orrin Mintleaf
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: The beloved, bearded dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at every Velvet Opera after-party and teaches the nobility to waltz. He always wears a wide-brimmed hat and tall, oddly heavy boots. His parties end with the best dancers "going on somewhere better."
  • Tells:
  • Perception DC 13: his boots clip-clop on stone like hooves.
  • He never takes off his hat, even indoors and even when bowing.
  • He refuses to dance on iron-studded floors and won't touch the Opera's iron railings.
  • His tunes are always somehow your song.
  • Insight DC 14: he scans the crowd for "dreamers" with the eye of a talent scout.
  • Mirror reflection: Gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls, and goat legs, dancing even when he's standing still.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. He loses himself in the dance past midnight: he kicks off the boots and flings away the hat. 2. A PC out-plays him in a music duel. His pride bursts the glamour. 3. Dawn breaks while he's still playing in the Lanternwood. 4. Someone stamps on his "foot" hard: an iron-heeled boot on the hoof.

Read-aloud: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots. The music is too good to stop. Master Mintleaf whoops, kicks one boot clean across the ballroom, then the other, and his hat goes sailing after them. Where his feet should be, polished hooves strike sparks from the marble. Gilded ram's horns curl from his chestnut hair; his trousers are suddenly fur from the hips down. The dancers scream, then laugh, then don't stop dancing. "No point hiding it now!" bellows Rillo Fennamint, pipes at his lips. "Who's coming to the after-party? The forest's only a short walk, and the moon's out!"

npcs.name: Lady Nocturne Vesh

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Impossibly beautiful in a way that is slightly wrong: no two witnesses describe her the same way. Her true form, revealed under true seeing, a broken glamour, or the Oathless Glass, has bone-white skin, black lips, eyes like starless night, and black hair woven with dead roses. She wears a high-collared gown of black velvet and spider-silk lace, long gloves, and a choker set with a single dark sapphire that holds a stolen name.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Patient, elegant, cruel in the gentlest possible voice. She enjoys being adored but cares only about control.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: She flatters you as the person you most want to be: "You were always meant for more than this, weren't you?" She offers belonging, recognition, and devotion. Every gift, compliment, and dance tightens the leash. She never threatens until the threat is unnecessary.

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: Nocturne is harvesting the true names of Vesperine's nobles (and anyone useful) through enchanted kisses and kiss-bound vows. When the Accord fails on Night 7, every name she holds becomes the Duke's possession, and hers to command. She means to enthrall at least one PC, especially an oathless traveler (Part 2), whose vows count double, and make them her puppet Oathwarden or her weapon against Caelum.

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: CR 11 (custom). AC 16, HP 150, speed 30 ft. Saves Wis +8, Cha +10. Resistant to nonmagical damage except cold iron, which she treats as a vulnerability. Spells (DC 18): charm person and suggestion at will; dominate person 1/day; mislead and major image 1/day each. Glamour Veil: she appears as each viewer's ideal; Insight DC 18 notices something "off." Kiss-Bound Vow: she can seal a vow only with a creature that speaks agreement. If the creature was Enthralled at the time, the vow is a forgery (see Freeing Victims). Name-Kiss (recharge 6): against a creature at Enthrallment 4, she can take their true name (Enthrallment 5). Legendary actions (3): Whisper (suggestion), Fade (teleport 30 ft), Rose-Thorn Lash (2d10 piercing, reach 15 ft).

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Madame Noor Vesperelle
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: A rich, mysterious widow "from across the sea" who arrived last spring and instantly became the city's most sought-after hostess. Her salon, the Black Fan, meets in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe ("a mourning custom of my homeland, darling"). Invitations are black envelopes sealed with a lip-print. She is the salon's center of gravity, the woman everyone wants to be seen with.
  • Tells:
  • She is never near an uncovered mirror. Her palazzo's draped mirrors are a tell in themselves (Insight DC 14 to find the "custom" suspicious).
  • She always wears long gloves, and she uses silver cutlery, never iron. An iron fork offered to her goes politely unused.
  • Guests can never quite describe her face afterward. An Intelligence DC 13 check to recall it fails for anyone at Enthrallment 1+.
  • Dead rose petals collect where she has sat.
  • Insight DC 18: her smile arrives a half-second before her eyes do.
  • Mirror reflection: Bone-white skin, black lips, starless eyes, a crown of dead roses, and the dark sapphire at her throat pulsing with a stolen name.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. A crepe-draped mirror is uncovered in her presence, or the Oathless Glass or a shard is turned on her. 2. Cold iron touches her skin. 3. She is laughed at publicly and sincerely (a successful Performance (Comedy) check against DC 18). 4. A PC reaches Enthrallment 4 with her. She reveals herself deliberately, to savor it. 5. The stroke of midnight at her Night 6 masquerade, when she unmasks for the whole Thornwake.

Read-aloud: The Black Fan Falls. Madame Vesperelle laughs, that low, warm laugh that has made half of Vesperine fall in love with her, and snaps her black lace fan shut. "Darling," she says, "you've been looking at the wrong face all evening." Behind her, the crepe slithers from the great mirror like a shed skin. In the glass stands someone else: skin white as a bone in moonlight, lips black as Ledger ink, eyes with no stars in them at all. The candles gutter. When you turn back from the mirror, the widow is gone and only the other one remains, smiling exactly the same smile. "There," says Lady Nocturne Vesh. "Isn't that better? Now we can stop pretending you weren't already mine."

npcs.role: Fair Folk · Mistress of Glamours (Thorn · Ruler of the Thornwake)
npcs.trueText: Impossibly beautiful in a way that is slightly wrong: no two witnesses describe her the same way. Her true form, revealed under true seeing, a broken glamour, or the Oathless Glass, has bone-white skin, black lips, eyes like starless night, and black hair woven with dead roses. She wears a high-collared gown of black velvet and spider-silk lace, long gloves, and a choker set with a single dark sapphire. Patient, elegant, cruel in the gentlest possible voice. She enjoys being adored but cares only about control.

npcs.name: Sir Merrow Ashgrave, the Sorrowkiss

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: A tall, sorrowful, beautiful knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths. He keeps his helm under his arm to show a pale face, grey eyes that always seem about to cry, and silver hair. A cloak of grey petals sheds and regrows as he walks, and his lips are dusted faintly with silver glimmer.

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Melancholy, courteous, and honest about being a monster. He believes he offers mercy: relief from pain.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: He offers comfort. He finds the grieving, the exhausted, the heartbroken and says, "Let me take it away, just for tonight." His blown kiss carries glimmer, a fey dust (refined from Moth Court dream-powder) that brings a rush of bliss and the absence of sorrow.

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: He is hooking Vesperine on glimmer, sold through the Thorn Syndicate in the Drowned Market. Glimmer-addicts can't resist Nocturne's commands, and the Syndicate gets rich while the city grows docile before Night 7. Queen Ilysse supplies the dream-powder under protest, and proof of this can turn the Moth Court against the Thornwake.

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: CR 7. Use the knight stat block with 120 HP, AC 18, and two longsword attacks (thorn-blade: +1d8 necrotic). Blown Kiss of Glimmer (recharge 5–6): a 15-ft cone of silver dust. DC 15 Wisdom save or gain 1 Enthrallment and become poisoned (blissed-out) for 1 minute; a creature already at Enthrallment 1+ also gains Glimmer Craving (below). Holding your breath (declared before the save) or a damp cloth over the face gives advantage. Sorrow's Mercy: he will not strike a creature that is weeping or grieving openly. (It's his last scrap of knighthood, and a player who figures this out can exploit it.)

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Brother Ash
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: A tall, grey-robed mourning friar of no order anyone can name. He sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes and Cypress Isle funerals, holds hands, and listens. The mourners he comforts stop crying, and many of them, oddly, come back to the Drowned Market for "something to help them sleep."
  • Tells:
  • A faint silver dust on his lips and on the hands of those he's comforted.
  • Grey petals drift from the hem of his robe.
  • He never eats or drinks at a wake.
  • He won't help carry a coffin and avoids the iron nails.
  • Insight DC 16: his grief is centuries older than he looks.
  • Mirror reflection: A knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths, helm under his arm, tears on his pale face.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Someone refuses his comfort and names him: "You're selling it, aren't you?" 2. His glimmer trade is threatened (the vats, the Syndicate couriers, or a dealer is attacked). 3. Someone grieves openly and honestly in front of him. Sorrow's Mercy compels him to stop pretending. 4. Cold iron, or a coffin nail pressed into his palm.

Read-aloud: The Friar's Armor. Brother Ash bows his head over the mourner's hands. "Let me take it away," he murmurs, "just for tonight." Then he looks up at you, and his face is full of an old and terrible tenderness. "No. You won't let me, will you?" The grey robe darkens and hardens; it is armor now, black plate grown over with thorns and inlaid with silver moths, and the petals of his cloak rise around him like ash in the wind. His lips glitter silver. "I am Sir Merrow Ashgrave," says the Sorrowkiss, setting down his helm. "And I am so very sorry for what I am about to do."

npcs.name: Amaranth

blocks.label: Appearance
blocks.html: Androgynous and serene, with elegant antlers threaded with roses and a long, high-collared, dusk-colored coat embroidered with thorns. They carry an enormous book bound in red leather, the Book of Forfeit Names, and they always smile, even when sad. (This is the "Fae Duke's Herald" of the Unravelling clock and art prompt #20.)

blocks.label: Personality
blocks.html: Polite, punctilious, and almost apologetic. A bureaucrat of doom with impeccable manners.

blocks.label: Flirt angle
blocks.html: Courtly gallantry. They kiss hands, offer to "simplify" your debts, and invite you to "add your name" to the book as a favor between friends ("Just the first name, darling, it's practically nothing").

blocks.label: Agenda
blocks.html: Amaranth tallies what Vesperine owes. From Night 5 they walk the city collecting names, signatures, and kiss-sealed acknowledgments of debt. On Night 7 they read the Book aloud, and every name in it goes to the Dusk Court unless the Accord is renewed. Amaranth is bound by the rules: they cannot lie, cannot take an unwilling name, and must honor any loophole a clever PC finds in the Book's fine print.

blocks.label: Stat & mechanic notes
blocks.html: CR 6. AC 15, HP 90. While under a host's hospitality (fed bread and salt in someone's home), Amaranth cannot harm or be harmed by that household. Debt-Call: one creature that owes a fey a favor must make a DC 15 Charisma save or be compelled to honor it immediately. Book of Forfeit Names: a name written in it gives the Dusk Court a claim on its owner. Striking a name requires reading Amaranth's fine print (Investigation DC 17) and finding the loophole. Each of the six Dusk Court debts in the Book has a different one: an unwitnessed signature, an expired date, a name misspelled, a debt already paid in a dream, and so on.

blocks.label: Glamour & reveal: as Notary Amar Thorne
blocks.html:
• Cover identity: A meticulous, soft-spoken notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows. They witness contracts, check wills, and explain fine print to frightened clients for very reasonable fees. Clients sometimes notice that the contract they signed is a little longer than they remember.
  • Tells:
  • They never lie, not even politely: "I can't say I love your hat, but it is certainly a hat."
  • The ink in their office blooms into tiny roses as it dries.
  • They refuse iron paperweights and use a polished river-stone instead.
  • Perception DC 14 in lamplight: the shadow of their head has antlers.
  • Everything smells faintly of roses and old paper.
  • Mirror reflection: An antlered herald in a dusk-colored coat, holding the vast red Book of Forfeit Names, and still smiling.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Dusk on Night 5. Amaranth reveals themself publicly, and with apologies, to begin collecting. 2. A PC signs anything Amaranth has notarized. 3. Someone finds a genuine loophole. Amaranth reveals themself out of sheer professional delight. 4. They are offered bread and salt as a guest. They must state their true name and nature before accepting.

Read-aloud: The Notary Closes the Ledger. Notary Thorne blots the last signature, examines it, and smiles that small, apologetic smile. "Thank you. That's everything in order." The lamps dim. The little office seems to grow taller, and so does the notary: antlers unfurl from their temples, threaded with roses; the drab clerk's coat flows into dusk-colored velvet embroidered with thorns. On the desk, the ledger swells into an enormous book bound in red leather, its pages whispering names. "I am Amaranth, Herald of the Dusk," they say gently. "Please don't be alarmed, darling. Everything you signed was perfectly legal. I made sure of it."

locations.name: The Velvet Opera
locations.html: A gold-and-crimson temple to spectacle. Five tiers of private boxes, each rented by a noble house and each with its own little curtain for "private conversations." Backstage is a maze of rope, sandbags, and costume racks. Feel: perfumed heat, applause, whispers behind fans.

locations.name: The Rosewater Gallery
locations.html: A long salon above the stage lined with mirrors and rose-trellises, centered on a fountain that flows with scented rosewater. Its tall clock is the city's most famous timepiece — and it stopped at 11:47 on the night of the murder. A secret door behind the mirror wall connects to the Dressing Gallery, where Madame Rook fits masks. The mirror wall's great central pane is the Oathless Glass (Part 2).

locations.name: The Sable Palazzo
locations.html: Aurelian's home in the Gilded Crescent: elegant, cold, and too big. His study holds a locked writing desk (riddle-lock), a portrait gallery with one portrait painted over, and his bedchamber, where a hidden cache holds his private journal.

locations.name: The Atelier of Madame Rook (Needle Row)
locations.html: A cozy shop overflowing with masks: feathered, porcelain, lacquered, beaded. Thessaly lives above it with three cats named after her ex-lovers. The back workroom holds glue pots, gold leaf — and, hidden in a hatbox, a wedding mask made for a bride forty years ago.

locations.name: Vos Perfumery (Needle Row)
locations.html: Glass bottles in every color, a copper still, and a tiefling who can identify anyone by scent. His order ledger is written in scent-code (riddle).

locations.name: The Hall of Vows
locations.html: White marble, silence, and the sound of a pen that writes by itself. The Ledger rests on a thorned lectern. Since the murder, the ink has begun to bleed and pages have started to blank out. The Vault of Broken Vows below stores torn-out, annulled pages — and one page that was deliberately removed decades ago.

locations.name: The Drowned Market
locations.html: Ankle-deep water, floating lanterns, stalls on stilts. The Thorn Syndicate's fence, Old Mother Brine, runs a shop called Things That Shouldn't Be Sold.

locations.name: The Tilted House
locations.html: The Lantern Watch headquarters, a building leaning so badly that pens roll off desks. Captain Hale's office has a locked strongbox containing a Syndicate purse.

locations.name: The Sable Crypt
locations.html: On Cypress Isle, the cemetery island. The Sable family tomb includes a marble sarcophagus inscribed Lady Isaveth Sable, Beloved Wife, Lost to the Sea — which is empty.

locations.name: The Thicketmoor
locations.html: Brambles the size of houses, golden honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud pits ogres consider a spa. Travellers vanish. Mostly men. Mostly loudly.

locations.name: The Lanternwood
locations.html: A forest where the trees give off soft blue light and moths the size of cats drift between them. Sleepers who wander here wake days later, smiling, with no memory of their dreams.

locations.name: The Saltgrave Coast
locations.html: Black cliffs, shipwrecks, and singing at night that every sailor pretends not to hear. Smugglers bring Syndicate cargo through the sea caves.

locations.name: The Duskvine Valley
locations.html: The most beautiful countryside in Carnelia: golden terraces, poplars, villages where everyone is a little too pale and very well-rested. Château Dusk crowns the hill.

locations.name: The Emberpeaks
locations.html: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs, and rope sky-bridges. Miners leave love poems at shrine-stones to keep the dragon in a good mood.

locations.name: The Gilded Crescent
locations.html: Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal. Balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.

locations.name: The Velvet Quarter
locations.html: Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens, and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf. The Rosewater Gallery (the murder scene) is on its second tier.

locations.name: Needle Row
locations.html: Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook, the city's most beloved maskmaker.

locations.name: The Drowned Market
locations.html: A half-sunken flea market under the old city, where the Thorn Syndicate sells anything, including secrets and people's debts.

locations.name: The Hall of Vows
locations.html: A white-marble temple-library on its own island, where the Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn. Tended by the Veiled Sisters.

locations.name: Lanternside
locations.html: Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, "the Tilted House."

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Poisoned
Languages Understands Common but can't speak

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the cherub is indistinguishable from a wax figurine on a mantel or cake.

entries.name: Melting Grace
entries.text: If the cherub takes Fire damage, it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn as it drips.
