entries.name: Wax Arrow
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition toward the next creature it sees until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Wax Cherub
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Vesperine's confectioners and candlewrights sculpt cherubs of scented wax for wedding cakes and opera boxes. A few soak up enough of the city's ambient longing to wake. A woken cherub keeps doing its job, badly: it shoots little wax arrows at strangers and giggles as they swoon at whoever happens to be nearby.
bestiary.where: Ballrooms, confectioners, the Velvet Opera's private boxes.
bestiary.tactics: It stays airborne and out of reach, shooting at whoever looks loneliest, and flees from candles. It is a nuisance, not a killer, and makes a good distraction in a larger scene.
hooks: A society wedding descends into chaos as the cake's cherubs start matchmaking the guests at random.
A chandler swears someone is enchanting her figurines, and the culprit is a lovesick apprentice.

entries.name: Glimmer-Dazed
entries.text: The reveler has Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition and Disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks.

entries.name: Crowd Cover
entries.text: While within 5 feet of another reveler, the reveler has Half Cover against ranged attacks.

entries.name: Bottle
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Bludgeoning damage.

bestiary.name: Masked Reveler
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Not every masked guest is a villain. Many are bored nobles, dock hands in borrowed silk, or dreamers dazed on glimmer, steered by a fey whisper or a Syndicate paymaster. Revelers make ideal minions for masquerade fights. Most of them would rather be dancing, and nearly all can be talked out of it.
bestiary.where: Any masquerade, ball, gambling salon, or canal-side party. Use as minions.
bestiary.tactics: Revelers swarm in groups of four to eight, surrounding a target and shouting for help from the music. Each flees if Bloodied. A DC 12 Charisma (Persuasion) check, or a splash of cold water, makes one stop fighting and wander off.
hooks: A hostess pays the party to keep her drunken guests from killing each other until midnight.
Every reveler at one ball wears the same porcelain mask, made by the same missing maskmaker.

bestiary.meta: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, Unaligned
lines: Immunities Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

entries.name: Rumor Mill
entries.text: Each creature that starts its turn in the swarm's space hears a whispered secret about one creature it can see (the GM chooses; half are true). It must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its turn.

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny moth. It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Dusty Wings
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 0 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4) Piercing damage, or 2 (1d4) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied.

bestiary.name: Gossip Moth Swarm
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Pale moths with wings patterned like tiny, overheard words. They gather wherever people whisper about each other, feeding on the warmth of shared secrets. Dream-readers of the Hush House say the moths are a lesser cousin of the Moth Court's dream-eaters, which would explain why they always know who is sleeping with whom.
bestiary.where: Salons, opera wardrobes, confessionals, hat shops, and attics full of old letters.
bestiary.tactics: The swarm smothers anyone holding a light and stays inside crowds, where area spells would hit bystanders. It disperses when its space is lit by bright light for a full round.
hooks: Someone is breeding gossip moths to steal secrets for blackmail, and they're nesting in the opera wardrobe.
A swarm keeps following one party member, whispering things about them that only their lover could know.
bestiary.imm: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

lines: Gear Chain Shirt, Lantern, Manacles, Shield, Spear

entries.name: Reflection Check
entries.text: The constable can tell whether a creature it can see within 30 feet is oathless (its reflection lags) by holding up its lantern-mirror (no action required).

entries.name: Spear
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Lantern Flash (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, one creature the constable can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target has the Blinded condition until the start of the constable's next turn.

bestiary.name: Lantern Watch Constable
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: The Lantern Watch keeps Vesperine's peace by lamplight and patience. Constables carry hooded lanterns backed with a sliver of mirror, the better to catch an oathless traveler's lagging reflection or a fey's missing shadow. Most are honest and underpaid; a few owe the Thorn Syndicate more than they could ever earn.
bestiary.where: Every street in Vesperine. Use for chases, arrests, and patrols.
bestiary.tactics: Constables fight in pairs, using Lantern Flash to blind a runner and then manacling them. They retreat and blow whistles rather than die, and three blasts bring a sergeant in 1d4 rounds.
hooks: A constable quietly asks the party to find out which of his colleagues is taking Syndicate coin.
The Watch is rounding up anyone with a lagging reflection, and the party's reflections lag.

lines: Gear Lantern, Longsword, Manacles, Splint Armor, Whistle

entries.name: Reflection Check
entries.text: As the constable's trait.

entries.name: Rally the Watch
entries.text: Allied Lantern Watch members within 30 feet of the sergeant have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sergeant makes two Longsword attacks.

entries.name: Longsword
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage if used with two hands.

entries.name: Lantern Flash (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the sergeant can see within 15 feet. Failure: The target has the Blinded condition until the start of the sergeant's next turn.

entries.name: Halt!
entries.text: Trigger: A creature within 5 feet of the sergeant moves away from it. Response: The sergeant makes one Longsword attack against the creature. On a hit, the creature's Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.

bestiary.name: Lantern Watch Sergeant
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Sergeants are veterans of a dozen masquerade murders and a hundred canal brawls. They know which salons pay protection and which nobles are untouchable, and they have opinions about both. A sergeant can be the party's best ally in Vesperine or its most persistent problem.
bestiary.where: Watch-houses, murder scenes, raids on the Drowned Market. Elite for constable patrols.
bestiary.tactics: The sergeant leads 2–4 constables, pinning a target with Halt! while the others close in. It negotiates before it kills and accepts a surrender honestly.
hooks: A sergeant offers to lose a warrant if the party retrieves her brother's gambling marker from the Blue Hour.
The sergeant investigating a murder is the murderer's alibi, and she knows it.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the mask is indistinguishable from an ordinary porcelain or lacquered masquerade mask.

entries.name: Worn
entries.text: While attached to a creature's face, the mask moves with the host, and attacks against the mask have Disadvantage unless they also target the host (a miss by 5 or less hits the host instead). The host can't speak except to say what the mask wishes.

entries.name: Latch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Psychic damage. If the target is a Medium or Small Humanoid not wearing a helm, the mask attaches to its face. The host can take an action to pull it free with a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check.

entries.name: Whispered Command
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, the mask's host. Failure: 5 (2d4) Psychic damage, and the host uses its next action or movement as the mask telepathically commands (it won't harm itself). Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Smiling Mask
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Some masks in Vesperine's antique shops were never made. They grew, like barnacles on the hull of the city's vanity, in the space behind a mirror where faces are forgotten. A Smiling Mask wants a face. It wants to be adored, to flirt, to be kissed at midnight. Its hosts later remember a wonderful evening that they did not choose.
bestiary.where: Mask shops on Needle Row, opera wardrobes, the attics of old noble houses.
bestiary.tactics: It hides on a mask-rack, latches onto the first guest who lifts it, and uses that host as a shield and a puppet. It abandons a host that is Bloodied and flees to find another face.
hooks: A shy clerk has become the toast of the season overnight, and her friends are frightened of her new smile.
A maskmaker's apprentice found a box of masks that are warm to the touch.

entries.name: Glimmer Rush
entries.text: While Bloodied, the glimmer-eater has Advantage on attack rolls and can't be Charmed or Frightened.

entries.name: Docile Thrall
entries.text: The glimmer-eater has Disadvantage on saving throws against spells and effects of the Thornwake (any servant of Lady Nocturne Vesh).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The glimmer-eater makes two Dagger attacks.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Snort Glimmer (1/Day)
entries.text: The glimmer-eater gains 7 (2d6) Temporary Hit Points and its Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Glimmer-Eater
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Glimmer is silver dust refined from the Moth Court's dream-powder and sold through the Thorn Syndicate. It makes everything shine. Then it makes everything dull, unless you take more. Long-time users grow pale and hollow-eyed, wiry, quick, and pliant to the Thornwake's whispered commands. They aren't evil, only hungry, and they can be saved.
bestiary.where: The Drowned Market, opium-and-glimmer dens, the back alleys behind the Velvet Opera.
bestiary.tactics: Glimmer-eaters attack in packs of three to six when commanded or desperate, using daggers and numbers. Offering a vial of glimmer (or convincingly faking one with a DC 13 Deception check) makes one stop fighting at once.
hooks: A noble hires the party to find her missing son, who is now a glimmer-eater in the Drowned Market.
The glimmer supply has suddenly been cut, and a hundred addicts are rioting near the Gull Steps.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless on a dress form or hanger, the gown is indistinguishable from ordinary clothing.

entries.name: Endless Waltz
entries.text: The gown doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks when it moves, so long as it moved at least 10 feet in a straight line that turn.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The gown makes two Sleeve Lash attacks. It can replace one of them with Embrace.

entries.name: Sleeve Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Embrace
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 12, one Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet. Failure: The target is pulled into a dance and has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12). While Grappled this way, the target has the Restrained condition and moves with the gown.

bestiary.name: Hollow Gown
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: A gown worn to the same ball every year for a lifetime keeps the shape of its wearer, and sometimes keeps her longing too. When the owner dies, the gown goes on dancing. Hollow gowns are animated by habit, not malice. They are drawn to music and drag the unwary into waltzes that end only when the partner collapses.
bestiary.where: Wardrobes of old houses, costume shops, abandoned ballrooms.
bestiary.tactics: The gown waltzes in from the shadows, embraces the nearest dancer, and whirls them away from their allies. It ignores anyone who stands perfectly still. Silencing the music (or cutting a seam with a critical hit) makes it collapse for 1 round.
hooks: A widowed duke wants his late wife's gown destroyed. It keeps returning to his bedroom door.
A costume shop is renting out gowns that walk back home on their own.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Immunities Poison; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Poisoned, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Cloying Perfume
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature (other than the ooze) that starts its turn within 10 feet. Failure: The creature has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. While Poisoned this way, it is dizzily enamored and can't willingly move away from the ooze. Success: The creature is immune to this trait for 24 hours.

entries.name: Amorphous
entries.text: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

bestiary.name: Attar Ooze
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: The perfumers of Needle Row pour spoiled batches into the canals, and the canals give them back. An attar ooze is a rose-pink slick of concentrated scent, sweet enough to make the eyes water and the heart race. Victims wander toward it smiling, convinced that someone they love is waiting just ahead.
bestiary.where: Perfumeries, bathhouses, canal drains in the Velvet Quarter.
bestiary.tactics: The ooze lurks in a drain or behind a curtain until its perfume has befuddled several creatures, then engulfs the nearest. Strong wind (a gust of wind spell or an open window in a storm) disperses its perfume trait for 1 minute.
hooks: A perfumer's signature scent is causing riots of infatuation, and the vats are alive.
A rival house sends a bottle of "exclusive attar" as a gift. The bottle is moving.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Poisoned, Prone

lines: Languages Every language its original knows

entries.name: Mirror Image Of You
entries.text: The reflection looks exactly like the creature whose reflection it stole, but backwards (its scars, parting, and rings are on the wrong side).

entries.name: Sunlight Shatter
entries.text: While in sunlight, the reflection has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The reflection makes two Glass Fingers attacks.

entries.name: Glass Fingers
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Mirror Step
entries.text: While within 5 feet of a mirror or other reflective surface, the reflection teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of another reflective surface it can see within 60 feet.

bestiary.name: Lagging Reflection
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: The Oathless Glass is not the only mirror in Carnelia that remembers. When a traveler passes through a mirror without a promise to anchor them, their reflection sometimes stays behind, angry and alone. It learns to walk. It practices their smile. Eventually it wants their life, and it is very good at pretending to be the one who belongs.
bestiary.where: Mirrored galleries, the Rosewater Gallery, dressing rooms, places the Oathless Glass has touched.
bestiary.tactics: It fights near mirrors, stepping between them to flank. It targets its original first and tries to swap places, knocking them unconscious and hiding the body. Breaking every mirror in a room traps it on foot.
hooks: A party member's reflection is a beat late, and then, one morning, it isn't there at all.
Two identical opera stars are each accusing the other of being the impostor.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the shardwing is indistinguishable from a stained-glass window panel or a glass sculpture.

entries.name: Prismatic Body
entries.text: In bright light, attack rolls against the shardwing from more than 30 feet away have Disadvantage.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The shardwing makes two Shard Claw attacks.

entries.name: Shard Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Shard Spray (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 14 (4d6) Slashing damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Shardwing
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: The glassblowers of the Lanternside district fire their kilns with elemental coals, and now and then a spirit of the earth's deep places wakes inside a cooling window. Shardwings are guardians of glass. They nest in cathedral rose-windows and opera skylights, and will defend them from thieves, birds, and clumsy duelists alike.
bestiary.where: Skylights, cathedral windows, glassworks, the Rosewater Gallery's dome.
bestiary.tactics: It drops from a skylight, sprays the largest group, then claws at anyone who carries a hammer or mace. It flees through the nearest window if reduced to 15 Hit Points or fewer.
hooks: The Velvet Opera's new stained-glass ceiling keeps cutting stagehands, and the panel of a winged saint is missing.
A glazier will pay well for a shardwing's heart-crystal, which is still alive.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the topiary is indistinguishable from an ordinary sculpted hedge in the shape of a swan, lion, or embracing lovers.

entries.name: Garden Maze
entries.text: The topiary doesn't need to see to navigate a hedge maze, and it knows the location of every creature touching a hedge within 60 feet.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The topiary makes two Thorned Embrace attacks.

entries.name: Thorned Embrace
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). The topiary can have two creatures Grappled at once.

bestiary.name: Rosewater Topiary
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Vesperine's noble gardens are watered with rosewater from the Lanternwood springs, and in the oldest estates the hedges have drunk enough fey water to stir. Topiaries are territorial, jealous of their gardens, and possessive of the lovers who meet in their shade. Couples who kiss in a topiary maze sometimes find the exits have moved.
bestiary.where: Noble estates, the Opera Gardens, abandoned walled gardens on the city's edge.
bestiary.tactics: It waits at a dead end of the maze, grapples intruders, and holds them while other topiaries close in. It releases anyone who offers it water or fertilizer, at least for a moment.
hooks: Guests at a garden party have gone missing in the hedge maze, and the hedges are thicker than this morning.
A gardener begs the party to prune her mistress's topiary swan before it eats the new husband.

lines: Senses Blindsight 10 ft., Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 13

entries.name: Candleflame Glamour
entries.text: While the drake hangs motionless from a ceiling, it is indistinguishable from a crystal chandelier, and creatures that see it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice its eyes among the prisms.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes two Crystal Bite attacks.

entries.name: Crystal Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Prism Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 21 (6d6) Radiant damage, and the creature has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Glittering Dazzle
entries.text: Trigger: A creature the drake can see hits it with an attack roll while the drake is in bright light. Response: The attacker must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Chandelier Drake
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Small, vain dragons with hides of faceted crystal, chandelier drakes love light, music, and applause more than gold. The great opera houses of Vesperine have each hosted one at some point, usually without knowing. A drake who nests above a stage considers the performers its hoard, and woe to the critic who pans its favorite soprano.
bestiary.where: Opera houses, ballrooms with high ceilings, the crystal gallery of the Opera Council.
bestiary.tactics: It drops from the ceiling mid-performance, breathes a blinding prism across the front rows, and then bites anyone who threatens its favorites. Praise or a beautiful song (DC 14 Performance) buys a round of peace.
hooks: The Velvet Opera's chandelier has eaten a critic. Management wants it to stop, but not to leave; ticket sales have never been better.
A collector wants a chandelier drake's egg, said to be a single flawless diamond that glows when sung to.

lines: Skills Acrobatics +7, Deception +9, Insight +5, Persuasion +6, Stealth +10
Gear Garrote, Masquerade Mask, Poisoned Stilettos, Studded Leather Armor
Languages Common, Thieves' Cant, one other

entries.name: Evasion
entries.text: If the garrote is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails, unless it has the Incapacitated condition.

entries.name: Flirt's Opening
entries.text: The garrote has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that has the Charmed condition, or that it has spoken with privately for at least 1 minute in the past hour.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The garrote makes two Poisoned Stiletto attacks, or one Stiletto attack and one Garrote attack.

entries.name: Poisoned Stiletto
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Poison damage.

entries.name: Garrote
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Slashing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). While Grappled, the target can't speak or cast spells with Verbal components.

entries.name: Charming Distraction
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, one Humanoid the garrote can see within 30 feet that can hear it. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Slip Away
entries.text: The garrote takes the Disengage or Hide action.

bestiary.name: Velvet Garrote
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: The Thorn Syndicate's most expensive assassins never look like assassins. They look like the most interesting person at the ball: a widow with a wicked laugh, a duelist with a poet's hands. They court their targets for an evening, lure them to a quiet balcony, and leave them there. The Syndicate calls them Velvet Garrotes, and it never hires one twice for the same city.
bestiary.where: Masquerades, opera boxes, gambling salons, rooftops of the Velvet Quarter.
bestiary.tactics: It isolates a target with flirtation, charms anyone who intervenes, and strikes from Half Cover with poisoned stilettos. It never fights fair and never fights long; if Bloodied, it slips away and tries again another night.
hooks: Someone at the masquerade has been paid to kill the party's patron, and they're dancing with her right now.
A garrote wants out of the Syndicate and will trade a client list for safe passage through the Oathless Glass.

lines: Resistances Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
Immunities Necrotic, Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained
Languages Common and the languages of every opera she sang

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.text: The diva can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. She takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if she ends her turn inside an object.

entries.name: Encore
entries.text: If the diva is destroyed while her opera's final score still exists, she re-forms on its stage at the next full moon. Burning the score, or performing her unfinished final aria for her, lays her to rest.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The diva makes two Spectral Caress attacks.

entries.name: Spectral Caress
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Aria of Ruin (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the diva that can hear her. Failure: 27 (5d10) Psychic damage, and the creature has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn, using its movement to approach the stage. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Vanish Into the Wings
entries.text: The diva has the Invisible condition until she makes an attack roll or uses Aria of Ruin, or until the start of her next turn.

bestiary.name: Phantom Diva
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Every opera house in Vesperine has a ghost, and the Velvet Opera has three. A phantom diva is the shade of a great soprano who died before her final bow, usually by poison, jealousy, or a falling sandbag. She is vain, theatrical, and lonely, and she is very fond of young understudies, whom she coaches and whose rivals she murders.
bestiary.where: Opera houses, concert halls, the flooded old theater in the Drowned Market.
bestiary.tactics: She sings from the rafters, slips invisibly between boxes, and saves Aria of Ruin for the moment the whole party is on stage together. She can be bargained with by anyone who flatters her technique sincerely.
hooks: The understudy for tonight's premiere has a ghostly patron, and the lead soprano is next.
A composer found the diva's unfinished aria and wants the party to keep her alive long enough to hear him play it.
bestiary.res: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
bestiary.imm: Necrotic, Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The muse has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Kindled Genius
entries.text: A creature that spends a short rest in the muse's company gains Inspiration-like favor; once before its next long rest, it can give itself Advantage on one ability check or attack roll.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The muse makes two Gilded Brush attacks, and it can use Spellcasting in place of one of them.

entries.name: Gilded Brush
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Radiant damage plus 9 (2d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The gallery muse casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Charm Person, Minor Illusion, Message; 2/Day Each: Hypnotic Pattern, Suggestion; 1/Day Each: Greater Invisibility, Mass Cure Wounds

entries.name: Stolen Breath
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature within 30 feet that the muse can see. Failure: The target is so moved by the muse that it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn. A creature that knows the muse's true name automatically succeeds.

bestiary.name: Gallery Muse
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Celestial patrons of art came to Vesperine a thousand years ago and fell in love with it. A few never left. A gallery muse lives inside a single masterpiece and steps out of the frame for the artists she favors. Her inspiration is real, her attention intoxicating, and her jealousy terrible. She is good, but she is not gentle, and she has never forgiven anyone who painted over her.
bestiary.where: The Rosewater Gallery, artists' garrets, temples of the arts.
bestiary.tactics: She prefers to dazzle rather than kill, using Hypnotic Pattern and Stolen Breath, then strikes with her brush at anyone threatening a work of art. If an artwork she inhabits is threatened, she surrenders anything to protect it.
hooks: A struggling painter has become a genius overnight. His friends say he hasn't slept in a month and won't leave the gallery.
Someone has stolen the muse's painting, and now she's walking the Velvet Quarter looking for it, and for a new artist.

entries.name: A Thousand Faces
entries.text: The fiend's masked face appears to every viewer as the face they find most beautiful. A creature that sees it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the fiend until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Kiss-Bargain
entries.text: Any willing creature the fiend kisses can make one wish of it (as the Suggestion spell's scope; the GM decides what is possible). The creature then owes the fiend one favor of equal weight, enforced by the Accord.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fiend makes three Masked Blade attacks, or it uses Spellcasting and makes one Masked Blade attack.

entries.name: Masked Blade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The masque fiend casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Charm Person, Disguise Self, Detect Thoughts; 2/Day Each: Dimension Door, Suggestion; 1/Day Each: Dominate Person, Geas

entries.name: Change of Partners
entries.text: Trigger: The fiend is hit by an attack roll while a creature it has Charmed is within 5 feet of it. Response: The fiend swaps places with that creature, which becomes the target of the attack instead.

bestiary.name: Masque Fiend
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Infernal courtiers love Vesperine's masquerades, where everyone already expects a handsome stranger to offer something too good to refuse. A masque fiend trades in kiss-bargains. It grants small wishes for small favors and keeps a ledger of who owes what. By the end of a season it can call in enough debts to swing an Opera Council vote.
bestiary.where: Masquerades, the Opera Council's antechambers, the Blue Hour's private rooms.
bestiary.tactics: It never fights alone if it can help it: it surrounds itself with Charmed admirers, swaps places with them under attack, and uses Dimension Door to leave when Bloodied. A creature that refuses its bargain with a clever counter-offer earns its genuine respect.
hooks: Half the Opera Council has kissed the same masked stranger this season.
A noblewoman wants out of a kiss-bargain she made at sixteen, and the fiend has come to collect at her wedding.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Languages Understands Common and Sylvan but can't speak

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The sentinel has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Mirror Bound
entries.text: The sentinel can't move more than 300 feet from the mirror it guards. If that mirror is broken, the sentinel has the Incapacitated condition until it is repaired.

entries.name: Reflective Hide
entries.text: When the sentinel succeeds on a saving throw against a spell that targets only it, the spell is reflected back at the caster, who must make the same save (or is the target of the same attack).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sentinel makes two Silvered Fist attacks.

entries.name: Silvered Fist
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) Force damage.

entries.name: Reflected Ray (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 36 (8d8) Radiant damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Silver Sentinel
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: When the Accord was signed, the first Oathwardens commissioned guardians for the mirrors that matter: a statue of living silver for each glass that touches another world. The sentinels still stand, polished and patient, in galleries where nobody remembers why they were placed. They wake only when someone tries to pass through without a promise.
bestiary.where: The Rosewater Gallery, the Opera Council's vault, any mirror connected to the Oathless Glass.
bestiary.tactics: It stands between intruders and its mirror, punching anyone who approaches and firing Reflected Ray down lines of attackers. It ignores anyone who speaks a sincere promise aloud in front of the glass.
hooks: A sentinel has woken in the Rosewater Gallery for the first time in thirty years, which means someone passed through the Oathless Glass.
The Syndicate wants the party to distract a sentinel while its burglars steal the mirror behind it.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Languages All languages known by anyone it has reflected, Telepathy 120 ft.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the reflection fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Hall of Mirrors
entries.text: The reflection is always surrounded by reflections of the people who look at it. Each creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the reflection and can see it must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or attack its own reflection (no effect) instead of taking an action this turn. A creature that averts its eyes automatically succeeds but has Disadvantage on attack rolls against the reflection.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The reflection makes three Glass Talon attacks.

entries.name: Glass Talon
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Steal Face (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 19, one creature the reflection can see within 60 feet. Failure: 44 (8d10) Psychic damage, and the reflection steals the target's face. The target can't be recognized by anyone, loses the ability to speak, and has Disadvantage on Charisma checks until the face is restored by Greater Restoration or the reflection's destruction. Success: Half damage only.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the thousand-faced reflection can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The thousand-faced reflection regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Mirror Lash
entries.text: The reflection makes one Glass Talon attack, dealing only the Slashing damage (16 (2d10 + 5)).

entries.name: Shift Through Glass
entries.text: The reflection teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see within 5 feet of a reflective surface.

entries.name: Who Are You? (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 19, one creature within 60 feet that the reflection can see. Failure: 22 (4d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Thousand-Faced Reflection
bestiary.region: Vesperine, the City of Masks
bestiary.lore: Lysander, the man in the Oathless Glass, says there is a thing at the bottom of every mirror: a reflection that never belonged to anyone, built from all the faces that ever looked and lied. Once in a generation it climbs up toward a glass that has grown thin. It wants a face of its own, and it collects other people's until it finds one that fits.
bestiary.where: The bottom of the Oathless Glass, the Rosewater Gallery's hall of mirrors, the endgame of *The Black Kiss*.
bestiary.tactics: It fights in a room of mirrors, stepping between them with legendary actions and using Steal Face on whoever leads the party. It focuses talons on anyone who has averted their eyes. Covering or shattering the mirrors in its lair halves its legendary action uses.
hooks: Faces are going missing from Vesperine's portraits, then from the people who sat for them.
Lysander begs the party to stop the thing climbing up through the Oathless Glass before Night 7.

entries.name: Pocket Bargain
entries.text: A creature that gives the buttonthief a button, ribbon, or small promise can ask it one question about the area within 1 mile; it answers truthfully, then flies off, delighted.

entries.name: Pinprick
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

entries.name: Filch
entries.text: The buttonthief steals one unattended or loosely worn item weighing no more than 1 pound from a creature within 5 feet. The creature notices if it succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

entries.name: Vanish
entries.text: The buttonthief takes the Hide action, even while only lightly obscured.

bestiary.name: Buttonthief
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Hedge-sprites of the Lanternwood's edge, mossy and button-eyed, no bigger than a hand. Buttonthieves collect fasteners, promises, and the small change of human life, which they trade among themselves like coins. They are harmless, mostly, and infuriating, always. Pipwhistle Dewlace is their most famous rogue.
bestiary.where: Hedgerows, garden walls, the Lanternwood's edge, the pockets of the unwary.
bestiary.tactics: Buttonthieves never fight. They steal, hide, and bargain. If cornered, one pricks a finger and darts away. Trading with them is often the fastest way to learn a road's secrets.
hooks: Every button on the party's clothing vanished overnight, and the culprits left a polite receipt.
A buttonthief offers to sell the party the "lost promise" of a missing noble.

entries.name: Drawn to Light
entries.text: The moth must use its movement to approach the brightest light source it can see within 60 feet, unless it is Charmed or Frightened.

entries.name: Proboscis
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Sleepy Dust (1/Day)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 11, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the moth. Failure: The creature has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, as it yawns uncontrollably.

bestiary.name: Glimmerwing Moth
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Cat-sized moths with violet-and-gold wings drift between the Lanternwood's glowing trees like slow lanterns. They feed on nectar, sweat, and spilled dream-dust from the Moth Court, and they are trained as steeds and hunting birds by the court's smaller fey. Their scales sparkle on the skin for days.
bestiary.where: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court's gardens, any lit window near a fey forest.
bestiary.tactics: Moths circle torchbearers and dust them to sleep. They scatter at once if their light source goes out or if anyone produces a brighter light elsewhere.
hooks: A swarm of glimmerwings is following the party's lantern deep into the Lanternwood.
A child of the village wants a glimmerwing as a pet and has already named it.

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the dancer is indistinguishable from a large spotted toadstool.

entries.name: Ring of Revelry
entries.text: While three or more ringcap dancers stand in a circle, any creature that enters the circle for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 11 Charisma saving throw or spend its turn dancing (it can take no actions and its movement keeps it inside the ring).

entries.name: Spore Slap
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

bestiary.name: Ringcap Dancer
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Fairy rings are not decorative. The toadstools that make them are ringcap dancers, mushroom-folk who feed on the exhaustion of revelers caught in their circles. Travelers who dance all night in a ring wake at dawn surrounded by fat, contented mushrooms, and a year older.
bestiary.where: Forest clearings, village greens near fey roads, the Lanternwood revels.
bestiary.tactics: Ringcaps stay still until someone is trapped in the ring, then shuffle closer to slap and spore the dancers. They are slow and foolish; uprooting one from the ring breaks the circle.
hooks: A bride never came home from her own wedding dance, and the village green has a new circle of mushrooms.
An alchemist pays well for ringcap spores, the key ingredient in a "dance-all-night" tonic.

lines: Resistances Acid, Cold, Fire, Necrotic, Thunder
Immunities Lightning, Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained
Languages Understands Sylvan but can't speak

entries.name: Lure
entries.text: A creature that sees the wisp's light for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or use its next movement to approach it, believing it a lantern carried by a friend.

entries.name: Shock
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Lightning damage.

entries.name: Dim
entries.text: The wisp extinguishes its light and has the Invisible condition until it uses Shock or relights as a Bonus Action.

bestiary.name: Lanternwisp
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The lights that lead travelers off the Lanternwood paths are minor fey that feed on fear and wonder in equal measure. Lanternwisps work with nymphs, ringcaps, and worse, leading their prey into ponds, rings, and briars, then sipping the panic like wine.
bestiary.where: Fey roads, marsh edges, the Lanternwood, any place where travelers get lost at night.
bestiary.tactics: The wisp leads victims toward hazards and allies, shocking anyone who stops following. It flees from anyone who ignores it, and it can be bribed with a story that frightens it.
hooks: A troupe of actors was led off the road by "the lights of an inn" and hasn't been seen since.
A lanternwisp offers to guide the party to the Moth Court, for a scream.
bestiary.imm: Lightning, Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

entries.name: Borrowed Life
entries.text: The swapper can magically take the appearance of a Small or Medium Humanoid it has observed for at least an hour (no action required while it sleeps in their bed). It keeps its own statistics.

entries.name: Iron Allergy
entries.text: A creature that touches the swapper with cold iron reveals its true form until the end of the swapper's next turn.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The swapper makes two Needle Bite attacks.

entries.name: Needle Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The hearth-swapper casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12): At Will: Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation; 1/Day Each: Charm Person, Sleep

bestiary.name: Hearth-Swapper
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Some fey want nothing more than to try a mortal life on for size. A hearth-swapper steals into a home, puts the rightful occupant to sleep under a hill, and takes their place for a season: eating their bread, doing their job badly, kissing their sweetheart too eagerly. The real person returns months later with no memory and a strange taste for honey.
bestiary.where: Villages near the Lanternwood, the farms of the Duskvine, anywhere a fey road crosses a doorstep.
bestiary.tactics: It avoids combat by bluffing. Exposed, it puts the nearest attacker to sleep, bites, and runs for the nearest hedge. It will trade the location of the sleeping original for its own freedom.
hooks: A baker has suddenly forgotten how to bake, but he has become a wonderful dancer.
Two identical brides arrive at the same wedding, and only one is allergic to the iron horseshoe over the door.

entries.name: Dream-Taster
entries.text: The courtier knows the most recent dream of any sleeping creature within 30 feet.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The courtier makes two Silk Rapier attacks, or one Silk Rapier attack and uses Dream Dust.

entries.name: Silk Rapier
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Dream Dust (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 10-foot Cube within 30 feet. Failure: The creature has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute or until it takes damage or another creature takes an action to shake it awake.

bestiary.name: Hushwing Courtier
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The tall, pale moth-fey of Queen Ilysse's court have feathered antennae and wings patterned with staring eyes. Courtiers are the queen's gentry and dream-harvesters. They glide into sleeping villages, sip dreams from dreamers' lips, and leave silver dust on the pillows. They are elegant, polite, and hopelessly addicted to the sweetness of mortal hope.
bestiary.where: The Moth Court's Cocoon Palace, sleeping villages, the Hush House in Vesperine.
bestiary.tactics: Courtiers put enemies to sleep first and duel the rest with rapier elegance. They never harm a sleeper, and they yield if offered a dream more delicious than the fight.
hooks: Villagers all over the valley wake exhausted and smiling, with silver dust on their pillows.
A courtier begs the party to help it quit dream-harvesting before the queen notices.

lines: Languages The languages it knew in life, most a century out of date

entries.name: Endless Dance
entries.text: The dancer can't stop moving. If it ends its turn in the same space it started, it takes 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Dawn Release
entries.text: If the dancer is in sunlight at dawn and a living creature dances one full minute with it, the dancer crumbles peacefully to dust and can't rise again.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The dancer makes two Grasping Whirl attacks.

entries.name: Grasping Whirl
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage, and the dancer can move the target up to 10 feet with it.

bestiary.name: Revel-Worn Dancer
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Mortals who join a fey revel and never leave dance on long after their hearts give out. Their bodies dry like pressed flowers; their finery rots to lace; their feet never stop. Revel-worn dancers are not cruel. They are desperate for a partner to share the burden, and they will drag one in whether that partner wants to dance or not.
bestiary.where: The Lanternwood revels, fairy rings, abandoned ballrooms near fey roads.
bestiary.tactics: Dancers whirl victims away from their allies and toward the deepest part of the revel. They pursue tirelessly and ignore anyone who stands still, which can be a lifesaving trick for the clever.
hooks: A grieving widower wants the party to bring home the wife who vanished into a fey revel forty years ago.
The ballroom of an abandoned manor plays music every midnight, and the dancers are getting closer to the doors.

lines: Languages Understands Sylvan but can't speak

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.text: The hound has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hound's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

entries.name: Scent of Debt
entries.text: The hound can track any creature that owes a debt to the Dusk Court, unerringly, across any distance on the same plane.

entries.name: Thorned Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Poison damage. If the target is a creature, it has the Prone condition if it is Medium or smaller and fails a DC 13 Strength saving throw.

bestiary.name: Briar Hound of the Dusk
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The Fae Duke of the Dusk keeps hounds grown from rose-briars and moonlight. Their coats are thorns, their eyes are dew, and their baying sounds like a choir in a cathedral. Briar hounds hunt those who owe the Dusk Court a debt: anyone who said "thank you" carelessly, ate fey food, or broke a fey bargain.
bestiary.where: The Lanternwood, the roads to the Dusk Court at twilight, any place a fey debt is owed.
bestiary.tactics: Hounds hunt in packs of three to six, knocking prey down and surrounding it. They stop at once if the quarry repays its debt or offers a fair new bargain.
hooks: A pack of briar hounds is baying outside the inn, and they want the bard who thanked a fey for the wine.
A broken leash of rose-stems is found on the road; a hound has slipped its master, and is hunting for itself.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The piper has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The piper makes two Hoof Kick attacks, or one Hoof Kick attack and uses Pipes of Revelry.

entries.name: Hoof Kick
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Pipes of Revelry
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 60 feet that can hear the pipes. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition for 1 minute and must dance (its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls). It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

bestiary.name: Revel Piper
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Goat-legged, horned, and grinning, revel pipers are the life of every fey party and the talent scouts of the Moth Court. They play the Velvet Opera's after-parties in human guise and lead the best dancers out to the Lanternwood "for an after-party," where Queen Ilysse's cocoons wait. Most pipers tell themselves it's all harmless fun.
bestiary.where: Fey revels, the Velvet Opera's after-parties, the Lanternwood roads.
bestiary.tactics: A piper charms the strongest enemy into dancing and kicks anyone who tries to stop the music. It flees laughing when Bloodied. It can be turned with a better party, a better dancer, or a genuine compliment.
hooks: The fiddler at tonight's ball has hooves inside his boots, and he's already chosen his dance partners.
A piper wants the party's help winning a musical duel against a rival, with a reward of anything in his pocket.

lines: Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Sticky Sweet
entries.text: A creature that touches the slick or hits it with a melee attack must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or have the Restrained condition until it escapes (a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check as an action). Weapons stuck this way are released if the slick dies.

entries.name: Irresistible Scent
entries.text: Beasts and Fey within 60 feet are drawn to the slick and must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw at the start of each turn or move toward it.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Acid damage.

bestiary.name: Nectar Slick
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The flowers of the Lanternwood bleed nectar so rich that it pools at the roots of the oldest trees. Left long enough, a pool learns to hunt. A nectar slick is a golden, translucent ooze full of drowned moths and petals. It smells of honey and summer, and creatures crawl into it smiling.
bestiary.where: The roots of ancient flowering trees, fey gardens, the Thicketmoor's honey-hives.
bestiary.tactics: It waits under a blossoming tree for something sweet-toothed to blunder in, then sticks it fast and digests it slowly. Fire makes it bubble and recoil, and it flees from smoke.
hooks: A beekeeper's whole hive has vanished into a glowing pool under the old linden tree.
Moth Court alchemists pay handsomely for a jar of slick; it's the base of the finest dream-mead.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Tremorsense 60 ft.; Passive Perception 13

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries.text: The matron can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without making an ability check.

entries.name: Web Walker
entries.text: The matron ignores movement restrictions caused by webs and silk, and knows the location of any creature touching its web.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The matron makes one Bite attack and one Silk Lash attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Poison damage.

entries.name: Silk Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 15 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Restrained condition until freed (DC 13 Strength check, or 10 Slashing damage to the silk).

entries.name: Cocoon (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one Restrained creature within 10 feet. Failure: The creature is wrapped in a dream-cocoon and has the Unconscious condition until freed. It has Total Cover while cocooned.

bestiary.name: Silkspinner Matron
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The Cocoon Palace was spun by spiders, not moths. Silkspinner matrons are the great pale spiders of the Moth Court, its weavers and jailers, who wrap sleeping dreamers in shining silk so the courtiers can feed on them at leisure. They serve the queen faithfully and dream, in their own slow way, of eating her.
bestiary.where: The Cocoon Palace, the Lanternwood's high canopy, abandoned silk mills.
bestiary.tactics: A matron hangs above a gallery, lashes one victim with silk, and cocoons it before biting the rest. It retreats into the ceiling when Bloodied and sends silk-lashes from cover.
hooks: Missing revelers are hanging in cocoons in the palace's high galleries, and the matron is guarding them.
A matron offers a secret bargain: help her poison the queen, and she'll release every dreamer.

lines: Senses Blindsight 10 ft., Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 14

entries.name: Glamoured Scales
entries.text: The drake's iridescent scales shift with its mood. It can magically have the Invisible condition while motionless in dim light or darkness.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes two Bite attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Glamour Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 27 (6d8) Psychic damage, and the creature has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn, during which it sees the drake as its dearest friend. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Shimmer Away
entries.text: Trigger: A creature the drake can see targets it with an attack roll. Response: The drake imposes Disadvantage on the roll and teleports up to 15 feet after the attack.

bestiary.name: Lilt Drake
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Little dragons, scaled in the colors of soap bubbles and stained glass, lilt drakes were hatched in the Feywild and never quite left. They breathe glamour instead of fire, a shimmering mist that makes enemies into friends. They collect compliments and keep favorites, and can't resist a mortal who sings.
bestiary.where: The Lanternwood, fey gardens, the edges of the Dusk Court's twilight.
bestiary.tactics: The drake breathes first, then fights anyone who resisted. If it is losing, it flatters, bargains, and offers to become the party's "dearest friend" for a song a day.
hooks: A lilt drake has charmed a whole village into worshipping it, and the villagers seem very happy.
A noble's daughter wants a lilt drake as a familiar and has hired the party to capture one politely.

entries.name: Muse's Bargain
entries.text: A creature that willingly accepts the leannan as its muse gains Advantage on all Charisma (Performance) checks and on checks to create works of art. Each time it benefits, it gains 1 Exhaustion level, which can't be removed while the bargain lasts. The bargain ends if the creature refuses the leannan three times in one night.

entries.name: Beloved Face
entries.text: The leannan appears as an achingly beautiful figure suited to the viewer's tastes, dressed in silk and moonlight. Detect Evil and Good or Truesight reveals a pale, hungry thing with ink-stained lips.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The leannan makes two Caress of Thorns attacks, or it makes one and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Caress of Thorns
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Psychic damage, and the leannan regains Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The silken leannan casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Charm Person, Disguise Self, Message; 2/Day Each: Suggestion, Invisibility; 1/Day Each: Hold Person, Modify Memory

entries.name: Whispered Encouragement
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the leannan has Charmed within 30 feet. Failure: The creature uses its Reaction to make one weapon attack against a creature of the leannan's choice.

bestiary.name: Silken Leannan
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: Painters, poets, and composers of Vesperine whisper about the leannan: a lover who appears to a struggling artist on the worst night of their life and makes them brilliant. The art is real, and so is the price. The leannan drinks the artist's vitality one masterpiece at a time and moves on when there is nothing left. She is flattering, attentive, and devastatingly sincere, until she isn't.
bestiary.where: Artists' garrets in the Velvet Quarter, the Lanternwood's edge, opera dressing rooms.
bestiary.tactics: The leannan keeps a Charmed devotee at her side as a shield and fights only when cornered. She targets whoever is trying to break the bargain, and she offers to become their muse instead.
hooks: The city's most celebrated young poet looks ten years older every week, and he refuses to give up his mysterious patron.
A leannan asks the party to protect her from a jealous former artist who wants her dead.

entries.name: Courtly Duel
entries.text: When a creature accepts the knight's formal challenge, both have Advantage on attack rolls against each other and Disadvantage against everyone else until one yields or drops. Interfering allies break the knight's oath; it then fights without honor.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The knight makes three Rose Blade attacks.

entries.name: Rose Blade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Gallant Challenge
entries.text: The knight challenges one creature it can see within 60 feet to a Courtly Duel. The creature can accept or refuse (no action required).

entries.name: Parry
entries.text: Trigger: A creature hits the knight with a melee attack roll. Response: The knight adds 3 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

bestiary.name: Thornknight of the Dusk Court
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The Fae Duke's knights wear armor grown from black rose-thorn and helms crowned with blossoms. They are courteous, romantic, and terrifying, and they keep every rule of chivalry to the letter. A thornknight will kiss your hand, compliment your eyes, and then kill you in a fair duel at dawn, weeping beautifully at your funeral.
bestiary.where: The Dusk Court's roads, the Lanternwood at twilight, the Night 7 endgame of *The Black Kiss*.
bestiary.tactics: It issues a challenge to the strongest-looking hero and fights honorably while that duel lasts. If the party gangs up on it, it calls its briar hounds and fights to kill.
hooks: A thornknight has challenged a party member to a duel "for the honor of a smile."
A knight defects from the Dusk Court for love of a mortal, and its former brothers are coming.

entries.name: Antlered Charge
entries.text: If the giant moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with Antler Gore on the same turn, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition if it is Large or smaller.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes two Antler Maul attacks.

entries.name: Antler Maul
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 18 (3d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hurl Log
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Antler Gore
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Elkhorn Giant
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The great antlered giants of the deep Lanternwood are huntsmen of the Fair Folk, oath-bound for centuries to run the Wild Hunt for whichever fey lord holds their horn. Between hunts they are shy, lonely, and fond of mortal songs. They wear antlers as crowns and remember the forest before it glowed.
bestiary.where: The deep Lanternwood, the roads of the Wild Hunt, standing-stone circles.
bestiary.tactics: It charges, gores, and smashes, hurling logs at fliers. A giant whose horn is held by an enemy fights without heart; one whose horn is returned becomes an ally for a season.
hooks: The Wild Hunt is riding tonight, and the giant at its head is weeping as it runs.
A merchant has bought an ancient carved horn at auction; an antlered giant has come to the city to get it back.

lines: Resistances Bludgeoning, Cold, Necrotic, Piercing, Slashing
Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

entries.name: Twilight Form
entries.text: The elemental can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch and through other creatures. Its space is Heavily Obscured. It can't enter bright light; it takes 11 (2d10) Radiant damage if it starts its turn in bright light.

entries.name: Fading Light
entries.text: Bright light within 30 feet of the elemental becomes dim light, and dim light becomes darkness, except light created by spells of 3rd level or higher.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The elemental makes three Dusk Touch attacks.

entries.name: Dusk Touch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 17 (3d8 + 4) Cold damage. If the target is a creature, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Gloaming Elemental
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: The Lanternwood is stuck at twilight because something lives in it: the gloaming, a primordial spirit of the hour between day and night, bound by the Moth Court's oldest bargain. Lesser gloamings drift free at its edges, cold violet mists with stars inside them. They hate dawn and dusk equally, for each one ends them.
bestiary.where: The Lanternwood's heart, the twilight roads to the Dusk Court, deep shadowed valleys.
bestiary.tactics: It snuffs out the party's lights, then surrounds the nearest target with cold. It never pursues into bright light and will bargain for darkness, such as a lantern smashed or a window shuttered.
hooks: The sun has failed to rise over one village for three days, and a violet mist sits on the church spire.
The Moth Court's bargain with the great gloaming is weakening, and its children are escaping.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The seraph has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Dream-Warden
entries.text: The seraph knows when any creature within 1 mile of it is having a nightmare, and can enter that creature's dream as a Bonus Action while it sleeps.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The seraph makes two Moonlit Glaive attacks.

entries.name: Moonlit Glaive
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The dawnmoth seraph casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Light; 2/Day Each: Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration; 1/Day Each: Dispel Evil and Good, Greater Restoration

entries.name: Wings of Morning
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature of the seraph's choice in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the seraph. Failure: The creature has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Undead and Fiends also take 9 (2d8) Radiant damage.

bestiary.name: Dawnmoth Seraph
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: For every dream the Moth Court eats, an old power from the upper heavens sends a guardian to watch over the dreamers. Dawnmoth seraphs are luminous winged celestials with wings like the first light. They stand vigil over the sleeping and fight the Moth Court quietly, in dreams. They are kind but uncompromising, and they think mortals sleep far too little.
bestiary.where: Above sleeping villages, the dreams of the innocent, the edges of the Lanternwood at dawn.
bestiary.tactics: A seraph blinds attackers with its wings, then strikes the most dangerous foe with its glaive. It heals innocents before it pursues enemies, and it never harms a sleeper, even an evil one.
hooks: A seraph appears in a party member's dream to warn that the Moth Court has tasted them.
The Moth Court has trapped a seraph in a cocoon, and its light is dimming the whole forest.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the herald fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The herald has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Voice of the Duke
entries.text: The herald speaks with the Fae Duke's authority. A creature that has made a bargain with any fey of the Dusk Court has Disadvantage on saving throws against the herald's spells.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The herald makes three Thorned Glaive attacks, or it makes two and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Thorned Glaive
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 10 ft. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The herald of the dusk court casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 20): At Will: Charm Person, Detect Thoughts, Misty Step; 2/Day Each: Dominate Person, Geas, Mass Suggestion; 1/Day Each: Plane Shift, Power Word Stun

entries.name: Command the Dance
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 20, up to three creatures within 60 feet that can hear the herald. Failure: The creature has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn and must use its movement to approach the herald, bowing.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the herald of the dusk court can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The herald of the dusk court regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Thorn Lash
entries.text: The herald makes one Thorned Glaive attack.

entries.name: Rose Step
entries.text: The herald teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see, leaving a burst of petals.

entries.name: Decree (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: The herald uses Spellcasting to cast Charm Person or Misty Step, or uses Command the Dance.

bestiary.name: Herald of the Dusk Court
bestiary.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
bestiary.lore: When the Accord fails on Night 7, the Fae Duke of the Dusk will not come himself. He will send his herald: a towering figure crowned in red roses and antlers of black thorn, robed in twilight, with a voice like a love song played at a funeral. The herald reads the Duke's claims aloud and collects every debt, one dance at a time.
bestiary.where: The Dusk Court, the Velvet Opera on Night 7, any place the Fae Duke's claim is pressed.
bestiary.tactics: The herald commands enemies into a bowing dance, then cuts them down. It uses Plane Shift to banish the most dangerous foe to the Dusk Court. It honors bargains exactly, and a clever party can trap it in its own terms.
hooks: At midnight on Night 7, the herald arrives at the Opera Council to read the Duke's claim. Every Anchor in the room tightens.
Prince Caelum begs the party to keep the herald from finding him before he can renounce his father.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The croakling can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Chorus Alarm
entries.text: When a croakling sees a stranger, every croakling within 300 feet falls silent. Creatures familiar with the Thicketmoor know that sudden silence means someone is coming.

entries.name: Sticky Tongue
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 1 Bludgeoning damage, and the croakling steals one small shiny object the target is holding loosely (DC 12 Strength check to keep hold).

bestiary.name: Croakling
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Jewel-bright bog frogs whose chorus fills the Thicketmoor every night. Locals call them the bog's gossips, since a croakling chorus that goes silent has saved more travelers than any watchman. They love shiny things, and an ogress's beauty kit is never quite complete for long.
bestiary.where: Every pond, ditch, and bog-pool in the Thicketmoor.
bestiary.tactics: Croaklings flee from anything bigger than a cat. They steal shiny objects and dive into the nearest pool.
hooks: A croakling swallowed a betrothal ring, and the bride-to-be wants it back before the Courting Moot.
The croaklings near the Sulking Stones have been silent for a week.

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: Bramble Body
entries.text: A creature that grapples the thornling, or hits it with an unarmed strike, takes 2 (1d4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Thorn Jab
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Thornling
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: The giant brambles of the Thicketmoor shed seed-pods that walk. Thornlings are knee-high tangles of briar with a single red berry for an eye. They swarm intruders the way ants swarm a dropped sweet, then plant themselves in the corpse. A field of thornlings is a field that recently ate someone.
bestiary.where: Bramble thickets, the edges of the Sulking Stones, overgrown ruins. Use as minions.
bestiary.tactics: Thornlings attack in groups of six or more and surround a single foe. They are mindless and fight to the last, but a flame of any size makes the whole swarm hesitate.
hooks: A peddler's road is overgrown overnight, and the bramble is walking.
The Honeyhorn Matrons offer a jar of honey per hundred thornlings burned.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The toad can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Standing Leap
entries.text: The toad's long jump is up to 20 feet and its high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start.

entries.name: Courtship Croak
entries.text: During the spring bloom, the toad has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature wearing a ring, flower crown, or veil.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Bludgeoning damage, and if the target is Small or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 11).

bestiary.name: Wedding Toad
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Each spring, the toads of the Thicketmoor process in solemn lines to the breeding pools, and nothing stops a wedding toad's procession. They are big as hounds, warty, and baffled. Bogfolk say a couple who sees a toad procession on their wedding day will be happy, if they survive it.
bestiary.where: Thicketmoor pools and causeways, especially in spring.
bestiary.tactics: A toad attacks anyone blocking its procession route and anything glittering. It flees into water when Bloodied.
hooks: A noble wedding has been planned beside the breeding pools, against all local advice.
A toad swallowed the Honeyhorn Matrons' heirloom wedding veil.

bestiary.meta: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, Unaligned
lines: Immunities Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny leech. It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Numbing Kiss
entries.text: A creature bitten by the swarm doesn't notice it unless it succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

entries.name: Bites
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 0 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Piercing damage, or 3 (1d6) Piercing damage if the swarm is Bloodied, and the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by the same amount until it finishes a Long Rest.

bestiary.name: Bloodbelle Leech Swarm
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: The bloodbelle leech is a rose-pink bog leech whose bite feels like a kiss. Its numbing saliva is prized by the hedge-witches of the moor for painless surgery and for love philters. Wading travelers sometimes emerge from a bog-pool rosy-cheeked, light-headed, and covered in them.
bestiary.where: Still bog-pools, mud spas, flooded peat cuts.
bestiary.tactics: The swarm hides in still water and feeds on anything that wades in. Salt or fire makes it release and retreat.
hooks: A hedge-witch needs a jar of bloodbelle saliva for an anesthetic, and the only colony is in the Sulking Stones' pool.
Couples bathing in a "lovers' spring" keep fainting, smiling, in the water.
bestiary.imm: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

entries.name: Charge
entries.text: If the boar moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with Tusk on the same turn, the target takes an extra 3 (1d6) Piercing damage and has the Prone condition if it is Large or smaller.

entries.name: Relentless (1/Day)
entries.text: If the boar takes 10 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 Hit Points, it is reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

entries.name: Tusk
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Honeyhorn Boar
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Honey-fattened boars the size of ponies, with golden bristles and tusks that the Honeyhorn ogresses polish for festivals. They root for the wasp-honey combs that fall from the giant brambles and are perpetually, aggressively sticky. The Matrons ride them to the Courting Moot.
bestiary.where: The Thicketmoor, Honeyhorn pens, the mud-wallows.
bestiary.tactics: A boar charges the nearest stranger and keeps goring until it is driven off with fire or honey.
hooks: A runaway boar has carried off the Matron's best courting-hat.
The Courting Moot's boar race needs riders, and the prize is a kiss from the winner's choice of ogress.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Unconscious
Languages Understands Common, can speak only in borrowed love poetry

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the swain is indistinguishable from an ordinary scarecrow.

entries.name: Lovelorn
entries.text: The swain won't attack the creature it is courting unless that creature attacks it first.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The swain makes two Clawed Glove attacks.

entries.name: Clawed Glove
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Bashful Gaze
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature the swain can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn and is overcome with pity and fondness for the swain. A creature that is immune to the Charmed condition is immune to this.

bestiary.name: Straw Swain
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Years ago, a lonely hedge-witch stuffed a scarecrow with love letters and wished it would court her. It did, then she died, and it kept courting. Now there are a dozen straw swains in the Thicketmoor, made by witches who should know better. They leave wildflowers on doorsteps, recite stolen poetry, and maul rivals in the cornfield.
bestiary.where: Thicketmoor farms, cornfields, the hedge-witches' cottages.
bestiary.tactics: A swain fights only rivals and anyone who harms its beloved. It flees from fire. Reading it a love letter (DC 12 Performance) ends its hostility for an hour.
hooks: A farmer's daughter has a secret admirer who leaves flowers, and her new fiancé was found torn apart in the barley.
A hedge-witch wants help making a straw swain, and the party is supposed to write the love letters.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Unconscious

lines: Gear Herbalism Kit, Love Philters (2), Quarterstaff

entries.name: Philter-Maker
