entries.text: The apprentice carries two love philters. A creature that drinks one has the Charmed condition toward the first creature it sees for 1 hour (DC 12 Wisdom save negates). The Accord voids any vow sworn while under a philter.

entries.name: Thorn Bolt
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 60 ft. Hit: 9 (2d8) Poison damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The hedge-witch apprentice casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 12): At Will: Druidcraft, Mending; 1/Day Each: Entangle, Cure Wounds, Sleep

bestiary.name: Hedge-Witch Apprentice
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Every cottage in the Thicketmoor has a witch or a witch's apprentice: young herbalists, midwives, and philter-brewers who learned from Auntie Sallowmere or one of her rivals. Most are kind, and some sell love potions that the Lantern Watch has outlawed twice. An apprentice in trouble is usually an apprentice who brewed something stronger than they meant to.
bestiary.where: Thicketmoor cottages, village markets, the edges of the bog.
bestiary.tactics: Apprentices avoid melee, entangle attackers, and pelt them with thorn bolts. They surrender readily, usually with a bargain on their lips.
hooks: An apprentice's love philter is loose at the Courting Moot, and the ogresses are drinking it.
Auntie Sallowmere's apprentice wants to break her mistress's curse on the Sulking Stones.

entries.name: Lovestruck
entries.text: If the suitor's beloved can see it, it has Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and Disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws.

entries.name: Courting Club
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hurl Boulder
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Bellowed Declaration (1/Day)
entries.text: The suitor roars its love to the heavens. Each creature within 30 feet that can hear it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Honeyhorn Suitor
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: The ogre men of Honeyhorn were cursed into standing stones for being too proud to say "I love you." Those freed from the Sulking Stones, and the ogres who wander in hoping to court a Matron, are enormous, sentimental, and painfully earnest. A suitor in love will fight anyone who looks at his sweetheart and weep at a well-sung ballad.
bestiary.where: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, the Courting Moot.
bestiary.tactics: He fights to impress, roaring declarations and smashing the biggest rival in sight. He stops at once if his beloved tells him to, or if someone helps him compose a better love poem.
hooks: A suitor wants the party to ghost-write his love letters to a Matron. Every bad rhyme makes him angrier.
Two suitors are dueling over the same ogress, and the duel is wrecking the village.

lines: Languages Speaks an old dialect of Common

entries.name: Peat-Preserved
entries.text: The sleeper looks freshly asleep, if leathery. It has Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks made to seem harmless.

entries.name: Drowned Promise
entries.text: The sleeper was sunk in the bog for breaking a vow. If the creature it wronged (or that creature's descendant) forgives it aloud, the sleeper has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sleeper makes two Peat Fist attacks.

entries.name: Peat Fist
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Bog Kiss
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature Grappled or Prone within 5 feet. Failure: 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn as its lungs fill with the taste of peat.

bestiary.name: Bog-Kissed Sleeper
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: In the old days, oath-breakers were drowned in the Thicketmoor, staked down with hazel and weighted with stones. The bog keeps them perfectly, brown and supple, their faces calm. When the peat-cutters dig too deep, a sleeper wakes, still wearing the noose or the wedding ring that condemned it, and it goes looking for the one it betrayed.
bestiary.where: Peat cuts, drowned causeways, the deepest pools of the Thicketmoor.
bestiary.tactics: The sleeper ambushes from the water, drags a victim down, and gives it the bog's kiss. It ignores everyone but its target unless attacked.
hooks: Peat-cutters unearthed a perfectly preserved bridegroom, and he's walking toward the village where his betrothed's granddaughter lives.
A sleeper wants to be forgiven, and only the party can find the descendant of the woman he jilted.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The saint has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Purifying Presence
entries.text: Water within 30 feet of the saint becomes clean and drinkable, and creatures that start their turn in it lose the Poisoned condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The saint makes two Lily Lash attacks.

entries.name: Lily Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Healing Touch (3/Day)
entries.text: The saint touches a creature, which regains 17 (3d8 + 4) Hit Points and is cured of one disease or curse of 3rd level or lower.

bestiary.name: Lilywater Saint
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Some of the moor's pools are holy. Pilgrims leave ribbons on the reeds there, and a pale woman crowned in water-lilies rises from the depths to heal the sick. The lilywater saints are celestial guardians of clean water, ancient and gentle. They are the reason the Thicketmoor hasn't swallowed the villages around it. Auntie Sallowmere hates them.
bestiary.where: Holy pools, pilgrim shrines, the clear springs at the moor's edge.
bestiary.tactics: A saint fights only to protect its pool or the innocent. It heals allies first and lashes polluters. If its pool is fouled, it weakens and pleads for help.
hooks: Someone has poured blackened oil into a saint's pool, and the village's children are sick.
A saint asks the party to deliver a healing lily to the Sulking Stones; she believes it can soften Sallowmere's curse.

entries.name: Mud Camouflage
entries.text: The mirecat has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in mud, reeds, or murky water.

entries.name: Pounce
entries.text: If the mirecat moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Claw attack on the same turn, the target has the Prone condition if it fails a DC 14 Strength saving throw, and the mirecat can make one Bite attack against it as a Bonus Action.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The mirecat makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

bestiary.name: Mirecat
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: A great swamp cat with a mud-slick pelt and webbed paws, the mirecat lurks with only its golden eyes above the water. It is the apex hunter of the Thicketmoor: patient, silent, and fond of ogre. The Honeyhorn Matrons wear mirecat-fur stoles to the Courting Moot, and it's said only the bravest suitor can bring one.
bestiary.where: The deep Thicketmoor, reed beds, sluggish rivers.
bestiary.tactics: It stalks from the water, pounces on the straggler, and drags it under. It retreats when Bloodied and comes back the next night.
hooks: A Matron will accept a courtship from anyone who brings her a mirecat pelt.
A mirecat has been taking the hedge-witches' goats, and something is wrong with its eyes.

lines: Senses Darkvision 120 ft., Tremorsense 30 ft.; Passive Perception 11
Languages Telepathy 60 ft. (it uses the voices of the dead)

entries.name: Voice of the Lost
entries.text: The reedwhisper can perfectly mimic the voice of anyone who drowned within a mile of its lair, and it knows enough of their memories to fool their loved ones.

entries.name: Reed Body
entries.text: While motionless in a reed bed, the reedwhisper is indistinguishable from ordinary reeds.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The reedwhisper makes two Reed Lash attacks and uses Drowning Whisper.

entries.name: Reed Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Drowning Whisper
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 60 feet that can hear the reedwhisper. Failure: 9 (2d8) Psychic damage, and the target must use its movement on its next turn to walk toward the deepest water it can see. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Reedwhisper
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Something sleeps beneath the Thicketmoor's reed beds that is not of this world: a tangle of hollow stalks and pale tendrils, with eyes like frog spawn. It learned to speak by listening to the drowned. A reedwhisper calls travelers in the voices of their lost loved ones, and their bodies are never found. The reed beds grow thicker every year.
bestiary.where: Reed beds, flooded causeways, the drowned villages under the moor.
bestiary.tactics: It lures victims with stolen voices, lashes them at the water's edge, and whispers until they walk in. It flees underwater when Bloodied.
hooks: A widow keeps hearing her drowned husband calling from the reeds, and last night she answered.
Sallowmere claims the reedwhisper is the real reason the ogre men were cursed, and she wants it dead.

lines: Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Amorphous
entries.text: The slurry can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Bog Body
entries.text: The ground within 10 feet of the slurry is Difficult Terrain. While motionless in a bog, the slurry is indistinguishable from mud.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The slurry makes two Pseudopod attacks.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Acid damage.

entries.name: Engulf
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 14, one Medium or smaller creature in the slurry's space. Failure: 10 (3d6) Acid damage, and the target is engulfed. It has the Restrained condition, can't breathe, and takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage at the start of each of its turns. It can escape with a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check.

bestiary.name: Peat Slurry
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: The Thicketmoor's peat is old enough to be hungry. A peat slurry is a living mass of black bog mud, roots, and preserved odds and ends: a shoe, a sword-hilt, a wedding crown. It moves at the speed of sinking. Bog-cutters measure their lives by not standing still too long.
bestiary.where: Mud-flats, peat cuts, the Honeyhorn spa, bog roads.
bestiary.tactics: It waits under the surface of a mud-flat, rises beneath the heaviest creature, and engulfs it. It never retreats, but it can't follow anyone onto stone.
hooks: The Honeyhorn mud spa has a new, very warm pool that keeps swallowing bathers.
Bog-cutters found a crown inside a peat slurry and want it fished out.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Gear Greatclub, Honey Pots (3), Courting Fan

entries.name: Matron's Regard
entries.text: The matron has Advantage on Charisma checks against Giants and against any creature that has complimented her today. A creature she has chosen as a "Moot candidate" has Disadvantage on checks to escape her grapple.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The matron makes two Greatclub attacks, or one Greatclub attack and one Scoop Up.

entries.name: Greatclub
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Scoop Up
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 16, one Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet. Failure: The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) and is carried under the matron's arm. While Grappled this way, it has the Restrained condition.

entries.name: Honey Pot
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 20/60 ft. Hit: 8 (1d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage, and the target's Speed is halved until it takes an action to scrape off the honey.

bestiary.name: Honeyhorn Matron
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Six Honeyhorn ogresses have ruled the Thicketmoor for forty years without their menfolk, ever since Auntie Sallowmere cursed the ogre men into the Sulking Stones. They are enormous, theatrical, bawdy, and lonely, and they've started "recruiting" handsome travelers for their Courting Moot. They are not cruel, exactly. They've simply forgotten how to ask.
bestiary.where: The Honeyhorn lodge, the mud spa, the Courting Moot (Side Adventure 1).
bestiary.tactics: A matron scoops up the most attractive target and lumbers off, clubbing pursuers and pelting them with honey. She can be talked down by a candidate who flirts back convincingly (DC 15 Persuasion), or by an offer to help break the curse.
hooks: A Matron has chosen a party member as her Moot candidate, and she's bringing him a dowry of honey.
The Matrons will release their "guests" if the party can make the Sulking Stones say "I love you."

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The crone can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Curse-Keeper
entries.text: The crone always knows the location and condition of any creature she has cursed. Her curses can be ended only by Remove Curse cast at 5th level or higher, or by fulfilling the curse's stated condition.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The crone makes two Bog Claw attacks, or one Bog Claw attack and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Bog Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Poison damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The mire crone casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 14): At Will: Disguise Self, Minor Illusion, Fog Cloud; 2/Day Each: Bestow Curse, Hold Person; 1/Day Each: Polymorph, Scrying

entries.name: Glamour of Youth
entries.text: The crone magically appears as a beautiful young woman until she takes damage or uses Bog Claw. Truesight reveals her true form.

bestiary.name: Mire Crone
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Auntie Sallowmere is the most famous, but she is not the only one. Mire crones are fey of the bog's bitter heart: ancient, clever, and wounded. Each was once spurned or betrayed. Each keeps her curses like pressed flowers, a reminder that no one should ever be too proud to say what they feel. They are villains with a point, which makes them dangerous.
bestiary.where: The heart of the Thicketmoor, crooked huts on stilts, curse-sites like the Sulking Stones.
bestiary.tactics: A crone fights from fog, holding the strongest foe and cursing the proudest. When Bloodied, she bargains, and she always offers to lift a curse in exchange for an honest confession.
hooks: A crone cursed a nobleman to croak like a frog until someone tells him the truth about his marriage.
Sallowmere will lift the Sulking Stones curse if the party can find a man in Vesperine brave enough to say "I love you" first.

lines: Languages Understands Sylvan but speaks only in creaks

entries.name: Siege Monster
entries.text: The lumberer deals double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Overgrowth
entries.text: At the start of each of the lumberer's turns, the ground within 15 feet of it becomes Difficult Terrain until the start of its next turn as roots erupt.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The lumberer makes two Slam attacks.

entries.name: Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 15 ft. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Bramble Hurl
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 60/180 ft. Hit: 27 (4d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage, and the area within 5 feet of the target becomes Difficult Terrain.

bestiary.name: Mossback Lumberer
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Some of the Thicketmoor's mossy hills are asleep. A mossback lumberer is an ancient bog-tree grown around a heart of peat, bearded with moss and crowned with brambles. It wakes when the bog is wounded: drained, burned, or cut for a road. Then it walks to the source of the wound and flattens it. Honeyhorn ogresses sing to them, and lumberers like the songs.
bestiary.where: The deep Thicketmoor, drained bog-margins, ancient groves.
bestiary.tactics: It wades into the largest group, slams, and hurls brambles at anyone fleeing. It ignores small creatures unless they carry fire or axes.
hooks: A baron is draining the bog for farmland, and a mossy hill has begun moving toward his manor.
The Honeyhorn Matrons offer a lumberer's song to anyone who protects their grove.

lines: Languages Abyssal, Common, Infernal, Telepathy 60 ft.

entries.name: Toadstool Throne
entries.text: While the tempter is within 30 feet of a bog-pool, it has Advantage on Charisma checks and on saving throws against the Charmed condition.

entries.name: Wish of the Bog
entries.text: A creature that kisses the tempter willingly can ask it for one thing it lost in the bog (an item, a memory, a love). The tempter returns it, and the creature owes it a true name (see Ledger & Oath).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The tempter makes three Barbed Tongue attacks, or two and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Barbed Tongue
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) Poison damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The bog tempter casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Charm Person, Disguise Self, Fog Cloud; 2/Day Each: Suggestion, Hold Person; 1/Day Each: Dominate Person, Dimension Door

entries.name: Murky Escape
entries.text: Trigger: The tempter takes damage while in water. Response: It teleports to an unoccupied space in water it can see within 30 feet.

bestiary.name: Bog Tempter
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Fiends have always loved bogs. They're full of lost things, and lost things are leverage. A bog tempter appears as a handsome, damp, golden-eyed stranger sitting on a toadstool, offering to find whatever you dropped in the water: a ring, a brother, a reason to live. Its true form is a bloated, beautiful, toad-like fiend in a waistcoat of lily pads, and its tongue is a barbed whip.
bestiary.where: The Thicketmoor's deepest pools, the Sulking Stones, any place where something precious was lost in water.
bestiary.tactics: It bargains first, charms second, and fights only when its deals are refused. It stays near water, teleporting through pools, and abandons any fight it is losing.
hooks: A grieving mother made a bog-kiss bargain to bring back her son, and the son who came home has golden eyes.
The tempter is buying the true names of the Honeyhorn ogre men, one wish at a time.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 22

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The fenwyrm can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the fenwyrm fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Rot-Lord
entries.text: Plants and Oozes within 1 mile of the fenwyrm's lair are its eyes; it knows when any creature enters the bog.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fenwyrm makes one Rending Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Rending Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 15 ft. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Acid damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Rot Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. Failure: 63 (14d8) Acid damage, and the creature has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the elder fenwyrm can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The elder fenwyrm regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Tail Swipe
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 20 ft. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Sink
entries.text: The fenwyrm moves up to half its Speed, and if it ends in water or mud, it has Total Cover until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Bog Call (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Roots and mud erupt in a 20-foot-radius Sphere the fenwyrm can see within 120 feet. Strength Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in the area. Failure: The creature has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Elder Fenwyrm
bestiary.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
bestiary.lore: Under the oldest pool of the Thicketmoor sleeps a dragon the color of rotting lilies, older than the Accord and fouler than the bog. The Elder Fenwyrm has bargained with every crone and tempter of the moor. It knows every secret dropped into the water, and it is very, very patient. Sallowmere claims she keeps it asleep with lullabies. She may be lying.
bestiary.where: The deepest pool of the Thicketmoor, the drowned village beneath it.
bestiary.tactics: It surfaces beneath the party, breathes rot, and sinks again. It fights from the water and uses Bog Call to pin fliers. It bargains with anyone who brings it a secret it doesn't know.
hooks: Sallowmere's lullabies have stopped, and the bog is bubbling.
The Thorn Syndicate wants the fenwyrm's hoard of drowned secrets, starting with the Opera Council's.

entries.name: Mimic
entries.text: The gullwit can mimic simple sounds it has heard, such as a whistle, a ship's bell, or a single shouted word. A creature that hears it can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 12 Wisdom (Insight) check.

entries.name: Beak
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage, and the gullwit steals one item of food or a small loose object.

bestiary.name: Gullwit
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Grey-and-white coastal gulls with black caps and too much intelligence in their eyes. The wreckers of Saltgrave train them to ring false ship's bells and shout "Land!" in the fog, and the gulls have taught the trick to their chicks. They are thieves, liars, and the best early warning on the coast.
bestiary.where: Every pier, cliff, and fishing boat on the Saltgrave Coast.
bestiary.tactics: Gullwits steal and flee. A flock can mob a single target, making it lose concentration (as a distraction) but rarely harming it.
hooks: The party's map was stolen by a gull, and the gull is now on a smuggler's shoulder.
Fishermen swear the gulls are ringing the harbor bell at night.

lines: Gear Hooked Pole, Leather Armor, Storm Lantern

entries.name: Wrecker's Footing
entries.text: The wrecker ignores Difficult Terrain caused by wet rocks, rigging, or debris.

entries.name: Hooked Pole
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 10 ft. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) Piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the wrecker can pull it up to 5 feet closer.

bestiary.name: Wrecker
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Captain Kray's wreckers lure ships onto the Saltgrave rocks with false beacons and stolen siren song, then row out with hooks and lanterns to loot the cargo. Most are desperate fishermen paid in rum and salvage. Few of them have ever killed anyone, though they have watched a great many people drown.
bestiary.where: The Saltgrave cliffs, the Smugglers' Grotto, false beacons. Use as minions.
bestiary.tactics: Wreckers work in gangs of four to eight, hooking enemies off their feet or into the surf. Each flees when Bloodied. A credible offer of pardon makes half of them throw down their poles.
hooks: A wrecker's widow wants revenge on Kray for the husband he left on the rocks.
The wreckers are on strike: they want a bigger share, and they'll help anyone who promises one.

bestiary.meta: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, Unaligned
lines: Immunities Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned
Senses Tremorsense 30 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Spined Carpet
entries.text: The swarm's space is Difficult Terrain. A creature that enters it or starts its turn there takes 2 (1d4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa. It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Spines
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 0 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4) Piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) Poison damage.

bestiary.name: Tidepool Urchin Swarm
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Violet sea-urchins with glowing tips carpet the tide-pools beneath the Saltgrave cliffs. They migrate in slow, spiny swarms, toward warmth and blood. The Drowned Choir uses them as a living moat, and the wreckers have learned to wear thick boots.
bestiary.where: Tide-pools, sea caves, the Smugglers' Grotto's lower stairs.
bestiary.tactics: The swarm creeps over anyone who stands still in a tide-pool. It cannot pursue fast creatures but turns narrow passages into agony.
hooks: The only route into the Choir Lagoon at low tide is a tunnel carpeted with urchins.
An apothecary will pay for urchin roe, a rare aphrodisiac (supposedly).
bestiary.imm: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

lines: Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Transparent
entries.text: In water, the jelly is invisible until it attacks; a creature must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice it.

entries.name: Water Bound
entries.text: Out of water, the jelly has the Incapacitated condition and loses 5 Hit Points at the end of each of its turns.

entries.name: Stinging Tendrils
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 10 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage. If the target is a creature, it has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn; while Poisoned this way it also has the Paralyzed condition if it is in water.

bestiary.name: Salt Jelly
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: A glassy bell of jelly the size of a barrel, trailing stinging threads like lace. Salt jellies drift into the Saltgrave coves in warm months and paralyze swimmers. The Drowned Choir keeps them like pets in its lagoon, which is why sailors who survive the sirens rarely survive the swim home.
bestiary.where: Warm coves, sea caves, the Choir Lagoon.
bestiary.tactics: It drifts in the path of swimmers, stings, and wraps paralyzed prey. It cannot pursue onto land.
hooks: Pearl-divers keep surfacing paralyzed, and one diver never surfaced at all.
A jelly is trapped in a tidal pool with a drowned smuggler's key glinting inside it.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Gear Cutlasses (2), Bosun's Whistle, Studded Leather Armor

entries.name: Whistle Command
entries.text: Allied wreckers within 60 feet that can hear the bosun's whistle have Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that is Prone.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The bosun makes two Cutlass attacks.

entries.name: Cutlass
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Shove Overboard
entries.text: The bosun shoves one creature within 5 feet. Strength Saving Throw: DC 12. Failure: The target is pushed 10 feet or has the Prone condition (bosun's choice).

bestiary.name: Wrecker Bosun
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Every wrecking gang has a bosun: the one who decides which lanterns to light, which survivors to pull from the surf, and which to leave. Bosuns are hard, clever, and loyal to Kray, until Kray stops paying. Several are quietly in love with Bel Okafor, Kray's first mate.
bestiary.where: The Smugglers' Grotto, the Wreckers' Beacon, Kray's warehouse. Elite for wrecker gangs.
bestiary.tactics: The bosun knocks foes prone and blows the whistle so the gang can finish them. If the fight turns, it bargains with information about the grotto.
hooks: A bosun offers to sell out Kray in exchange for passage off the coast.
The bosun's daughter is aboard the next ship due to wreck, and the bosun doesn't know.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The kelpwrack can breathe air and water.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless in water, the kelpwrack is indistinguishable from a raft of floating seaweed.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The kelpwrack makes two Frond attacks.

entries.name: Frond
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 15 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Each turn a creature Grappled by the kelpwrack starts underwater, it can't breathe.

bestiary.name: Kelpwrack
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Great rafts of brown kelp float in the bays of the Saltgrave Coast, and some of them are hunting. A kelpwrack is a carnivorous seaweed colony that wraps swimmers and holds them under, fertilizing itself on the drowned. The wreckers dump bodies near the kelp beds, which keeps the kelpwracks fat and lazy.
bestiary.where: Bays, harbor mouths, the Smugglers' Grotto's sea-door.
bestiary.tactics: It grabs swimmers and drags them down, holding two at once. It retreats from fire.
hooks: A kelpwrack has wrapped itself around a sunken chest of Syndicate gold.
The kelp beds have spread to the harbor, and fishing boats are being dragged under.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The crab can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Sea-Glass Shell
entries.text: The crab's translucent shell is studded with sea-glass and bottle shards worth 2d6 × 10 GP to a glassmaker if harvested intact.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The crab makes two Pincer attacks.

entries.name: Pincer
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). The crab has two pincers, each of which can grapple one target.

bestiary.name: Glasscarapace Crab
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The Saltgrave's great crabs grow their shells from wreck-glass: bottles, portholes, lamp-chimneys, and the lenses of drowned spyglasses. In moonlight a glasscarapace glows like a stained-glass window crawling across the sand. They are territorial, delicious, and very hard to kill with a sword.
bestiary.where: Beaches, tide caves, wreck-strewn shallows.
bestiary.tactics: A crab grabs the nearest creature in each pincer and squeezes until it stops moving, then drags it into the surf.
hooks: A glassmaker in Lanternside wants an intact sea-glass shell for the Opera Council's new window.
A crab has a drowned captain's spyglass grown into its shell, with the lens still working.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The siren can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Stolen Voice
entries.text: While the Pearl Heart is held by an enemy, the siren must use Keening against any creature that the Pearl Heart's holder commands, even her allies, and she weeps while she does it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The siren makes one Claw attack and uses Keening.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Keening
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature of the siren's choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from her that can hear her. Failure: 10 (3d6) Psychic damage, and the creature has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn, during which it must move toward the siren or into the water. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Kiss for Luck (1/Day)
entries.text: The siren kisses a willing creature within 5 feet. It gains a Swim Speed equal to its Speed and can breathe water for 1 hour. Under the Accord, this kiss seals a small promise.

bestiary.name: Choir Siren
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The Drowned Choir are merfolk sirens, sea-green and silver-scaled, who have lived peaceably in the Saltgrave caves for centuries. Since Captain Kray stole the Pearl Heart that holds their voices, they have been forced to sing ships onto the rocks every night. Most of the Choir would kill Kray in a heartbeat. All of them would rather be free.
bestiary.where: The Choir Lagoon, sea caves, the Saltgrave cliffs (Side Adventure 3).
bestiary.tactics: A siren under compulsion stays in the water, keening at anyone the Heart's holder names. A free siren fights with tooth and claw for her sisters and sings for allies instead.
hooks: A chained siren whispers to the party between songs and begs them to steal the Pearl Heart.
Quill-Fin, a young siren, dares the party to kiss her for luck, then offers to guide them through the underwater ways.

entries.name: Water Breathing
entries.text: The eel can breathe only underwater.

entries.name: Silver Glow
entries.text: The eel sheds dim light in a 30-foot radius. Creatures that see it underwater for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 20 (3d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Electric Coil
entries.text: One creature within 5 feet of the eel that is in the same water takes 5 (1d10) Lightning damage.

bestiary.name: Moon Eel
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Silver-white eels as long as a fishing boat rise to the surface on full-moon nights to feed. Their skin glows softly, and their coils crackle with lightning. Sailors call them the moon's hounds. A moon eel in the harbor means the tide will be strange, and nobody should swim.
bestiary.where: Deep coves, moonlit harbors, sunken wrecks.
bestiary.tactics: It bites from below, coils and shocks, and retreats into deep water if Bloodied.
hooks: A moon eel has nested in the wreck of the *Maris Grace*, where Kray hid his strongroom's spare key.
Moon-eel skin makes the best diving suits on the coast, and the Choir considers the eels sacred.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The lanternmaw can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Lure-Light
entries.text: The lanternmaw's glowing lure can take the appearance of a lantern, a lighthouse beam, or a candle in a window. A creature that sees it and fails a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw believes it is what it appears to be.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The lanternmaw makes one Bite attack and one Lure Lash attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14).

entries.name: Lure Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 15 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage, and the lanternmaw pulls the target up to 10 feet toward it.

bestiary.name: Lanternmaw
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The anglerfish of the deep Saltgrave grow to monstrous size near the wrecks, where the false beacons have taught them a trick. A lanternmaw lurks in sea caves and harbor shallows, dangling a lure that looks like a lantern in a window. Lost sailors swim toward it and find the open mouth.
bestiary.where: Deep sea caves, wreck-holes, harbor depths at night.
bestiary.tactics: It hides in darkness, lures prey close, and bites. If Bloodied, it douses its light and retreats into the deep.
hooks: Smugglers swear a "ghost light" is leading their boats into a sea cave, and boats keep vanishing.
A lanternmaw's lure is said to be a perfect lighthouse lamp, if anyone can cut it free.

entries.name: Drowning Debt
entries.text: The fiend knows the name of every sailor who promised "anything" to survive a storm, and it can track any of them across the sea.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The fiend can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fiend makes two Hooked Claw attacks.

entries.name: Hooked Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) Cold damage.

entries.name: Call in the Debt (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 12, one creature within 30 feet that owes the fiend a debt. Failure: 18 (4d8) Necrotic damage, and the target's lungs fill with seawater. It can't breathe until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Bilge Fiend
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Every sailor in a storm has prayed, "Get me home and I'll give you anything." Bilge fiends answer. They are hunched, barnacled devils with ledger-books of soaked parchment, and they come aboard after the storm to collect. They are scrupulously polite and always willing to renegotiate, at interest.
bestiary.where: Ship holds, wrecks, storm-wracked harbors.
bestiary.tactics: A fiend corners its debtor, calls in the debt, and claws anyone who interferes. It flees into the water when Bloodied, and it is back next week.
hooks: A grizzled captain asks the party to protect him tonight. He made a storm-promise forty years ago.
A bilge fiend offers to cancel Captain Kray's debts if the party will deliver Kray's soul.

entries.name: Waiting at the Pier
entries.text: The bride is bound to the place she drowned. If the person who broke her betrothal promise (or someone who honestly takes on that promise) marries her in a mock ceremony at moonrise, she is laid to rest.

entries.name: Sodden Veil
entries.text: Creatures within 10 feet of the bride smell salt, roses, and rot, and have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The bride makes two Drowning Caress attacks, or uses Kiss of the Deep.

entries.name: Drowning Caress
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Kiss of the Deep
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature the bride has Charmed or Grappled within 5 feet. Failure: 22 (4d10) Cold damage, and the target's lungs fill with seawater; it can't breathe until it takes an action to cough the water out. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Veil Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Cold damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14).

entries.name: Lovelorn Beckon
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature within 30 feet that can see the bride. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn and must move toward the bride by the shortest route.

bestiary.name: Drowned Bride
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: She waits at the end of the pier in a sea-rotted wedding gown, her veil dripping, her bouquet of dead roses held in both hands. Every coast has its drowned bride: a woman who threw herself into the sea, or was pushed, on the eve of a wedding that never came. She is lonely and beautiful in moonlight. She wants to be kissed, and her kiss is the sea.
bestiary.where: Piers, cliffs, beaches where lovers meet, the Saltgrave Coast.
bestiary.tactics: She beckons the most attractive stranger, lashes them close with her veil, and kisses them under. She ignores anyone holding a wedding ring until she has heard their story.
hooks: A drowned bride appears every night at the end of Saltgrave pier, and this week she spoke a living groom's name.
The bride's betrothed is still alive, an old man in Vesperine who never stopped regretting it.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Languages Understands Aquan but can't speak

entries.name: Living Reef
entries.text: The sentinel regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns while it is in salt water and has at least 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Song-Bound
entries.text: The sentinel obeys whoever sings the Drowned Choir's warden-song correctly (DC 15 Charisma (Performance) check, or a Choir siren's word).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sentinel makes two Coral Fist attacks.

entries.name: Coral Fist
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Reef Wall
entries.text: Trigger: An ally within 5 feet of the sentinel is hit by an attack roll. Response: The sentinel adds 4 to the ally's AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

bestiary.name: Coral Sentinel
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The Drowned Choir grew guardians from living coral long ago, giants of pink and white reef with sea-fans for crests. They stand motionless in the Choir Lagoon for decades at a time. Since Kray stole the Pearl Heart, he has learned enough of the warden-song to command two of them. The sentinels hate him in their slow, stony way.
bestiary.where: The Choir Lagoon, Kray's strongroom, drowned temples.
bestiary.tactics: A sentinel guards its post, punches anything that approaches, and shields its allies. It fights in water whenever it can.
hooks: The coral sentinels guarding Kray's strongroom will obey anyone who learns the warden-song.
A sentinel has walked out of the sea and up the beach, looking for the Pearl Heart.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The warden has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Beacon
entries.text: The warden sheds bright light in a 60-foot radius. Ships within 5 miles that can see the light can't be lured off course by false beacons or siren song.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The warden makes two Beacon Mace attacks.

entries.name: Beacon Mace
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 13 (3d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Searching Beam
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 18 (4d8) Radiant damage, and the creature has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Lamplight Warden
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The old lighthouse at Saltgrave Point was blessed by a sea-saint, and its keeper never quite died. Lamplight wardens are celestials bound to lighthouses, tall and grave with lanterns for hearts, who keep the light lit in every storm. Kray's false beacons are an insult to their oath, and the wreckers fear them more than the Watch.
bestiary.where: Lighthouses, cliff shrines, harbor chapels.
bestiary.tactics: A warden blinds wreckers with its beam and drives them from the cliffs. It never pursues into the sea, and it begs anyone it meets to relight a lighthouse that has gone dark.
hooks: The Saltgrave Point lighthouse has gone dark, and its warden has been chained in its own lantern-room.
A warden asks the party to put out Kray's false beacon, then light its true lamp before the next storm.

lines: Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

entries.name: Water Form
entries.text: The elemental can enter an enemy's space and stop there, and it can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Freeze
entries.text: If the elemental takes Cold damage, its Speed is reduced by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The elemental makes two Slam attacks.

entries.name: Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Whelm (Recharge 4–6)
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 16, each creature in the elemental's space. Failure: 23 (4d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage, and the creature is pulled into the elemental. It has the Restrained condition and can't breathe until it escapes (DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check). Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Undertow Elemental
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The current that drags swimmers out past the breakers has a will of its own. Undertow elementals are huge, slow-witted spirits of the sea's pull. They are usually content to roll pebbles and sink boats that anchor in the wrong place. The stolen siren song of the Drowned Choir has stirred them, and they are rising into the shallows for the first time in centuries.
bestiary.where: Breakers, harbor mouths, sea caves, storm surges.
bestiary.tactics: It rolls over the largest group, whelms them, and drags them into deeper water. It cannot leave the sea for more than a minute.
hooks: The tide has stopped going out at Saltgrave, and the harbor is drowning one dock at a time.
An elemental is guarding the wreck of the ship that carried the Pearl Heart's original casket.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 14

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The drake can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Storm-Rider
entries.text: The drake has Advantage on Dexterity saving throws and attack rolls while flying in a storm.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Lightning Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 90-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Failure: 44 (8d10) Lightning damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Spindrift Drake
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Slate-blue sea-dragons with wings like stormsails ride the gales that pound the Saltgrave cliffs. Spindrift drakes nest on offshore rocks, fish for sharks, and hoard ships' figureheads, which they arrange in admiring circles. They are vain, playful, and quick to anger. A drake that adopts a ship as its own will escort it through any storm.
bestiary.where: Offshore rocks, storm skies, the open sea off Saltgrave.
bestiary.tactics: It dives out of the storm, breathes lightning down the deck, and claws its way along the rigging. It flees when Bloodied, unless its hoard is threatened.
hooks: A spindrift drake has taken a fancy to the party's ship's figurehead, and it's following them.
Kray's wreckers have been stealing the drake's figureheads, and the drake blames the Choir.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The giant can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Siege Monster
entries.text: The giant deals double damage to objects and structures, including ships.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes two Anchor attacks.

entries.name: Anchor
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 15 ft. Hit: 23 (3d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it has the Prone condition.

entries.name: Hurl Wreckage
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +11, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 29 (4d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Tide Stomp
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +11, reach 5 ft. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

bestiary.name: Breakwater Giant
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: Some of Saltgrave's sea-stacks have faces. Breakwater giants are enormous barnacle-crusted folk who sleep in the surf, waking every few decades to rebuild the reefs and drown anyone who has disturbed them. They swing the anchors of ships they have sunk. Old sailors leave gifts of rope and ale on the rocks to keep them sleeping.
bestiary.where: Sea-stacks, reefs, harbor mouths.
bestiary.tactics: It wades out of the surf, smashes boats and docks, and hurls wreckage at anyone on the cliffs. It accepts a gift and a sincere apology for any wrong done to the sea.
hooks: Kray's beacon fire woke a breakwater giant, and it is wading toward the Smugglers' Grotto.
A giant's anchor is the last piece of a famous treasure ship, and the Syndicate wants it.

lines: Languages Understands all languages but can't speak; Telepathy 1 mile

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the Silence fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Devourer of Voices
entries.text: No sound exists within 60 feet of the Silence. Creatures in that area have the Deafened condition and can't cast spells with Verbal components. A creature whose voice the Silence has eaten (see Swallow Song) remains mute until the Silence dies.

entries.name: Water Breathing
entries.text: The Silence can breathe only underwater.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Silence makes three Tentacle attacks.

entries.name: Tentacle
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 30 ft. Hit: 19 (3d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage. If the target is Huge or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 18).

entries.name: Swallow Song (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 18, each creature in a 120-foot Emanation originating from the Silence. Failure: 55 (10d10) Psychic damage, and the creature's voice is eaten (see Devourer of Voices). Success: Half damage only.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the Silence Below can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The Silence Below regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Lash
entries.text: The Silence makes one Tentacle attack, dealing only the Bludgeoning damage (19 (3d8 + 6)).

entries.name: Undertow
entries.text: Each creature Grappled by the Silence is pulled up to 30 feet toward it.

entries.name: Stillness (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 19, one creature within 120 feet. Failure: The target has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn as an absolute silence fills its mind.

bestiary.name: The Silence Below
bestiary.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
bestiary.lore: The Drowned Choir sings for a reason older than their peace with the land: to keep something asleep. Far below the Choir Lagoon, in a trench no light has touched, lies a vast pale thing of tentacles and eyes that feeds on sound. With the Choir enslaved and singing ships to ruin instead of lullabies, the Silence Below is waking up, and the first sign is that the waves have stopped making noise.
bestiary.where: The trench beneath the Choir Lagoon, the climax of *The Song Beneath Saltgrave* at higher levels.
bestiary.tactics: It rises in absolute silence, eats the party's voices, and drags them down one by one. Restoring the Choir's true song (with the Pearl Heart) gives everyone Advantage against it and forces it to retreat if Bloodied.
hooks: The surf at Saltgrave has gone silent, and fishermen are coming home mute.
Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa reveals the Choir's true purpose and begs the party to return the Pearl Heart before the Silence wakes.

entries.name: Tipsy
entries.text: The rat has Disadvantage on Dexterity checks but Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition.

entries.name: Cellar Nose
entries.text: The rat can smell fresh blood and spilled wine within 300 feet, and it always knows the way out of a cellar.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Wine Rat
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: The cellars of Château Dusk run with fat, wine-drunk rats that nibble the corks and drink the drips. They are tame enough to eat from a hand and too fuddled to run. Servants say that if the wine rats ever leave a cellar, something worse has moved in.
bestiary.where: Wine cellars, taverns, the barrel labyrinths of the Duskvine.
bestiary.tactics: Wine rats flee from anything that moves quickly. Following a rat leads to the nearest exit or the freshest blood.
hooks: The rats have abandoned the deep cellars of a vineyard all at once.
A rat stumbles out of a wall with a sealed love letter stuck to its tail.

entries.name: Enthralled
entries.text: The servant has the Charmed condition toward its master and can't be Charmed by anyone else. It repeats a DC 12 Wisdom save whenever it witnesses its master harm an innocent, ending the condition on a success. A thrall can't consent to anything while enthralled; the Accord voids any oath it swears.

entries.name: Pallid
entries.text: The servant has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws and on any check made in sunlight.

entries.name: Carving Knife
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +2, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Slashing damage.

bestiary.name: Thrall Servant
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Lucan Vey's thralls are villagers taken from the lower terraces, bitten often enough to obey and not often enough to turn. They pour the wine at the Harvest Masquerade with glassy eyes and fresh bandages at their wrists. They are victims, not villains, and every one of them can be freed.
bestiary.where: Château Dusk, the Harvest Masquerade, any noble house of the night. Use as minions, and encourage saving them.
bestiary.tactics: Thralls interpose themselves between their master and danger and fight clumsily. A thrall freed from its charm usually collapses in tears and then helps.
hooks: A thrall slips the party a note in a napkin: Help us. The cellar chapel.
A family in the village begs the party to find their daughter, who went to work at the château and stopped writing home.

bestiary.meta: Medium Swarm of Tiny Beasts, Unaligned
lines: Immunities Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny bat. It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Grape-Lovers
entries.text: The swarm prefers ripe grapes to blood, and it ignores any creature that throws it a bunch of grapes for 1 minute.

entries.name: Bites
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 0 ft. Hit: 5 (2d4) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Vintner's Bat Swarm
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Fruit bats roost by the thousand in the château towers and descend on the vineyards at dusk. Most eat grapes. Those that have tasted something richer at the masquerade come back for more, and their bites leave small, itching, crescent-shaped marks that the guests find rather fashionable.
bestiary.where: Château towers, vineyards at dusk, the barrel labyrinth.
bestiary.tactics: The swarm smothers lights and harries anyone who runs. Grapes or bright light disperse it.
hooks: The vineyard's harvest is being stripped overnight, and the bats are getting bolder.
A swarm keeps circling one guest's balcony, and she says she likes it.
bestiary.imm: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

entries.name: Blood Scent
entries.text: The hound has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks to find a creature that is Bloodied.

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries.text: While in sunlight, the hound has Disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic damage.

bestiary.name: Gravehound
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: House Dusk bred its hunting dogs on the leavings of the masquerade for three centuries, and now the dogs are something else: hairless, grey, red-eyed, and quiet. Gravehounds track runaways through the vineyards by the scent of blood. Lucan Vey keeps a pack in the crypt-chapel.
bestiary.where: The Duskvine's vineyards at night, Château Dusk's kennels, the crypt-chapel.
bestiary.tactics: They hunt in packs of three or four and go for the Bloodied. They won't follow into sunlight or across running water.
hooks: Escaped thralls are being run down in the vineyards at night.
Marta Ilic's son's dog came home a gravehound, and it still knows his scent.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries.text: The fledgling can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without making an ability check.

entries.name: Sun-Scorned
entries.text: While in sunlight, the fledgling has Disadvantage on attack rolls and takes 7 (2d6) Radiant damage at the start of each of its turns. It can't regain Hit Points in sunlight.

entries.name: Invited Only
entries.text: The fledgling can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of its occupants.

entries.name: Fresh Regret
entries.text: A fledgling turned within the last month still remembers its name. Calling it by name (DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check) makes it hesitate, and it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fledgling makes one Claw attack and one Bite attack.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage, and the fledgling regains Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

bestiary.name: Dusk Fledgling
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Lucan Vey's secret army is made of stolen villagers turned too fast and fed too little. Dusk fledglings are feral, starving, and confused. They wear the clothes they were taken in and sometimes call out for family. Countess Morwenna would destroy them out of pity. Lucan keeps them in cages until he needs them.
bestiary.where: The crypt-chapel beneath Château Dusk, the barrel labyrinth, abandoned farmhouses in the valley.
bestiary.tactics: Fledglings swarm from the ceilings and go for the throat. They flee light and hesitate when called by their names.
hooks: Among the fledglings in the crypt-chapel is Marta Ilic's son, turned only a week ago.
A fledgling escaped to the village and is hiding in its family's cellar. They're feeding it.

lines: Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Amorphous
entries.text: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Intoxicating Fumes
entries.text: A creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of the ooze must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) Acid damage.

bestiary.name: Lees Ooze
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: The dregs at the bottom of a thousand-year-old cask are not dead, merely waiting. A lees ooze is a slow, purple-black mass of sediment and spent yeast that seethes in the deepest barrels of the Duskvine. It smells of very good wine and very bad decisions.
bestiary.where: Barrel labyrinths, wine cellars, abandoned wineries.
bestiary.tactics: It oozes out of a cask's bung hole as someone passes, fumes them dizzy, and digests them. It is slow and can be outrun easily.
hooks: A cellarman fell into a cask of the '87 and has not come out.
The countess's sommelier wants a sample of a lees ooze, which he insists is the secret to the Crimson Vintage.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the sanguivine is indistinguishable from an ordinary grapevine heavy with dark red fruit.

entries.name: Blood-Ripened
entries.text: Grapes picked from a sanguivine that has fed in the past day heal 2 (1d4) Hit Points when eaten, and taste faintly of iron.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sanguivine makes two Vine Lash attacks.

entries.name: Vine Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 15 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13).

entries.name: Drink
entries.text: Each creature Grappled by the sanguivine takes 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage, and the sanguivine regains Hit Points equal to the total.

bestiary.name: Sanguivine
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: The oldest vines of the Duskvine were watered with something other than rain. A sanguivine is a great gnarled grapevine whose roots have learned to drink blood, and whose grapes are fat, dark, and delicious. The Crimson Vintage is rumored to come from a single sanguivine in the countess's private walled garden. The rumor is true.
bestiary.where: Old vineyards, walled gardens, the terraces above Château Dusk.
bestiary.tactics: It waits until a picker reaches for its fruit, grapples, and drinks. It cannot move far, so retreating out of reach is always an option.
hooks: Pickers on the high terrace are being found pale and dead among the grapes.
The countess's sanguivine has spread beyond her walled garden.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the lurker is indistinguishable from an enormous wine cask.

entries.name: Adhesive Staves
entries.text: A creature that touches the lurker has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13). Ability checks to escape this grapple have Disadvantage.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The lurker makes one Bite attack and one Stave Slam attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Stave Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

bestiary.name: Cask Lurker
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Shape-shifting ambushers have always loved wine cellars: dark, quiet, and full of people reaching for things. A cask lurker mimics a great oak barrel down to the chalk marks, and it smells convincingly of oak. When a cellarman sets down his candle to tap it, the barrel opens a mouth full of staves.
bestiary.where: Wine cellars, warehouses, the barrel labyrinth.
bestiary.tactics: It waits, sticks fast to the first creature that touches it, and bites. It can't chase anyone, so it fights only what it catches.
hooks: The barrel labyrinth's map is wrong because some of the barrels move.
A lurker has swallowed the key to the Vintage Vault.

lines: Gear Brigandine, Hand Crossbow, Hawthorn Stakes, Holy Water (2), Sunlamp

entries.name: Hunter's Oath
entries.text: The hunter has Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions caused by Undead.

entries.name: Sunlamp
entries.text: As a Bonus Action, the hunter can unshutter its sunlamp, casting sunlight in a 15-foot Cone until the start of its next turn (1/Day).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The hunter makes two Hawthorn Stake attacks, or two Hand Crossbow attacks.

entries.name: Hawthorn Stake
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Hand Crossbow
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +5, range 30/120 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Duskvine Hunter
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Not all of the Duskvine's villagers are frightened. Some are angry. The hunters are farmers, priests, and widows who learned the old ways from their grandparents: hawthorn, garlic, holy water, and patience. They are brave and fair, and they are about to storm Château Dusk with torches over crimes the countess didn't commit.
bestiary.where: Duskvine villages, chapels, the vineyard roads at night.
bestiary.tactics: Hunters work in threes, opening sunlamps on the undead while the others stake. They negotiate with the living and surrender to no one dead.
hooks: A mob of hunters is marching on the château, and the party has until midnight to prove Lucan is the culprit.
A hunter wants the party to help her find her husband's grave, which was opened from the inside.

lines: Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Unconscious

entries.name: Intoxicating Aura
entries.text: Creatures that start their turn within 10 feet of the elemental must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition until the start of their next turn.

entries.name: Bubbling Form
entries.text: The elemental can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The elemental makes two Slosh attacks.

entries.name: Slosh
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Fizz (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the elemental. Failure: 18 (4d8) Poison damage, and the creature has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Ferment Elemental
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: When a vat of must ferments in a cellar touched by elemental magic, the bubbles sometimes stand up. A ferment elemental is a reeling, singing column of purple wine and froth. It is drunk on itself and in love with everyone. It wants to party. Unfortunately, its idea of a party is drowning the guests.
bestiary.where: Pressing rooms, fermentation halls, festival cellars.
bestiary.tactics: It sloshes into crowds, fizzes, and topples revelers. Sealing it in a cask (DC 15 Strength check while it is Bloodied) ends the fight with a very expensive vintage.
hooks: The pressing room has flooded with a dancing purple elemental that keeps hugging the servants.
A vintner wants an elemental captured alive for "a very special bottling."
bestiary.imm: Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Unconscious

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 10
Languages Understands the commands of its maker but can't speak

entries.name: Slick Floor
entries.text: The ground within 15 feet of the juggernaut is slick with grape must and is Difficult Terrain.

entries.name: Commanded
entries.text: The juggernaut obeys whoever holds its iron key. Lucan Vey holds it now.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The juggernaut makes two Press Slam attacks, or one Press Slam attack and uses Crush.

entries.name: Press Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Crush
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 15, one Prone or Grappled creature within 5 feet. Failure: 22 (4d10) Bludgeoning damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Press Juggernaut
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Château Dusk's great grape-press is older than the château: an enchanted engine of oak beams, iron screws, and stained stone. Lucan animated it to guard the cellar stair. It walks on squealing timbers and smells of crushed fruit. It is not malicious. It simply presses whatever it's told.
bestiary.where: The pressing room of Château Dusk, old wineries, the Duskvine harvest festival.
bestiary.tactics: It blocks the stair, slams intruders down on the slick floor, and crushes them. It stops at once if its key is taken from Lucan.
hooks: The pressing room is the only way to the cellars, and the press is awake.
A vintner wants the juggernaut decommissioned without damaging a single beam. It's a historic press.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Languages Common, Elvish, and the languages of three dead empires

entries.name: Invited Only
entries.text: The courtesan can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of its occupants.

entries.name: Sun-Scorned
entries.text: The courtesan takes 14 (4d6) Radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight, and it can't regain Hit Points while in sunlight.

entries.name: Velvet Dark
entries.text: The courtesan has Advantage on Charisma checks made in candlelight or darkness.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The courtesan makes one Claw attack and one Bite attack, or uses Enthralling Gaze and makes one Claw attack.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) Piercing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage. The courtesan regains Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. It can bite only a creature that is willing, Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained.

entries.name: Enthralling Gaze
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature the courtesan can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition for 1 hour, or until it takes damage. While Charmed, it regards the courtesan as a trusted friend and will not harm it. A creature that succeeds is immune to this courtesan's Gaze for 24 hours. A Charmed creature can't consent; the Accord voids any bargain it makes.

entries.name: Mist Step
entries.text: The courtesan teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see in dim light or darkness.

bestiary.name: Crimson Courtesan
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Not every noble of the night is civilized. Crimson courtesans are rogue members of House Dusk who reject the countess's rule of willing donors. They are ravishing, cultured, and predatory. They glide through masquerades in silk, choose a guest, enchant them with a glance, and lead them away to a private room. The victim wakes days later, pale, in love, and missing a week.
bestiary.where: The Harvest Masquerade, Vesperine's late-night salons, private boxes at the Velvet Opera.
bestiary.tactics: It enthralls a guard or lover to protect it, bites only the helpless, and mist-steps away from anyone holding a holy symbol. Countess Morwenna will gladly help destroy a courtesan if asked.
hooks: A charismatic stranger has been visiting the same young noble every night for a week, and she won't let anyone open the curtains.
The countess offers a bounty for a courtesan who has been hunting at her masquerade, against every rule of her house.

entries.name: Harvest Strength
entries.text: The giant can carry a full wine cask (or a Medium creature) under each arm without slowing down.

entries.name: Grape-Stained
entries.text: The giant has Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against anyone who has drunk Duskvine wine in the last day; it can smell what they're feeling.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes two Barrel Club attacks.

entries.name: Barrel Club
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (3d6 + 5) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hurl Cask
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +8, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 21 (3d10 + 5) Bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 5 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition in the spray of wine.

bestiary.name: Vintner Giant
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: House Dusk did not plant the Duskvine. The vintner giants did, three thousand years ago, and they still tend the highest terraces where no mortal can climb. They are slow-spoken, grape-stained, and deeply fond of the valley's people. They have watched the villagers vanish with growing anger, and they have begun to suspect the château.
bestiary.where: The high terraces of the Duskvine, giant-sized wine cellars carved into the hills.
bestiary.tactics: A giant fights only to protect its vines or the valley's people, clubbing hard and hurling casks. It can be reasoned with, especially over a good bottle.
hooks: A vintner giant has blocked the château road and will let no one pass until someone explains the missing villagers.
The giants' oldest vine is withering, and they believe House Dusk poisoned it.

entries.name: Endless Thirst
entries.text: The fiend has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that is Bloodied.

entries.name: Parching Presence
entries.text: Liquids within 30 feet of the fiend begin to evaporate. A creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the fiend gains 1 Exhaustion level unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw (once per creature per day).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fiend makes three Parched Claw attacks.

entries.name: Parched Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Drain the Glass
entries.text: The fiend drinks a potion, a flask of wine, or a vial of blood within 5 feet and regains 16 (3d10) Hit Points.

bestiary.name: Thirstfiend
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Some of the Duskvine's oldest bargains were made with things from the dry hells. A thirstfiend is a gaunt, cracked, wine-dark demon summoned to sate a hunger, and it never stops being thirsty. It drinks wine, blood, tears, and sweat. A vineyard it haunts withers in a season. Lucan Vey is rumored to have summoned one to cover his tracks.
bestiary.where: Withered vineyards, the crypt-chapel, dry wells.
bestiary.tactics: It rushes the weakest-looking enemy, claws until it is Bloodied, then drinks. It flees nothing and hates holy water above all things.
hooks: A vineyard has withered overnight, and the vintner's whole family is found dried like raisins.
Lucan has bound a thirstfiend to guard his coffin, and its leash is weakening.

lines: Senses Darkvision 120 ft., Tremorsense 60 ft.; Passive Perception 12

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: The horror can breathe air and liquid.

entries.name: Vintage Dreams
entries.text: A creature that has drunk wine from a cask the horror inhabited is plagued by dreams of drowning in red, and the horror can communicate with it telepathically at any distance.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The horror makes three Tendril attacks.

entries.name: Tendril
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 15 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15) if it is Large or smaller.

entries.name: Silt Cloud (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: The horror exhales a cloud of red sediment in a 20-foot Emanation. The area is Heavily Obscured until the end of the horror's next turn, and each creature in it has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw.

bestiary.name: Sediment Horror
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: In the deepest cellar of Château Dusk is a cask no one has opened in four centuries. Something lives in the dregs: a mass of red tendrils and lidless eyes that came up from below the valley when the first cellars were dug. It feeds on dreams of those who drink from its barrel, and it has dreamed its way into half the valley.
bestiary.where: The deep cellars of Château Dusk, flooded crypts, ancient wine vats.
bestiary.tactics: It fights from its vat, grappling victims with tendrils and pulling them into the wine. It fills the cellar with silt and retreats into deeper liquid when Bloodied.
hooks: Everyone who drank the château's "special reserve" is dreaming the same dream of a red cellar.
The countess asks the party to seal the oldest cask forever. She will not say what she saw inside it.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The penitent has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Sunbound
entries.text: The penitent sheds sunlight in a 15-foot radius and dim light for a further 15 feet. It can suppress this light as a Bonus Action.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The penitent makes two Sunblade attacks.

entries.name: Sunblade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The dawnwarden penitent casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Light; 1/Day Each: Daylight, Dispel Evil and Good, Zone of Truth

entries.name: Judgment
entries.text: Trigger: An Undead within 30 feet of the penitent regains Hit Points. Response: The Undead takes 13 (3d8) Radiant damage.

bestiary.name: Dawnwarden Penitent
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: Long ago, a sun-angel fell in love with a noble of the night, and she failed to destroy him when she had the chance. Her penance is to hunt his kind forever. Dawnwarden penitents are celestials in scorched plate with sunlight leaking through the seams. They are utterly certain, and they draw no distinction between the countess, who feeds on willing donors, and Lucan, who does not.
bestiary.where: The Duskvine Valley, Vesperine's temples, wherever House Dusk has gone too far.
bestiary.tactics: It strikes the oldest Undead first and lights the room with Daylight. It fights mortals only if they defend the Undead, and it can be persuaded (DC 18) that a civilized monster deserves a trial.
