hooks: A penitent has arrived in the Duskvine to burn Château Dusk, and the party knows the countess is innocent of the disappearances.
Sir Valentin Dusk asks the party to plead his case to a penitent who has him cornered.

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 15

entries.name: Connoisseur
entries.text: The drake can identify the vintage, origin, and any poison in a liquid by smell alone, and it can taste a creature's emotions in its blood.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Wine-Dark Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 17, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 40 (9d8) Necrotic damage, and the creature has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn, reeling as if very drunk. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Claret Drake
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: A wine-red dragon with scales like old stained glass and breath that smells of sweet rot, the claret drake is a gourmand among wyrms. It hoards vintages, not gold, and drinks the best of every harvest from the valley's vineyards as tribute. Lately it has also acquired a taste for the Crimson Vintage, and it wants the countess's sanguivine for itself.
bestiary.where: A cavern-cellar above the Duskvine, the château's rooftops, the high vineyard terraces.
bestiary.tactics: It breathes from the air, then lands to bite and rend whoever smells most interesting. It retreats to its cellar-lair when Bloodied, and it negotiates for tribute of rare wine.
hooks: The drake demands the Duskvine's entire harvest as tribute this year, and the château has agreed.
Lucan offers the drake the countess's sanguivine in exchange for its help on Night 7.

lines: Skills Deception +13, Insight +9, Perception +9, Persuasion +19, Stealth +11
Senses Darkvision 120 ft., Truesight 30 ft.; Passive Perception 19
Languages All languages spoken in Carnelia in the last thousand years

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the patriarch fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Sun-Scorned
entries.text: The patriarch takes 21 (6d6) Radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight and has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks there.

entries.name: Undying Lineage
entries.text: If the patriarch drops to 0 Hit Points outside its coffin, it becomes a cloud of red mist and returns to its coffin within 2 hours, where it regains 1 Hit Point after 1 hour. A hawthorn stake through its heart while it rests in its coffin destroys it.

entries.name: Invited Only
entries.text: The patriarch can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of its occupants.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The patriarch makes two Claw attacks and one Bite attack. It can replace any attack with a use of Blood Command.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) Piercing damage plus 17 (5d6) Necrotic damage, and the patriarch regains Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

entries.name: Blood Command
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 21, one creature within 60 feet that the patriarch can see. Failure: The target has the Charmed condition until the end of its next turn and uses its next action to attack a creature the patriarch chooses. A Charmed creature can't consent; the Accord voids any oath it swears under this command.

entries.name: Blood Tide (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 19, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the patriarch. Failure: 54 (12d8) Necrotic damage. Success: Half damage.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the crimson patriarch can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The crimson patriarch regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Rake
entries.text: The patriarch makes one Claw attack.

entries.name: Red Mist Step
entries.text: The patriarch becomes red mist and moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, then reforms.

entries.name: Feast (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: The patriarch makes one Bite attack.

bestiary.name: Crimson Patriarch
bestiary.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
bestiary.lore: House Dusk was founded by a single ancient noble who has slept in the deepest crypt of the Duskvine for two hundred years: Morwenna's maker, the Crimson Patriarch. He ruled the valley as a tyrant until she put him to rest with a goblet of drugged vintage and a sealed door. Lucan Vey has found the door. If the Patriarch wakes, the rule of willing donors ends, and so do the villages.
bestiary.where: The Sealed Crypt beneath Château Dusk; a capstone threat for Side Adventure 4 at high level.
bestiary.tactics: He commands thralls and spawn to swarm, saves Blood Tide for clustered foes, and feeds whenever he can. If destroyed outside his coffin, he retreats there as mist. The heroes must find it, and they must strike at dawn.
hooks: Lucan's real plan is to wake the Patriarch and offer him Morwenna's Council vote.
Countess Morwenna asks the party, quietly and in shame, to help her finish what she began two centuries ago.

entries.name: Glowing Skin
entries.text: The newt sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius and is warm to the touch. Miners keep them in jars as lanterns and hand-warmers.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Fire damage.

bestiary.name: Ember Newt
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Bright orange newts that bask in the Emberpeaks' hot springs and swim through lava-warmed pools. Miners consider them lucky, children consider them pets, and the copper dragon Vexirra considers them a snack. When the newts leave a spring all at once, the spring is about to erupt.
bestiary.where: Hot springs, mine tunnels, the slopes of the Emberpeaks.
bestiary.tactics: Newts flee. A cornered newt bites and scurries into the nearest crack.
hooks: Every ember newt in the valley has vanished from the springs overnight.
A miner's "lucky newt" is glowing brighter every day, and it is growing.

entries.name: Catalogued
entries.text: The clerk knows the location of every item in the hoard it serves and has Advantage on checks to find, appraise, or identify an object.

entries.name: Dragon's Protection
entries.text: If the clerk calls for help, its dragon patron hears it from up to 1 mile away.

entries.name: Quill-Knife
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Hoard-Clerk
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: The Lonely Wyrm Vexirra keeps ten thousand love letters, and someone has to sort them. Hoard-clerks are small, bespectacled folk of many peoples who serve dragons as archivists, accountants, and occasional therapists. They are devoted, pedantic, and frightened of fire, and they gossip constantly about the letters.
bestiary.where: Dragon lairs, the Emberpeaks mining towns, auction houses in Vesperine.
bestiary.tactics: Clerks hide behind shelves, throw quill-knives, and call their dragon. Each surrenders if threatened with the destruction of a catalogued item.
hooks: A hoard-clerk has fled the dragon's lair with a single letter, and it is terrified of what's written in it.
Clerks are selling "duplicate" letters from the hoard in the mining town, and some are not duplicates.

entries.name: Sure-Footed
entries.text: The ibex has Advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it Prone.

entries.name: Charge
entries.text: If the ibex moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with Ram on the same turn, the target has the Prone condition if it fails a DC 13 Strength saving throw.

entries.name: Ram
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 2 (1d4) Fire damage.

bestiary.name: Cinder Ibex
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Wild goats with coal-black horns that glow red at the tips, cinder ibexes leap between ledges above the lava flows and graze on fire-lichen. The miners' children race them on the sky-bridges, and the ibexes always win.
bestiary.where: The cliffs and lava fields of the Emberpeaks.
bestiary.tactics: An ibex charges intruders near its kids, then leaps away to a ledge it knows no one else can reach.
hooks: An ibex has stolen a miner's lunch and the key to the shrine-stone, which was in the lunch.
A herd of cinder ibex is fleeing down the mountain all at once.

bestiary.meta: Medium Swarm of Tiny Constructs, Unaligned
lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned
Languages Understands every language its letters were written in

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and can move through any opening large enough for a folded letter. It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Heartfelt Words
entries.text: A creature that starts its turn in the swarm's space must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be overwhelmed by the confessions it reads, gaining Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Papercuts
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 0 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Slashing damage.

bestiary.name: Love-Letter Swarm
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Ten thousand love letters in one place soak up a lot of feeling. In Vexirra's hoard, the oldest and most passionate letters sometimes rise into whirling flocks of paper, all sealing wax and desperate prose. They defend the hoard like a jealous lover. Read aloud, they are mostly harmless. Ignored, they cut.
bestiary.where: Vexirra's lair, post offices, the attics of the heartbroken.
bestiary.tactics: The swarm surrounds intruders, reading itself at them. A creature that reads one letter aloud with real feeling (DC 12 Performance) calms the swarm for 1 minute.
hooks: A love-letter swarm has escaped the lair and is delivering itself, very aggressively, all over the mining town.
The party needs one specific letter from the swarm; it's the only proof of a secret marriage.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the emberbloom is indistinguishable from an ordinary red mountain flower.

entries.name: Seed Burst
entries.text: When the emberbloom dies, it bursts. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature within 10 feet. Failure: 7 (2d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

entries.name: Ember Spit
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 30/90 ft. Hit: 9 (2d8) Fire damage, and flammable objects it hits ignite.

bestiary.name: Emberbloom
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Bright red flowers grow where lava has cooled, and miners pick them for sweethearts at their peril. An emberbloom spits glowing seeds that set dry grass ablaze, the better to clear room for its children. Pressed emberblooms stay warm forever and are a traditional Emberpeaks love token.
bestiary.where: Cooled lava fields, the slopes below Vexirra's lair.
bestiary.tactics: Blooms grow in patches of four to eight and spit embers at anything that moves. They can't move fast enough to matter, so retreat is easy.
hooks: A suitor needs an emberbloom bouquet for a dragon's approval. The only patch is on a lava flow.
The fields below the mine are burning every night, and the miners blame arson.

lines: Senses Blindsight 10 ft., Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 12

entries.name: Gift-Seeker
entries.text: The wyrmling has Disadvantage on attack rolls against any creature that has given it a gift of treasure within the last hour.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Ember Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 17 (5d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Ember Wyrmling
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Dragons of the Emberpeaks hatch from eggs laid in lava, coppery-red and hot to the touch. Wyrmlings are curious, greedy, and very loud. They steal anything shiny, eat anything warm, and adore anyone who brings them presents. Vexirra has none of her own, and she is lonelier for it.
bestiary.where: Lava caves, dragon lairs, very warm attics.
bestiary.tactics: A wyrmling breathes on the biggest threat and bites whoever is closest. It flees to its parent when Bloodied and can be bribed with treasure.
hooks: A wyrmling has followed the party home after they tossed it a coin, and now it lives in their inn room.
Somebody is selling dragon eggs from the Emberpeaks, and Vexirra will burn the town if she finds out.

lines: Languages Understands Ignan but can't speak

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries.text: The hound has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hound's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Ash Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, each creature in a 15-foot Cone. Failure: 14 (4d6) Fire damage, and the creature has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn from the ash. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Cinderhound
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Black hounds with coal-bright eyes and smoke curling from their jaws, cinderhounds were bred by mine-lords to guard their copper from thieves. Now they run wild through the abandoned shafts. They hunt in packs and follow the smell of copper, which makes them excellent at finding coin purses.
bestiary.where: Abandoned mines, smelters, lava tubes.
bestiary.tactics: The pack surrounds a target, breathes ash to blind it, and bites. They flee from deep water.
hooks: A pack of cinderhounds has taken over the old Redvein Mine, where a miner hid his love letters.
Someone in the Syndicate is training cinderhounds to sniff out Vexirra's treasure routes.

lines: Immunities Fire; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 8

entries.name: Molten Body
entries.text: A creature that touches the ooze or hits it with a melee attack takes 4 (1d8) Fire damage. Nonmagical metal weapons that hit it warp, taking a permanent −1 penalty to damage rolls (cumulative; destroyed at −5).

entries.name: Cooling
entries.text: If the ooze takes Cold damage, its AC increases by 4 and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 10 ft. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) Bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage.

bestiary.name: Slag Ooze
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Smelters dump their slag into the gorges, and the gorges are warm enough to keep it moving. A slag ooze is a sullen, glowing mass of molten waste metal that slides through the old smelting halls, eating ore and warping swords. Smiths say a sword quenched in a slag ooze's death-pool never breaks.
bestiary.where: Smelters, forges, lava gorges.
bestiary.tactics: It slides toward the nearest metal and engulfs it, ignoring everything else. Cold slows it to a crawl.
hooks: A slag ooze has swallowed the smelter's strongbox.
A smith wants a sword quenched in a slag ooze's death-pool for the Opera Council's champion.
bestiary.imm: Fire; Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.text: While motionless, the lurker is indistinguishable from a heap of gold coins, goblets, and jewels.

entries.name: Adhesive
entries.text: A creature that touches the lurker has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14).

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The lurker makes one Bite attack and one Coin Lash attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Coin Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

bestiary.name: Gilt Lurker
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Dragons' hoards attract things that look like treasure. A gilt lurker is a shapeshifting ambusher that has coated its hide in a dragon's discarded coins until it is indistinguishable from a pile of gold. It feeds on thieves, and dragons tolerate it the way people tolerate guard dogs. The coins stuck to it are real.
bestiary.where: Dragon hoards, treasure vaults, bank cellars.
bestiary.tactics: It waits for greedy hands, sticks fast, and bites. It never leaves the hoard.
hooks: The party's thief reached into a pile of gold, and the gold reached back.
Vexirra will pay a reward to anyone who can rid her lair of a lurker. It keeps eating her suitors.

lines: Immunities Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained
Languages The languages it knew in life

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.text: The ash can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Unsent Letter
entries.text: The ash is bound to the love letter it burned in life. If the letter's ashes are gathered and its words are spoken aloud to their intended recipient (or their grave), the ash is laid to rest.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The ash makes two Burning Touch attacks.

entries.name: Burning Touch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Fire damage plus 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Cry of the Spurned (Recharge 6)
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 14, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation that can hear the ash. Failure: 18 (4d8) Psychic damage, and the creature has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Jilted Ash
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: A miner who burned his love letter instead of sending it. A bride who threw her suitor's poem into the forge. Their regret outlived them. A jilted ash is a figure of drifting embers and smoke, still clutching the charred corner of a page. It haunts the place where the letter burned and attacks anyone who looks happy.
bestiary.where: Shrine-stones, old forges, abandoned miners' cottages.
bestiary.tactics: It drifts through walls, burns the couple in the party first, and screams when outnumbered. Speaking gently about its lost love makes it pause.
hooks: A jilted ash haunts the shrine-stone where the miners leave love poems, and it has started burning them.
Vexirra's hoard contains the original copy of the letter the ash burned, and she won't part with it easily.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

lines: Immunities Fire, Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

entries.name: Fire Form
entries.text: The dancer can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch. A creature that touches it or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 5 (1d10) Fire damage.

entries.name: Hypnotic Flames
entries.text: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the dancer and can see it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition until the start of its next turn. While Charmed this way, its Speed is 0 as it watches, entranced.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The dancer makes two Searing Caress attacks.

entries.name: Searing Caress
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Fire damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage if the target is Charmed.

entries.name: Twirl
entries.text: The dancer moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, leaving a trail of fire that deals 5 (1d10) Fire damage to any creature that enters it before the start of the dancer's next turn.

bestiary.name: Ash Dancer
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Some fire spirits are drawn to music. An ash dancer is a sinuous, laughing figure of flame that appears in smelters and forges where someone is singing, and it dances until the building burns down. It is flirtatious, vain, and endlessly entertaining, and it takes enormous offense if no one watches it.
bestiary.where: Smelters, forges, festival bonfires, the Emberpeaks' midsummer revel.
bestiary.tactics: It entrances onlookers with its dance, then caresses them to ash. It ignores those who refuse to look at it, and it can be persuaded to leave by a performance better than its own.
hooks: An ash dancer is holding court in an abandoned smelter, and miners keep going to watch it.
A bard wants to challenge an ash dancer to a dance-off, and needs bodyguards.
bestiary.imm: Fire, Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Unconscious

lines: Immunities Fire, Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Languages Understands Dwarvish and Common but can't speak

entries.name: Heated Body
entries.text: A creature that touches the warden or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Fire Absorption
entries.text: Whenever the warden is subjected to Fire damage, it regains Hit Points equal to the Fire damage dealt instead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The warden makes two Forge Hammer attacks.

entries.name: Forge Hammer
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Bellows Blast (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 27 (6d8) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Forgewarden
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: The great smelters of the Emberpeaks were built by dwarves who left a century ago, and left their guardians behind. Forgewardens are iron colossi with furnaces in their chests and hammers for hands. They still tend fires no one feeds and guard ore no one mines, and they attack anyone who touches the anvils.
bestiary.where: Abandoned dwarven smelters, mountain forges, ore vaults.
bestiary.tactics: It stands at the forge, hammers anything that comes close, and blasts groups with its bellows.
hooks: A forgewarden is the only thing that can reforge a broken dragon-scale, and it won't let anyone near its anvil.
Miners want to reopen the old smelter, but its warden still thinks it's working the night shift.
bestiary.imm: Fire, Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 14

entries.name: Treasure Sense
entries.text: The drake knows the exact location and value of every coin and gem within 120 feet of it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 28 (8d6) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

bestiary.name: Hoard Drake
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Young dragons too small to keep a mountain build their first hoards in mineshafts and ruined towers. Hoard drakes are jealous, nervous, and obsessed with counting. They negotiate over every copper and remember every insult. The best of them grow into great wyrms. The worst become miserly tyrants of a single valley.
bestiary.where: Abandoned mines, ruined watchtowers, the lesser peaks of the Emberpeaks.
bestiary.tactics: It fights from atop its hoard, breathing on intruders, and pursues thieves to the ends of the earth.
hooks: A hoard drake demands a "tax" from the sky-bridge, one coin per traveler, and it's getting greedier.
A young drake wants to court Vexirra and needs the party's help writing the perfect love letter.

lines: Senses Darkvision 120 ft., Tremorsense 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11

entries.name: Gold Fever
entries.text: Creatures within 60 feet of the gold-hunger that carry at least 10 GP worth of treasure hear it whispering promises of more. Such a creature must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw at the start of its turn or use its action to grab the nearest treasure it can see.

entries.name: Tunneler
entries.text: The gold-hunger can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed, leaving a 5-foot tunnel lined with veins of fool's gold.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The gold-hunger makes three Gilded Maw attacks.

entries.name: Gilded Maw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target is carrying gold, it also takes 4 (1d8) Psychic damage.

bestiary.name: Gold-Hunger
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Deep beneath the Emberpeaks something follows the copper seams, eating metal and the greed of those who mine it. Miners call it the gold-hunger: a segmented, glittering horror with a dozen gilded mouths. It whispers of riches until miners dig toward it, then it swallows them with their picks. When the copper seams start singing, it is near.
bestiary.where: Deep mines, copper seams, the roots of the Emberpeaks.
bestiary.tactics: It bursts from the rock under whoever carries the most treasure, using Gold Fever to scatter the party. Dropping all gold makes a creature invisible to its tremorsense.
hooks: Miners in the Redvein shaft hear singing in the copper, and three of them have dug into the dark without stopping.
The gold-hunger is tunneling toward Vexirra's hoard, and she wants the party to deal with it quietly.

lines: Languages Common, Draconic, Infernal, Telepathy 60 ft.

entries.name: Devil's Charm
entries.text: The suitor has Advantage on Charisma checks against Dragons and against any creature that has written a love letter in the past year.

entries.name: Smoldering Gaze
entries.text: A creature that meets the suitor's eyes and fails a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw finds it irresistibly charming and has Disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against it for 1 hour.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The suitor makes three Brimstone Rapier attacks, or two and uses Spellcasting.

entries.name: Brimstone Rapier
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Fire damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The brimstone suitor casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Charm Person, Disguise Self, Message; 2/Day Each: Suggestion, Fireball; 1/Day Each: Dominate Person, Wall of Fire

entries.name: Gallant Escape
entries.text: Trigger: The suitor is Bloodied for the first time. Response: It teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see in a puff of sulfur, blowing a kiss.

bestiary.name: Brimstone Suitor
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Infernal courts would dearly love a dragon's allegiance, and dragons are notoriously vain. Brimstone suitors are fiendish ambassadors of romance, horned and dashing, in coats of smoke and cinder-silk. They court dragons with poetry, flattery, and contracts. One has been writing to Vexirra for a year, and his letters are very good.
bestiary.where: Vexirra's lair, Vesperine's salons, any place a lonely, powerful creature can be flattered.
bestiary.tactics: He charms the most dangerous foe, fences with the rest, and flees with a flourish when Bloodied. He never kills a dragon's guests in front of the dragon.
hooks: Vexirra's newest admirer signs his letters "B." and smells faintly of sulfur.
A brimstone suitor offers to help the party win a dragon's favor, in exchange for one signature on one page.

entries.name: Kiln Heart
entries.text: A creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of the giant takes 3 (1d6) Fire damage from the heat pouring off it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes two Kiln Hammer attacks.

entries.name: Kiln Hammer
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 10 ft. Hit: 19 (3d8 + 6) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hurl Molten Stone
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +10, range 60/240 ft. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Slag Fling
entries.text: One creature the giant can see within 30 feet takes 10 (3d6) Fire damage as the giant flicks molten slag at it (no attack roll).

bestiary.name: Kiln Giant
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: The kiln giants of the high Emberpeaks fire pottery, glass, and bricks in volcanic vents, and trade them to the valleys below. They are craftsmen above all, proud of their work and furious when it is broken. They wear armor of fired clay. They consider Vexirra a valued customer and a terrible gossip.
bestiary.where: High volcanic vents, giant workshops, the trade road down the Emberpeaks.
bestiary.tactics: A giant hammers intruders who threaten its kilns and flings slag at archers. It can be reasoned with by anyone who praises its craft knowledgeably.
hooks: A kiln giant's masterpiece urn was stolen from its workshop and sold in Vesperine.
The kiln giants are refusing to trade with the lowlands until someone apologizes for a broken vase. It was the Oathwarden's.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The seraph has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Rebirth in Flame
entries.text: When the seraph dies, it bursts into flame and leaves a glowing egg. Unless the egg is doused in water within 1 minute, the seraph is reborn from it after 1 week.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The seraph makes three Phoenix Blade attacks.

entries.name: Phoenix Blade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) Fire damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The cinder seraph casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Light; 2/Day Each: Cure Wounds, Flame Strike; 1/Day Each: Heal, Wall of Fire

entries.name: Wings of Flame
entries.text: The seraph flies up to half its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and each creature it passes within 5 feet of takes 7 (2d6) Fire damage.

bestiary.name: Cinder Seraph
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: Legend says the Emberpeaks were raised by a phoenix that fell from the heavens, and that its children still nest above the clouds. Cinder seraphs are celestial firebirds in humanoid form, with wings of living flame and eyes like the sun through smoke. They burn away evil and are reborn from their ashes. They regard dragons as overgrown lizards.
bestiary.where: The summits of the Emberpeaks, above the clouds, volcanic shrines.
bestiary.tactics: A seraph strikes from the sky, sweeping through enemies on Wings of Flame and cutting down fiends first. It heals innocents and gives up a fight rather than burn a village.
hooks: A seraph's egg has been stolen from the summit and is being sold at auction in Vesperine.
The seraphs want the brimstone suitor dead, and they want the party to lure him into the open.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 25
Languages Common, Draconic, Giant, Ignan, and the language of every love letter ever written to it

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the wyrm fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Lonely Heart
entries.text: The wyrm has Disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against flattery, and Advantage on saving throws against any effect that would make it hostile to a creature that has written it a sincere letter.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The wyrm makes one Rending Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Rending Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 15 ft. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) Piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) Fire damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d6 + 8) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Heartfire Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 21, each creature in a 90-foot Cone. Failure: 99 (18d10) Fire damage. Success: Half damage.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the heartfire wyrm can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The heartfire wyrm regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Tail Swipe
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +14, reach 20 ft. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 8) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Smoldering Look
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 19, one creature the wyrm can see within 120 feet. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn, or the Charmed condition if it has ever flattered the wyrm.

entries.name: Wing Gust (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 22, each creature within 15 feet of the wyrm. Failure: 15 (2d6 + 8) Bludgeoning damage and the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only. The wyrm then flies up to half its Fly Speed.

bestiary.name: Heartfire Wyrm
bestiary.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
bestiary.lore: The ancient dragons of the Emberpeaks are copper-red and furnace-hot, their scales veined with molten light. Vexirra the Lonely Wyrm is one; there were others once. A heartfire wyrm hoards not gold but devotion: love letters, poems, oaths of fealty. It is lonely in a way only something that lives forever can be. Use this stat block for Vexirra if things go badly, or for her jealous ancient rival.
bestiary.where: The highest lair of the Emberpeaks; a capstone for *A Hoard of Love Letters* at high level.
bestiary.tactics: It breathes from the air, then lands to rend and swipe. It uses Smoldering Look on flatterers, whom it distrusts and adores. It can always be talked down by a letter that moves it (DC 20 Persuasion, or a genuinely good letter written at the table).
hooks: Vexirra's ancient rival has come to the Emberpeaks to burn her hoard of letters, and she asks the party for help.
A heartfire wyrm will grant a single wish of fealty to anyone who writes it a love letter it hasn't heard before.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Poisoned
Languages Understands Common but can't speak

entries.name: Living Ink
entries.text: The inkling can flatten itself into a blot on any page or wall and move through cracks as narrow as a quill nib.

entries.name: Copyist
entries.text: The inkling can perfectly copy any signature it crawls over.

entries.name: Ink Splash
entries.text: Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 15 ft. Hit: 2 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has Disadvantage on its next attack roll as ink stings its eyes.

bestiary.name: Inkling
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Notaries of the Accord write in ink laced with oath-salts, and spilled oath-ink sometimes wakes. An inkling is a crawling blot with a single gleaming eye, endlessly curious about documents. Forgers love them. Honest clerks loathe them, because a single inkling can wreck a decade of filing.
bestiary.where: Notaries' offices, the Syndicate's archive, libraries.
bestiary.tactics: Inklings flee, hide in paper, and copy signatures for whoever feeds them parchment.
hooks: Contracts across the Notary Quarter are signing themselves overnight.
A forger's inkling escaped and copied the Oathwarden's signature onto a hundred blank pages.

entries.name: Name-Stolen
entries.text: The thrall's true name is held by another. It has the Charmed condition toward the name-holder and can't be Charmed by anyone else. If its name is spoken back to it by someone who knows it, it repeats a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on a success. It can't consent to anything while Name-Stolen.

entries.name: Fading
entries.text: The thrall's edges blur in dim light, giving it Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and Disadvantage on Charisma checks.

entries.name: Grasp
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +3, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) Bludgeoning damage.

bestiary.name: Vowbound Thrall
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: A person whose true name has been taken, through a kiss-bound vow or a signature on the wrong page, begins to fade. Their friends forget them in the middle of conversations. Their reflections grey. And they obey the one who holds their name. Lady Nocturne Vesh has hundreds of them, and every one is a person waiting to be called home.
bestiary.where: The Thornwake's revels, the Syndicate's archive, the streets of Vesperine near Night 7. Use as minions, and reward freeing them.
bestiary.tactics: Thralls fight sluggishly in crowds. Speaking a thrall's true name, or destroying the page it's written on, frees it.
hooks: The party's contact in Vesperine has started fading, and nobody else remembers her name.
A crowd of grey-edged people is walking toward the Opera on Night 7, and none of them are blinking.

lines: Languages Understands Common and can repeat one sworn sentence it has heard

entries.name: Sworn Memory
entries.text: The raven perfectly remembers the last oath sworn in its presence and can recite it in the swearer's voice. Under the Accord, this recitation counts as testimony.

entries.name: Beak
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing damage.

bestiary.name: Witness Raven
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Every notary of the Accord keeps a raven to witness oaths. Ravens don't lie, can't be bribed (except with cheese), and remember forever. When a notary dies, their raven goes feral and haunts the places where oaths were sworn, repeating the last vows it heard to anyone who will listen.
bestiary.where: Notaries' offices, oath-stones, rooftops of the Notary Quarter.
bestiary.tactics: Ravens peck at oath-breakers and fly off. A raven that is fed will follow its new patron for a day.
hooks: A feral raven keeps reciting a wedding vow in the dead Oathwarden's voice.
The Syndicate wants every witness raven in the Notary Quarter dead before Night 7.

lines: Resistances Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
Immunities Necrotic, Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained
Languages The languages it knew in life

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries.text: The shade can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Unkept Promise
entries.text: The shade died with a promise unkept. If someone fulfills that promise for it, the shade is laid to rest.

entries.name: Regretful Touch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage, and the target has Disadvantage on its next saving throw against the Charmed condition.

bestiary.name: Oath-Broken Shade
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Those who die with a sworn promise unkept don't always rest. An oath-broken shade is a grey, flickering figure that repeats its unkept vow over and over, reaching for anyone who looks like the person it failed. Most are pitiable. All are cold to the touch.
bestiary.where: Graveyards, old battlefields, notaries' offices, wherever oaths were broken by death.
bestiary.tactics: The shade drifts through walls, touches the living, and retreats into stone when threatened.
hooks: A shade at the Velvet Opera keeps whispering, "I promised I'd come back for you."
Keeping a dead soldier's promise to his mother would lay three shades to rest.
bestiary.res: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
bestiary.imm: Necrotic, Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The fiendling has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Fine Print
entries.text: The fiendling can read any contract instantly and knows every loophole in it. It will share one for a price.

entries.name: Stinging Quill
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Poison damage.

entries.name: Vanish
entries.text: The fiendling has the Invisible condition until it attacks or until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Clause Fiendling
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Every infernal contract comes with a small devil to make sure it's honored. Clause fiendlings are bat-winged, bespectacled, and wickedly pedantic. They perch on their client's shoulder, whisper about the fine print, and sting anyone who tries to tear up the page. They love loopholes the way cats love birds.
bestiary.where: Notaries' offices, debtors' prisons, the shoulders of the desperate.
bestiary.tactics: A fiendling stays invisible near its contract and stings anyone who touches it. It flees, cursing, when Bloodied, and it reports everything to its master.
hooks: A fiendling has been assigned to the party's patron, and it wants to renegotiate.
For a single soul-coin, a fiendling will reveal the loophole in Lady Nocturne's name-contracts.

lines: Senses Darkvision 60 ft., Truesight 10 ft.; Passive Perception 14
Languages Understands Common but can't speak

entries.name: Scent of Perjury
entries.text: The hound knows when a creature within 30 feet tells a deliberate lie, and it can track an oath-breaker unerringly across any distance on the same plane.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) Psychic damage. If the target has broken an oath sworn under the Accord, it also has the Prone condition.

bestiary.name: Oathhound
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Accord's courts breed hounds to hunt perjurers: lean, white, silver-eyed dogs whose ears prick at every lie. An oathhound is incorruptible. It cannot be bribed or befriended, only commanded by a sworn notary or Oathwarden. With the Oathwarden dead, the hounds of the Accord are running loose, and they are hungry.
bestiary.where: The Accord's courthouses, the Notary Quarter, the roads of the Velvet Marches.
bestiary.tactics: Oathhounds hunt in pairs, targeting liars first. They ignore anyone who has never broken a vow.
hooks: A pack of oathhounds is following one of the party, and the party member insists they've never lied.
The Syndicate is using stolen oathhounds to sniff out who has been talking to the Watch.

lines: Immunities Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone
Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 9

entries.name: Sealing
entries.text: A creature Grappled by the ooze at the end of its turn has its mouth sealed with hot wax and can't speak or cast spells with Verbal components until it uses an action to peel the wax away.

entries.name: Pseudopod
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) Fire damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 12).

bestiary.name: Wax Seal Ooze
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Red sealing wax, warmed and poured a thousand times over secrets, can come to love them. A wax seal ooze is a glossy crimson blob that lives in archives and drips over open letters, re-sealing them. It doesn't like readers, so it seals their mouths shut.
bestiary.where: Archives, notaries' offices, the Opera Council's records room.
bestiary.tactics: It drops from a shelf onto anyone opening a document, grapples, and seals their lips.
hooks: The Syndicate's blackmail archive is guarded by a wax seal ooze, and every letter has been re-sealed.
A notary's oldest seal has started walking.
bestiary.imm: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

lines: Gear Notary's Seal, Sealing Daggers, Contract Satchel
Languages Common, Infernal, Sylvan, and two others

entries.name: Binding Signature
entries.text: A creature that signs a contract the broker presents is bound by its terms as if by a Geas (save DC 13) for as long as the contract says. A creature that is Charmed or coerced when it signs is not bound, and the broker knows it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The broker makes two Sealing Dagger attacks.

entries.name: Sealing Dagger
entries.text: Melee or Ranged Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) Piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The oath-broker casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13): At Will: Comprehend Languages, Message; 1/Day Each: Command, Hold Person, Zone of Truth

entries.name: Clause of Recourse
entries.text: Trigger: A creature within 30 feet that owes the broker anything hits it with an attack. Response: The attacker makes a DC 13 Charisma saving throw. Failure: The attack misses instead.

bestiary.name: Oath-Broker
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Notaries who discovered they could make more money writing bad contracts than honest ones became oath-brokers. Silver-tongued and impeccably dressed, they'll bind anyone to anything: debt, service, marriage, a name. They work for the Syndicate, for Lady Nocturne, and for anyone who pays. They are, crucially, scrupulous about consent. A forced signature is worthless, and they know it.
bestiary.where: The Notary Quarter, Syndicate dens, the back rooms of the Velvet Opera.
bestiary.tactics: A broker talks first, always, and fights only when the paperwork fails. It throws daggers from behind bodyguards and uses Hold Person on whoever seems likeliest to tear up a contract.
hooks: An oath-broker holds the deed to the party's safehouse and wants to discuss terms.
Someone signed a party member's name to a marriage contract. The broker is very sorry, legally speaking.

lines: Senses Blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius); Passive Perception 10

entries.name: Written Thorns
entries.text: Each thorn on the briar is a tiny barbed letter. A creature hit by the briar sees a word of its own secret written on its skin for 1 hour.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The briar makes two Thorn Lash attacks.

entries.name: Thorn Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 15 ft. Hit: 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13) if it is Medium or smaller.

bestiary.name: Inkthorn Briar
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Under the Syndicate's archive grows a hedge watered with spilled ink. Its thorns are letters and its leaves are pages, and it whispers fragments of every secret ever written in the vault above. Lady Nocturne planted it to guard her name-ledger.
bestiary.where: The Syndicate's archive, overgrown libraries, the garden of a dead notary.
bestiary.tactics: The briar grapples the nearest creature and drags it into its thorns. Fire sends it into a frenzy of thrashing.
hooks: The path to Nocturne's name-ledger runs through an inkthorn briar that knows everyone's secrets.
A notary's garden has sprouted a briar overnight, and the notary is missing.

lines: Immunities Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned
Languages Understands Common but can't speak

entries.name: Catalogue
entries.text: The sentinel knows the exact location of every document in its archive. If any is removed without a signed slip, it knows instantly.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The sentinel makes two Ledger Slam attacks.

entries.name: Ledger Slam
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Confiscate
entries.text: Strength Saving Throw: DC 14, one creature within 10 feet holding a document or book. Failure: The sentinel takes the document and files it inside its chest.

bestiary.name: Archive Sentinel
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Accord's great archive is guarded by sentinels of bronze and oak: tall, faceless constructs with filing drawers for ribs and brass ledger-books for fists. They have no malice, only a need for order. Remove a document without a signed slip and they will follow you to the ends of Carnelia to get it back.
bestiary.where: The Accord's archive, the Syndicate's vault, any great library.
bestiary.tactics: The sentinel targets whoever holds a stolen document, confiscates it, then escorts the thief out.
hooks: The evidence that proves Lady Nocturne's crimes is in the Accord's archive, and the clerk who signs slips is dead.
A sentinel has walked out of the archive and into the city, hunting an overdue library book.
bestiary.imm: Poison, Psychic; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned

lines: Immunities Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Poisoned
Languages The languages it knew in life

entries.name: Bound to the Oath
entries.text: The forsworn dead always knows the direction and distance to the creature it swore its unkept oath against. If reduced to 0 Hit Points while that creature lives, it rises again at dawn with all its Hit Points.

entries.name: Turn Resistance
entries.text: The forsworn dead has Advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns Undead.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The forsworn dead makes two Oathblade attacks.

entries.name: Oathblade
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) Slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Accusing Glare
entries.text: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature the forsworn dead can see within 30 feet. Failure: The target has the Paralyzed condition until the end of its next turn. If it is the object of the oath, it is instead Paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.

bestiary.name: Forsworn Dead
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Some knights died swearing vengeance, and the Accord, which honors oaths above all, will not let them rest until they get it. The forsworn dead are armored corpses with grave-light in their eyes, walking slowly and tirelessly toward their betrayers. They can't be bargained with or turned away. They'll stop when the oath is fulfilled, or when someone convinces them it was unjust.
bestiary.where: Old battlefields, the roads of the Velvet Marches, the Accord's courthouse steps.
bestiary.tactics: It ignores everyone but the object of its oath unless they get in the way. Then it hacks through them.
hooks: Sir Valentin Dusk's old squire has risen as forsworn dead, and he's walking toward Valentin.
The forsworn dead marching on Vesperine swore their oaths against the Thornwake. They could be useful allies.

lines: Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

entries.name: Swirling Pages
entries.text: The inkstorm is a whirlwind of ink and loose pages. Its space is Heavily Obscured, and it can enter a hostile creature's space.

entries.name: Blotting
entries.text: Any written text the inkstorm passes over is smeared and unreadable unless it is protected by magic.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The inkstorm makes two Ink Lash attacks.

entries.name: Ink Lash
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 10 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Inkstorm
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: When the Syndicate burned the Accord's lower archive, the ink and paper didn't burn. They rose. An inkstorm is a howling whirlwind of black ink and fluttering pages, every one of them a ruined contract. Notaries fear them more than fire.
bestiary.where: Ruined archives, the Notary Quarter, storms over the Accord's courts.
bestiary.tactics: The storm surges into crowds, blinding them, and blots out any contract being carried.
hooks: An inkstorm is circling the Notary Quarter, and every contract it touches is being voided.
Someone wants an inkstorm released inside the Syndicate's archive.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained

lines: Languages Understands every language but can speak only names it has eaten

entries.name: Forgettable
entries.text: Creatures that can see the gnawer have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice it, and forget its appearance a minute after it leaves their sight.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The gnawer makes three Gnaw attacks.

entries.name: Gnaw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Eat a Name
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 5 feet that is Bloodied. Failure: The target forgets its own name, and everyone who knows it forgets it too, until the gnawer dies or a Remove Curse is cast on the target. While nameless, the target has Disadvantage on Charisma checks.

bestiary.name: Nameless Gnawer
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Some things live between the lines of the Accord. A nameless gnawer is a thin grey shape with too many teeth and no face, which eats names. A person whose name is gnawed away is forgotten by everyone, even those who love them. Lady Nocturne's name-ledger attracts gnawers like spilled sugar attracts ants.
bestiary.where: Between the lines of contracts, archives, Nocturne's vault, the shadows of the Notary Quarter.
bestiary.tactics: The gnawer ambushes from walls, focuses on one victim until Bloodied, then eats its name and slips away. Calling the victim's name aloud lets the target and its allies retain their memory.
hooks: Something is eating names in the Notary Quarter, and nobody can remember who went missing.
A gnawer has eaten one of the party's names. Only something written before the bite can bring it back.

lines: Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 120 ft.; Passive Perception 15
Languages Common, Draconic, and every language it has read

entries.name: Living Record
entries.text: The drake's scales are inked with every contract it has witnessed. It can recite any of them verbatim and knows instantly if a creature within 60 feet is breaking one.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The drake makes one Bite attack and two Claw attacks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Claw
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +8, reach 5 ft. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Ink Breath (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 45 (10d8) Psychic damage, and the target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Vellum Drake
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: A vellum drake is a dragon of the archives: pale as fresh parchment, scales lettered in fine black script, breath of ink. The Accord keeps a few as living witnesses to its most important treaties. They love order, reading, and being consulted. They hate being lied to.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high archive, the courthouse roofs, ancient libraries.
bestiary.tactics: The drake breathes ink to blind, then bites oath-breakers. Proving it was lied to turns it on the liar.
hooks: The only surviving copy of the Accord's founding treaty is tattooed on a vellum drake that has gone missing.
A vellum drake will testify against Lady Nocturne, if the party can get it safely to the courts.

entries.name: Compound Interest
entries.text: Whenever a creature that owes the fiend a debt takes damage from it, the creature takes an extra 4 (1d8) Psychic damage for each week the debt is overdue (maximum 4d8).

entries.name: Debt-Sense
entries.text: The fiend knows the exact amount and location of every debtor in its ledger.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The fiend makes three Ledger Chain attacks.

entries.name: Ledger Chain
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 (1d8) Necrotic damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 17).

entries.name: Collect
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 16, one creature Grappled by the fiend. Failure: The target gains 1 Exhaustion level as the fiend takes something it is owed: a memory, a year, a color it will never see again.

bestiary.name: Usury Fiend
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Debts in Carnelia are taken seriously, and some debt-collectors are not mortal. A usury fiend is a hulking, grey-skinned devil in a moneylender's coat, wrapped in chains of iron links engraved with debtors' names. It collects for the debt-hells beneath the Accord's courts. It's always polite, and it always collects.
bestiary.where: Debtors' prisons, the Syndicate's counting houses, the debt-hells below the Accord.
bestiary.tactics: It drags debtors to it with chains and Collects. It will accept payment mid-fight. A fair offer actually stops it, though the new terms are never good.
hooks: A usury fiend has come for Sabine Velour's debt, with interest.
The fiend will forgive one debt if the party collects another for it, from a very dangerous debtor.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The seraph has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Witness of Vows
entries.text: The seraph knows every oath sworn within 1 mile of it and whether it is being kept. Creatures can't lie in its presence.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The seraph makes three Oath-Spear attacks.

entries.name: Oath-Spear
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +9, reach 10 ft. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) Radiant damage.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The vow seraph casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17): At Will: Detect Evil and Good, Zone of Truth; 2/Day Each: Dispel Magic, Remove Curse; 1/Day Each: Geas, Heal

entries.name: Release the Bound
entries.text: The seraph ends the Charmed condition on one creature it can see within 60 feet, or breaks one contract made under coercion.

bestiary.name: Vow Seraph
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: When the Accord was founded, its signatories called on the heavens to witness. The heavens sent vow seraphs: six-winged, silver-armored, eyes like scales of balance. They watch over every oath in Carnelia. They are furious about Lady Nocturne, who forces vows from people who can't refuse them.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high chamber, oath-stones, any place a great vow is sworn.
bestiary.tactics: The seraph frees thralls first with Release the Bound, then spears oath-breakers. It will not harm anyone who is being coerced.
hooks: A vow seraph will free every one of Nocturne's thralls, if someone proves the vows were coerced.
The seraph has judged a party member an oath-breaker and wants an explanation.

entries.name: Verdict
entries.text: Once the giant has heard both sides of a dispute, its ruling is magically binding as a Geas (save DC 17) on any party who agreed to arbitration.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The giant makes three Gavel attacks.

entries.name: Gavel
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 23 (3d10 + 7) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Sentence
entries.text: Constitution Saving Throw: DC 20, one creature the giant hit this turn. Failure: 9 (2d8) Thunder damage and the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

bestiary.name: Arbiter Giant
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Accord's highest court is presided over by giants: grey-bearded, plate-armored arbiters who have judged disputes between kingdoms for a thousand years. They are fair, ponderous, and absolutely incorruptible. With the Oathwarden dead, the arbiter giants are the last judges anyone trusts.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high court, ancient treaty-stones, the borders between kingdoms.
bestiary.tactics: An arbiter fights only to enforce a verdict or defend its court. It pounds the most dangerous foe and sentences anyone who strikes it.
hooks: The arbiter giants will try Lady Nocturne, if the party can drag her into court.
An arbiter has ruled against the party's patron, and the patron wants the verdict overturned.

lines: Immunities Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned
Languages All languages ever sworn in

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the Oathwarden fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: The Last Oath
entries.text: The Oathwarden is bound to finish the oath it swore in life. If destroyed before then, it re-forms at the Seal of the Accord in 1d10 days. It can be laid to rest only by fulfilling the oath or by a court of the Accord releasing it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Oathwarden uses Vowfire twice.

entries.name: Vowfire
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 18, one creature the Oathwarden can see within 120 feet. Failure: 38 (7d10) Necrotic damage. A creature that has broken an oath sworn under the Accord also has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage only.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries.text: The undying oathwarden casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 18): At Will: Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Zone of Truth; 2/Day Each: Banishment, Hold Monster; 1/Day Each: Power Word Stun, Wall of Force

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the undying oathwarden can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The undying oathwarden regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Oathbreaker Touch
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +10, reach 5 ft. Hit: 13 (3d8) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Recite the Oath
entries.text: Each creature within 30 feet that can hear the Oathwarden makes a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. Failure: The Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Undying Oathwarden
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: The Oathwarden of the Accord was murdered on the eve of Night 7. Some say it didn't stay dead. This stat block is for the undying Oathwarden: a gaunt, robed figure with the Seal of the Accord burned into its chest and candle-flame eyes, risen to finish the last oath it swore. Whether that oath was to protect Vesperine or to punish it depends on what the party learns.
bestiary.where: The Accord's high chamber, the Seal vault, the climax of the Night 7 storyline.
bestiary.tactics: It hurls Vowfire at oath-breakers, holds monsters, and recites its oath to cow lesser foes. It speaks before it fights and will stand down if shown its oath has been fulfilled.
hooks: The dead Oathwarden has been seen walking the Accord's halls, asking for the party by name.
The Oathwarden's last oath was to destroy whoever broke the Accord, and the evidence points at someone the party loves.
bestiary.imm: Poison; Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned

lines: Skills Arcana +18, Deception +18, History +18, Insight +10, Perception +10
Immunities Fire, Poison; Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
entries.text: If the Archivist fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: The Archivist has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: The Forfeit Ledger
entries.text: The Archivist's ledger holds every name forfeited under a broken infernal contract. While the ledger is within 1 mile, the Archivist can't be permanently destroyed. Destroying the ledger frees every name in it.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries.text: The Archivist makes three Quill Talon attacks.

entries.name: Quill Talon
entries.text: Melee Attack Roll: +13, reach 15 ft. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) Slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Read the Forfeit (Recharge 5–6)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 20, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the Archivist. Failure: 66 (12d10) Psychic damage, and the target has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn as it hears its own name read from the ledger. Success: Half damage only.

Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the forfeit archivist can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The forfeit archivist regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Rend Page
entries.text: The Archivist makes one Quill Talon attack.

entries.name: Amend Contract
entries.text: The Archivist ends one effect on itself, or imposes Disadvantage on the next saving throw of one creature it can see within 60 feet.

entries.name: Foreclose (Costs 2 Uses)
entries.text: Charisma Saving Throw: DC 20, one creature within 60 feet that has signed any contract. Failure: The creature gains 1 Exhaustion level and can't regain Hit Points until the end of its next turn.

bestiary.name: Forfeit Archivist
bestiary.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
bestiary.lore: Beneath the Accord's courts are the debt-hells, and at their bottom is the Forfeit Archivist: a vast, many-winged devil of red ink and black vellum, with quills for talons. Every name ever lost to a broken infernal contract is written in its ledger. It is patient, courteous, and old as the first lie. Lady Nocturne Vesh signed with it long ago, which is why her name-ledger works. It is also why she is afraid.
bestiary.where: The deepest debt-hell beneath the Accord; an epic-tier capstone for the Ledger & Oath storyline.
bestiary.tactics: It reads names from the Forfeit to stun the party, then tears through them with Quill Talons. It will negotiate at any point. It loves a bargain more than a victory. Burning the ledger is the only lasting win.
hooks: Lady Nocturne's contract with the Archivist comes due on Night 7, and she would rather the party paid it.
Every forfeited name in Carnelia, including the party's lost friends, is in one book at the bottom of the debt-hells.

bestiaryInfo.title: The Carnelia Bestiary
bestiaryInfo.subtitle: Monsters of Masque, Glamour, Salt, and Oath

collections.name: Masquerade & Mirror
collections.intro: Vesperine never takes its mask off. Behind the opera boxes, gambling salons, and canal-side galleries, the city breeds monsters out of vanity, gossip, perfume, and the silvered glass of a thousand mirrors. Some of them are only rumors in velvet. Others wait in the reflections, patient as debt. Most of these creatures can pass for guests until the music stops.

collections.name: Fair Folk & Glamour
collections.region: The Lanternwood, the Moth Court, and the Dusk Court beyond
collections.intro: Where the trees glow blue and the sky forgets to finish setting, the Fair Folk keep court. Their monsters are guests, servants, hounds, and lovers, and every one of them understands bargains better than you do. Nothing here is simply hostile. Everything here wants something, and most of it will ask nicely first.

collections.name: Bog & Thicket
collections.region: The Thicketmoor, the Sulking Stones, and Sallowmere's fen
collections.intro: Brambles the size of houses, honey dripping from wasp hives, and warm mud the ogresses call a spa. The Thicketmoor is ridiculous right up to the moment it drowns you. Its monsters are bawdy, territorial, and often lovesick, and the bog itself remembers every broken promise sworn on its banks.

collections.name: Salt & Siren
collections.region: The Saltgrave Coast, the Smugglers' Grotto, and the drowned deep
collections.intro: Ships wreck on the Saltgrave cliffs every night, and the sea keeps what it takes. The coast's monsters sing, lure, wreck, and drown, and a few of them only want to be kissed once more before the tide turns. Every sailor here knows the rule: never answer a song you can feel in your teeth.

collections.name: Vine & Blood
collections.region: The Duskvine Valley and Château Dusk
collections.intro: The Duskvine is beautiful the way a cut is beautiful. Its vineyards climb toward châteaux where the old nobility of House Dusk keep candlelit masquerades, willing donors, and a famous vintage. Not every noble is civilized, not every vine drinks rain, and the cellars run deeper than the maps.

collections.name: Ember & Hoard
collections.region: The Emberpeaks, the copper mines, and the Lonely Wyrm's lair
collections.intro: Steaming hot springs, copper-veined cliffs, rope sky-bridges, and a dragon who hoards love letters. The Emberpeaks are hot-tempered and covetous. Their monsters guard treasure, crave treasure, or simply are treasure that has learned to bite. Some of them are lonely enough to talk first.

collections.name: Ledger & Oath
collections.region: The Accord's courts, the Syndicate's archives, and the debt-hells below
collections.intro: In Carnelia, a kiss is a contract and a promise is a chain. The Accord binds every vow sworn in its lands, and where vows break, things crawl out of the ink. These monsters enforce, collect, devour, and forge oaths. Many of them are perfectly polite. All of them read the fine print.

tables.title: Reflection Drift (d6)
tables.note: At each dawn, each traveler rolls a d6; on a 1, roll here.
rows: Your reflection winks at someone you were talking to. They wink back.
Your reflection mouths a word: the answer to a riddle you haven't solved yet (GM's choice whether it's right).
Your reflection is wearing something far more daring than you are, and passers-by comment on it.
Your reflection points toward a clue in the room.
Your reflection is crying. It won't say why until you keep your promise.
Your reflection is missing for an hour. Somewhere in the city, people swear they saw you.

tables.title: Which Gateway Character? (d8)
tables.note: Solo: roll once. Group: roll once for the party, or each player rolls for a split-party opening.
rows: Lysander of the Silvered Glass
Rosewater Gallery, seconds after the murder
Main plot (Act I)
Sabine Velour
The Blue Hour salon, Velvet Quarter
Underworld thread: Varo, Hale, Drowned Market
Prince Caelum of the Dusk
Edge of the Lanternwood
Side Adventure 2 and the Fae endgame
Marisol Tidewhisper
A sea cave beneath the Saltgrave Coast
Side Adventure 3
Sir Valentin Dusk
A gilded mirror in Château Dusk
Side Adventure 4
Comic misfire: Little Gretch's hand-mirror. The shard was in an ogress's beauty kit. The PCs land in the Honeyhorn mud spa, and Gretch decides they are a gift from the gods for the Courting Moot.
The Thicketmoor
Side Adventure 1
Comic misfire: one of Vexirra's polished copper scales. The PCs land face-first in ten thousand love letters, and a dragon is very interested in where they came from.
The Emberpeaks
Side Adventure 5

Rivalry! Roll twice more (reroll 6–8). Both gateway characters reach through at once and grab a hand each. The PCs land wherever the first one leads, and the second shows up within a night, jealous and competitive.
First roll's landing
Both threads, plus a love triangle

tables.title: The Unravelling — Seven Nights
tables.note: Each night without an Oathwarden, roll on or choose from this table.
rows: Minor oaths fail. Gambling debts erase themselves; a dozen card-salon brawls erupt.
Love-vows weaken. Couples across the Gilded Crescent wake up and wonder why exactly they married each other. Comic and tragic in equal measure.
Trade contracts fail. Bread prices triple; the Syndicate profits. Riots in Lanternside.
Old curses, held at bay by protective oaths, slip free. Ghosts walk the Cypress Isle cemetery.
The Fae Duke's heralds — beautiful, smiling, antlered — appear at dusk, asking politely who will pay.
The masks of Vesperine begin to stick to their wearers' faces. Panic.
At midnight, the Accord fails. Unless a new Oathwarden is sworn, the Fae Duke claims the city's founding bloodlines (and their city) as his debt.

tables.title: The Clue Trail (Keystones ★)
tables.note: Any three Keystone clues make a solid accusation of the killer.
rows: Rosewater Gallery (murder scene)

★ Clock stopped at 11:47 (Riddle 6 on its case reveals the pendulum was knocked, not wound down). Lavender silk mask-ribbon snagged on the trellis by the mirror wall. The black stain is darkest under where the mask sat, faint on the lips.
Investigation DC 12 (ribbon), Medicine DC 14 (stain pattern)
Someone came through the mirror door before midnight; the poison was in the mask
Dressing Gallery (behind mirror wall)
★ The original, unpoisoned mask of Aurelian, hidden in a costume trunk — its ribbon cut, not frayed. Actors' testimony: Thessaly "stepped out around quarter to."
Investigation DC 14, or Persuasion DC 12 with the actors
Masks were swapped; Thessaly left her station
Sable Palazzo (study)

Riddle-locked desk (Riddle 1): Aurelian's journal — "The masks remember. She cannot. She must not." — and the faceless porcelain mask sent to him anonymously. A painted-over portrait in the gallery (scrape it or use detect magic): a young bride with Thessaly's eyes.
Riddle; Investigation DC 15 for the portrait
Aurelian had a secret involving a woman he wronged
Vos Perfumery
Widow's Sigh identification. ★ Coded order ledger (Riddle 3): "Madame R. — bloodrose, 1 vial." Oath-breaking salts order for "Lady C.M." (red herring).
Riddle; Ezren's cooperation
Thessaly tested the poison; Celestine looks guilty
Drowned Market (Mother Brine)

Password riddle (Riddle 5). Mother Brine's sale record: "Old vellum page, wedding oath, sold to lady in grey veil for 3 masks." ★ One of the three masks, still on display — signed inside with Thessaly's maker's mark.
Riddle; Persuasion DC 13 or 20 ducats
