tables.title: Enthrallment — The Five Stages
columns: Warning signs others can notice (Insight or Medicine DC 13, or automatic at stage 3+)
rows: Smitten
Daydreams of the fey; disadvantage on Perception checks to notice them approaching (you want them to surprise you).
Humming the fey's tune; a faint scent of their flowers; glittering pupils.
Beguiled
Disadvantage on Insight checks against the fey; defends them in conversation; cannot consent to romance (table rule).
Speaking in half-rhymes; flinching from iron; losing small stretches of time.
Enthralled
Charmed by the fey. Follows one suggestion from them per day. Will not willingly reveal the fey's secrets.
The fey's colors appear in their clothing; their reflection wears a crown of the fey's flowers (an oathless traveler's reflection may try to warn them).
Bound
Any vow the fey requests is "sealed" (a forged kiss-oath; see Freeing Victims). The victim acts as the fey's agent when the fey is within 1 mile; the GM may take control in key scenes.
Cold hands; no shadow at noon; they no longer use their own name.
Nameless

Their true name is stolen and kept by the fey (in a jar, a jewel, or the Book). Friends must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence check to remember who they are. The victim becomes an NPC servant of the fey until freed.
Others' memories of them blur; their handwriting vanishes from letters.

tables.title: Counter-Charms & Protections
rows: Cold iron

Carrying it: advantage on saves against fey charm. Touching iron to an enthralled victim: an immediate new save to reduce Enthrallment by 1 (once per victim per day). Cold-iron weapons hurt Thorns badly.
A true name, spoken thrice
Call an enthralled friend by their full true name three times: they get a new save with advantage, reducing Enthrallment by 1 on a success (by 2 if the caller loves them).
Cold water
Dunking or splashing a victim's face ends charmed and sleep effects from fey and grants a new save. (Ondine hates this.)
Refusing gifts
Politely refuse the same fey's gift three times and you're immune to that fey's gift and food triggers for 24 hours. Rudeness doesn't count; it must be gracious.
Fair exchange
Pay for a fey gift with something of equal value and it adds no Enthrallment. Haggling is encouraged.
Never "thank you"
Say "I'm grateful," "you're kind," or "I'll remember this" instead. Players who slip up should be teased mercilessly.
Clothes inside out
Advantage on saves against glamours and illusions (and disadvantage on Charisma checks with mortals, who think you're ridiculous).
Bread and salt
Under a mortal host's roof, fey who accept bread and salt cannot use charm on that household for the night.
Laughter

Fey glamours can't stand mockery. A Performance (Comedy) check vs. the fey's spell DC makes the glamour flicker: everyone sees their true form for 1 round, and Thorns have disadvantage on their next charm.
The Oathless Glass and its shards
Mirrors linked to the Glass show fey in their true forms. A shard held up to a victim lets them see the fey's true face (new save, advantage).
A freely given true kiss

The Accord's oldest law: a kiss freely given in genuine love, with the victim's consent given before enthrallment or by a sincere standing promise between partners, outranks a fey kiss. It can end stage 1–4 Enthrallment once per campaign per victim, at the GM's discretion. Never forced, and never a kiss on someone who can't currently agree; a hand-kiss or brow-kiss is enough.

secrets.title: The Truth — who killed Aurelian Sable
secrets.html:
The killer is Madame Thessaly Rook, the beloved maskmaker — who is secretly Lady Isaveth Sable, Aurelian's first wife.

Thirty-one years ago, Isaveth was the heiress of House Sable, one of the city's founding families, whose blood is bound to the Accord. She fell for a handsome, penniless apprentice of the Hall of Vows named Aurel Fenn. At their wedding she kissed him and swore the traditional, romantic vow: "Everything I am is yours."

Aurel knew the Ledger's ink better than anyone. He used his apprentice's access to have the Ledger read her vow literally. Overnight, her name, her title, her inheritance, and her very memory of herself transferred to him. He became "Aurelian Sable," the grieving widower of a bride "lost to the sea." She woke on the Lanternside docks with no name, no past, and a wedding ring she couldn't explain. An old maskmaker took her in. She became Thessaly Rook — and spent thirty years making masks for the man who stole her face.

Six months ago, Varo Kestrel of the Thorn Syndicate stole a page from Aurelian's private desk as blackmail material: the original wedding-vow page, which Aurelian had secretly cut out of the Ledger decades ago. The Syndicate fence, Old Mother Brine, didn't understand what it was and sold it as "antique vellum" to a lady in a grey veil buying lace for masks. When Thessaly touched the page that held her own vow, every memory came back at once.

The method. Thessaly made Aurelian's festival mask, as she had every year for thirty years.

  1. She obtained Widow's Sigh — a fey moth-orchid toxin, inert until it meets the scent of bloodrose — from the Moth Court of the Lanternwood, paying with her dream of her own wedding day.
  2. She knew Seraphine always wears Ezren Vos's bloodrose perfume, and that Aurelian would kiss Seraphine at midnight.
  3. She sabotaged the ribbon of Aurelian's festival mask so that it would fray during the evening. At 11:45, as she'd planned, Aurelian sent for her to fix it.
  4. At 11:47, she slipped through the secret door behind the mirror wall from the Dressing Gallery and swapped his mask for an identical one lined with Widow's Sigh. Brushing past, her skirts caught the long pendulum of the gallery clock beside the mirror wall — stopping it at 11:47 — and her mask-ribbon snagged on the rose trellis.
  5. At midnight, Seraphine's bloodrose-scented kiss and breath activated the toxin in the mask's lining. The black stain spread from beneath the mask, not from his lips.
  6. She stashed the original, unpoisoned mask in a costume trunk in the Dressing Gallery, meaning to collect it after the chaos. She hasn't managed it yet.

Motive. Revenge — and restoration. With Aurelian dead and the Ledger keeperless, the Accord demands a new Oathwarden of founding blood within seven nights. Isaveth intends to step forward, prove who she is with the vow-page, and reclaim her name, House, and fortune. She does not intend for the city to fall — but she underestimated how fast the oaths would unravel, and she's frightened.

What she wants from the PCs. At first: to steer them toward Celestine (who had motive and bought "poison"). Later, if exposed: their help to be named Oathwarden. She is the GM's most dangerous, most sympathetic NPC.

secrets.title: The Clue Trail & Red Herrings
secrets.html:
The PCs need any three "Keystone" clues (marked ★ below; the side adventures offer four more) to make a solid accusation of Thessaly. Each location also offers red herrings and leads to other places. No single clue is required — there are ten Keystones across the campaign, and the truth can be reached by many roads.

Location Clues found DC / Method Points toward
Rosewater Gallery (murder scene) ★ Clock stopped at 11:47 (Riddle 6 on its case reveals the pendulum was knocked, not wound down). Lavender silk mask-ribbon snagged on the trellis by the mirror wall. The black stain is darkest under where the mask sat, faint on the lips. Investigation DC 12 (ribbon), Medicine DC 14 (stain pattern) Someone came through the mirror door before midnight; the poison was in the mask
Dressing Gallery (behind mirror wall) ★ The original, unpoisoned mask of Aurelian, hidden in a costume trunk — its ribbon cut, not frayed. Actors' testimony: Thessaly "stepped out around quarter to." Investigation DC 14, or Persuasion DC 12 with the actors Masks were swapped; Thessaly left her station
Sable Palazzo (study) Riddle-locked desk (Riddle 1): Aurelian's journal — "The masks remember. She cannot. She must not." — and the faceless porcelain mask sent to him anonymously. A painted-over portrait in the gallery (scrape it or use detect magic): a young bride with Thessaly's eyes. Riddle; Investigation DC 15 for the portrait Aurelian had a secret involving a woman he wronged
Vos Perfumery Widow's Sigh identification. ★ Coded order ledger (Riddle 3): "Madame R. — bloodrose, 1 vial." Oath-breaking salts order for "Lady C.M." (red herring). Riddle; Ezren's cooperation Thessaly tested the poison; Celestine looks guilty
Drowned Market (Mother Brine) Password riddle (Riddle 5). Mother Brine's sale record: "Old vellum page, wedding oath, sold to lady in grey veil for 3 masks." ★ One of the three masks, still on display — signed inside with Thessaly's maker's mark. Riddle; Persuasion DC 13 or 20 ducats The vow-page went to Thessaly
Hall of Vows / Vault of Broken Vows Vault door riddle (Riddle 2); needs Varo's key or Thieves' Tools DC 18. Inside: the Ledger, bleeding ink; a missing page stub dated 31 years ago with surviving text: "…Aurel Fenn and Isaveth Sable, everything I am…" The Veiled Sisters confirm that a vow-page touched by its swearer restores what it holds. Riddle + access; History DC 13 Aurelian stole his wife's identity
Sable Crypt (Cypress Isle) Riddle 4 on the sarcophagus. ★ The tomb of "Lady Isaveth Sable" is empty, except for a wedding veil of lavender silk matching the ribbon in the Gallery. Ghosts (Night 4+) whisper "she lives, she sews, she smiles." Riddle; Athletics DC 15 to open the lid otherwise Isaveth is alive; lavender links to Thessaly
Thessaly's Atelier (Search with a warrant or by stealth.) A hatbox holding a thirty-year-old wedding mask and ★ the vow-page itself, wrapped in lavender silk. A pressed moth-orchid in a book of poems. Investigation DC 16 or Stealth DC 15 to search unseen Proof of identity and motive; the orchid points to the Lanternwood
The Lanternwood (side quest) Queen Ilysse of the Moth Court will reveal (if bargained with) that "a silver-haired woman traded the dream of her wedding day for a sigh of our orchid." See Side Adventure 2 Confirms Thessaly obtained the poison

Speak with Dead & truth magic. Aurelian's corpse answers honestly but knows little: "I kissed her and I burned" (misleads toward Seraphine); "The masks remember"; if asked about his wife: "Everything she was is mine." Zone of truth works normally, but Thessaly answers only literal questions literally ("Were you in the Dressing Gallery all evening?" "I was in and around it, yes, darling.").

Red Herrings

  1. The Poison Kiss. Everyone believes Seraphine's kiss killed him. It did — but only as the trigger.
  2. Celestine's "Poison." The white crystals in her vanity are fake oath-breaking salts. The burned love letter makes her look like a conspirator.
  3. Hale's Purse. A Syndicate bribe — real corruption, unrelated to murder.
  4. Varo's Stolen Key. He was caught robbing the corpse's coat — a thief, not a killer.
  5. Dream-Moth Dust. Traces of dream-moth dust on Aurelian's collar point to the Lanternwood and the Moth Court. He used it recreationally. (But following it to the Lanternwood does uncover the orchid trade.)
  6. The Syndicate Frame. On Night 3, the Thorn Syndicate plants a forged letter signed "S." in Seraphine's dressing room ("It will be done at midnight") to keep her pliable. A DC 15 Investigation check spots the forgery (the ink is fresh; Seraphine signs with a little lark doodle, not a letter).

secrets.title: Riddle answers — The Black Kiss
secrets.html:
Running riddles. Read the riddle aloud and give the players time. If they're stuck, allow an Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) check (DC 13) for a hint; a failed check still gives the hint, but costs time (advance the night by one scene) or attracts trouble.

Riddle 1 — Aurelian's Desk (a brass lock shaped like lips; speak the answer to it)

Carved to smile, I cannot laugh;
I wear no face, yet I am half
of every lie the dancers tell.
Lift me, love, and break the spell.

Answer: A mask. Hint: "What does every dancer in Vesperine wear tonight?"

Riddle 2 — The Vault of Broken Vows (carved above the door; a Veiled Sister asks it)

Given freely, I weigh nothing;
broken, I'm as heavy as stone.
Lips make me, lies unmake me,
and I am never wholly your own.

Answer: A promise (an oath / a vow). Hint: "What is this whole hall full of?"

Riddle 3 — Ezren's Scent-Coded Ledger (the cipher key on the first page)

I arrive before the lover
and linger when she's gone.
You cannot see or hold me,
yet I swear where she has been.

Answer: A scent (perfume). Saying "scent" lets the reader realize each customer is recorded under the name of a scent. Ezren's code-names: Lavender = Madame Rook; Frost-Lily = Lady Celestine; Bloodrose = Seraphine. The page reads: "Lavender — 1 vial bloodrose."

Riddle 4 — The Empty Sarcophagus (inscribed on the lid of Isaveth's tomb)

What can be stolen, yet never be touched,
lost while you hold it, and taken with a kiss —
and returned to its owner only by being spoken?

Answer: A name. Speaking "a name" — or speaking "Isaveth" — slides the lid open. Hint: "What's carved above every tomb?"

Riddle 5 — Mother Brine's Password (she asks it through a slot in her door)

I have leaves but no branches,
a spine but no bones;
I hold a thousand kisses
and I've never been kissed.

Answer: A book (the Ledger). Hint: "What does every scholar and lover in the Hall of Vows keep their eyes on?"

Riddle 6 — The Gallery Clock (engraved on its glass case; solving it lets the PCs open the case without breaking the enchantment protecting it)

I have a face but cannot see,
two hands but cannot hold.
I strike, but I wound no one;
stop my heart and I grow cold —
yet the moment of my dying
is the truth I've always told.

Answer: A clock. Inside, the pendulum is bent sideways and caught with a strand of lavender silk — knocked, not wound down. The stopped time, 11:47, is the moment someone came through the mirror door.

secrets.title: Nocturne and the murder (late reveal)
secrets.html: How it ties to the murder. Thirty-one years ago it was Nocturne who whispered the trick to young Aurel Fenn: that a wedding vow of "everything I am is yours" could be read literally. Her price was Aurel's own true name, which is why Aurelian's corpse, under speak with dead, cannot say his birth name. She holds it in a jar of black glass. This is a secret for very late reveals; it changes nothing about who killed him.

secrets.title: Glamours & Reveals — the eight guises
secrets.html:
Fey (true self) Human alias Cover identity in Vesperine Glamour DC
Lady Nocturne Vesh Madame Noor Vesperelle A wealthy foreign widow who hosts the Black Fan, the most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent 18
Prince Caelum of the Dusk Cael Rosier A charming rose merchant and high-stakes gambler, a regular at The Blue Hour 17
Ondine Mirewillow Dina Mire A laughing bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside 14
Rillo Fennamint Master Orrin Mintleaf Dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at the Velvet Opera's after-parties 14
Pipwhistle Dewlace Pip Dewley A bubbly, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble tavern on Needle Row 12
Sir Merrow Ashgrave Brother Ash A grey-robed mourning friar who sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes 16
Amaranth Notary Amar Thorne A soft-spoken contract notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows 16
Queen Ilysse of the Hush Madame Ilse Hush A veiled dream-reader who sells sleep-tonics at the Hush House in the Velvet Quarter 16
  • The Guise. A fey's human guise is an illusion that also fools touch, smell, and sound. It is not a spell that detect magic reveals at a glance; it is part of what the fey is. True seeing, a shard of the Oathless Glass, or a successful Insight check against the fey's Glamour DC (listed below) lets one viewer see through it. That viewer then knows the truth, but everyone else still sees the human.
  • The Mirror Rule. Reflections always show the true face (Part 2). Fey in disguise avoid mirrors, still water, and polished silver: they drape mirrors, stand with their backs to windows, and ripple the wine in their glass. A PC who deliberately watches a fey's reflection needs a Perception check (DC 10 in good light, DC 15 in candlelight or a crowd) to catch a clear look. On a success, they see the true form in the glass. Oathless travelers (Glass-Marked PCs) have advantage on this check, because the Glass "wants" them to see.
  • Cold Iron. Every disguised fey reacts to cold iron: a flinch, a hiss, a burn mark, gloves that never come off. Touching cold iron to a disguised fey's bare skin forces a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, its glamour flickers for 1 round, and everyone present glimpses the true form.
  • Tells. Each fey has small, recurring tells. Reward players who notice patterns across sessions; you might give a free Allure box or Inspiration to the first player who says "Wait. Have we ever seen her near a mirror?"
  • Reveal Shock (optional). When a fey drops its glamour dramatically, each mortal witness who didn't already know makes a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or is frightened (Thorns) or charmed (Tempters) until the end of its next turn. The shock of beauty, or of betrayal, hits hard.
  • Relationships carry over. Allure and Enthrallment earned with the human guise apply to the true fey. A PC who flirted with "Pip the barmaid" has been flirting with Pipwhistle all along, and Enthrallment gained from the guise counts in full. Any romance that happened while a PC was unaware they were dealing with a fey is grounds for a sharp in-world grievance, and the Accord would let the PC void any kiss-oath sealed under that deception.

secrets.title: Guise: Lady Nocturne Vesh as Madame Noor Vesperelle
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: A rich, mysterious widow "from across the sea" who arrived last spring and instantly became the city's most sought-after hostess. Her salon, the Black Fan, meets in a candlelit palazzo where every mirror is draped in black crepe ("a mourning custom of my homeland, darling"). Invitations are black envelopes sealed with a lip-print. She is the salon's center of gravity, the woman everyone wants to be seen with.
  • Tells:
  • She is never near an uncovered mirror. Her palazzo's draped mirrors are a tell in themselves (Insight DC 14 to find the "custom" suspicious).
  • She always wears long gloves, and she uses silver cutlery, never iron. An iron fork offered to her goes politely unused.
  • Guests can never quite describe her face afterward. An Intelligence DC 13 check to recall it fails for anyone at Enthrallment 1+.
  • Dead rose petals collect where she has sat.
  • Insight DC 18: her smile arrives a half-second before her eyes do.
  • Mirror reflection: Bone-white skin, black lips, starless eyes, a crown of dead roses, and the dark sapphire at her throat pulsing with a stolen name.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. A crepe-draped mirror is uncovered in her presence, or the Oathless Glass or a shard is turned on her. 2. Cold iron touches her skin. 3. She is laughed at publicly and sincerely (a successful Performance (Comedy) check against DC 18). 4. A PC reaches Enthrallment 4 with her. She reveals herself deliberately, to savor it. 5. The stroke of midnight at her Night 6 masquerade, when she unmasks for the whole Thornwake.

Read-aloud: The Black Fan Falls. Madame Vesperelle laughs, that low, warm laugh that has made half of Vesperine fall in love with her, and snaps her black lace fan shut. "Darling," she says, "you've been looking at the wrong face all evening." Behind her, the crepe slithers from the great mirror like a shed skin. In the glass stands someone else: skin white as a bone in moonlight, lips black as Ledger ink, eyes with no stars in them at all. The candles gutter. When you turn back from the mirror, the widow is gone and only the other one remains, smiling exactly the same smile. "There," says Lady Nocturne Vesh. "Isn't that better? Now we can stop pretending you weren't already mine."

secrets.title: Guise: Prince Caelum of the Dusk as Cael Rosier
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: A dashing, red-coated rose merchant who supplies every ballroom in the Gilded Crescent and loses fortunes at Sabine's card tables with a grin. Everyone knows Cael; no one knows where he lives. His roses are famous for never wilting.
  • Tells:
  • He never says "thank you," and he deftly sidesteps it when others say it to him ("Don't thank me, darling, it's bad luck").
  • Roses near him bloom; cut flowers in a room open as he enters.
  • Perception DC 15 in candlelight: the shadow of his head has antlers.
  • He flinches from iron coins and pays only in silver and gold.
  • Insight DC 17: he speaks in carefully true sentences and never tells a plain lie.
  • Mirror reflection: Twilight-violet skin, golden eyes, rose-twined antlers, and a briar crown. In the glass he looks at the viewer directly and puts a finger to his lips.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. He seals a kiss-bound bargain. Roses burst from the air as the vow takes. 2. Nocturne threatens a PC he has grown fond of, and he reveals himself to stand in her way. 3. A PC reaches Allure 3 with him and asks the right question (Insight DC 18, Part 6). He chooses to show them. 4. Sunset in the Lanternwood, where his glamour simply will not hold. 5. A cold-iron blade at his throat.

Read-aloud: The Rose Merchant's True Face. Cael sighs, the way a man sighs when a card game has gone on too long, and sets down his glass. "I did so enjoy being ordinary," he says. Every rose in the room opens at once. The red coat lengthens into rose-petal velvet stitched with thorns; his skin deepens to the violet of the last minute before night; and from his dark curls rise antlers twined with climbing roses, brushing the chandelier, which chimes. His eyes are molten gold. "Prince Caelum of the Dusk," he says, bowing, "and still, I promise, your friend. I simply wasn't allowed to say so until now."

secrets.title: Guise: Ondine Mirewillow as Dina Mire
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: The giggling, sun-freckled bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside, the city's cheapest and most popular bathhouse. She scrubs backs, braids hair, and gossips about everyone. Patrons who doze in the warm pools sometimes wake much later than they meant to.
  • Tells:
  • Her hems are always damp, though she never seems to get wet.
  • Frogs sing in the drains when she laughs.
  • The baths' lost-and-found holds a suspicious mountain of single shoes.
  • She has worked at the Lilywater "for years," but the oldest regulars swear she hasn't aged in forty.
  • Insight DC 14: she asks every customer for "just a little something," such as a ribbon or a lock of hair.
  • Mirror reflection: She ripples any water near her, so the PCs have disadvantage on the Perception check in water. In a mirror she has green-gold skin, willow-leaf hair, and eyes that ripple like a pond.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Cold water splashed in her face. She shrieks and the glamour slips away with the water. 2. Someone mentions Auntie Sallowmere: a flash of fury, and frogs everywhere. 3. She is caught red-handed with a sleeping customer's shoes. 4. She uses Water Stride to escape, vanishing into one pool and laughing out of another.

Read-aloud: The Bath-Girl in the Bubbles. Dina is mid-giggle, a braid of somebody's hair half-finished in her fingers, when the bucket of cold water hits her. She shrieks, and the shriek turns into a laugh like a brook in spring. The freckles slide off her like wet paint. Her skin is green-gold now, her hair a cascade of willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, her eyes dark and rippling. Every frog in the drains begins to sing. "Well, that was rude," says Ondine Mirewillow, wringing out a lily. "And I was being so good. Mostly. Does anyone want their shoes back?"

secrets.title: Guise: Rillo Fennamint as Master Orrin Mintleaf
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: The beloved, bearded dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at every Velvet Opera after-party and teaches the nobility to waltz. He always wears a wide-brimmed hat and tall, oddly heavy boots. His parties end with the best dancers "going on somewhere better."
  • Tells:
  • Perception DC 13: his boots clip-clop on stone like hooves.
  • He never takes off his hat, even indoors and even when bowing.
  • He refuses to dance on iron-studded floors and won't touch the Opera's iron railings.
  • His tunes are always somehow your song.
  • Insight DC 14: he scans the crowd for "dreamers" with the eye of a talent scout.
  • Mirror reflection: Gilded ram's horns, chestnut curls, and goat legs, dancing even when he's standing still.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. He loses himself in the dance past midnight: he kicks off the boots and flings away the hat. 2. A PC out-plays him in a music duel. His pride bursts the glamour. 3. Dawn breaks while he's still playing in the Lanternwood. 4. Someone stamps on his "foot" hard: an iron-heeled boot on the hoof.

Read-aloud: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots. The music is too good to stop. Master Mintleaf whoops, kicks one boot clean across the ballroom, then the other, and his hat goes sailing after them. Where his feet should be, polished hooves strike sparks from the marble. Gilded ram's horns curl from his chestnut hair; his trousers are suddenly fur from the hips down. The dancers scream, then laugh, then don't stop dancing. "No point hiding it now!" bellows Rillo Fennamint, pipes at his lips. "Who's coming to the after-party? The forest's only a short walk, and the moon's out!"

secrets.title: Guise: Pipwhistle Dewlace as Pip Dewley
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: The bubbly, curly-haired, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble, a cozy tavern on Needle Row. She's everyone's favorite: quick with a tray, quicker with gossip, and always asking for "a little something for luck." Buttons go missing whenever she's near.
  • Tells:
  • Buttons vanish from coats wherever she's been, and her apron pockets jingle.
  • She serves everything in pewter and never touches the iron tankards on the top shelf.
  • Startle her and, for a blink, she seems much smaller (Perception DC 12).
  • Faint pink sparkles cling to anyone she kisses on the nose "for luck."
  • Insight DC 12: she trades favors for favors and remembers every promise down to the word.
  • Mirror reflection: A hand-sized pixie with dragonfly wings, standing on the bar where Pip's tray should be, waving cheerfully.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. She sneezes, especially at pepper or dust. Pop. 2. Someone pays her in buttons. She can't help it: she shrinks with glee. 3. A PC refuses one of her tiny promises, or breaks one she's owed. 4. Someone offers her a whole cake. 5. Cold iron in her hand. She drops to pixie size with a squeak and hides in a teacup.

Read-aloud: The Barmaid Goes Pop. Pip leans across the bar, beaming, a tray of steaming teacups balanced on one hand. "Now, sweet thing, a little kiss on the nose for luck, and you'll owe me just one teensy song—" Someone drops a pouch of shiny brass buttons on the counter. Pip's eyes go enormous. There is a sound like a cork leaving a bottle, a puff of pink glitter, and the teacups crash down onto an empty floor. Something the size of your hand zips up out of the wreckage on dragonfly wings, clutching a button like a shield, glowing bright, delighted pink. "Ohhh, those are lovely," squeaks Pipwhistle Dewlace. "Oops. Um. Surprise?"

secrets.title: Guise: Sir Merrow Ashgrave as Brother Ash
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: A tall, grey-robed mourning friar of no order anyone can name. He sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes and Cypress Isle funerals, holds hands, and listens. The mourners he comforts stop crying, and many of them, oddly, come back to the Drowned Market for "something to help them sleep."
  • Tells:
  • A faint silver dust on his lips and on the hands of those he's comforted.
  • Grey petals drift from the hem of his robe.
  • He never eats or drinks at a wake.
  • He won't help carry a coffin and avoids the iron nails.
  • Insight DC 16: his grief is centuries older than he looks.
  • Mirror reflection: A knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths, helm under his arm, tears on his pale face.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Someone refuses his comfort and names him: "You're selling it, aren't you?" 2. His glimmer trade is threatened (the vats, the Syndicate couriers, or a dealer is attacked). 3. Someone grieves openly and honestly in front of him. Sorrow's Mercy compels him to stop pretending. 4. Cold iron, or a coffin nail pressed into his palm.

Read-aloud: The Friar's Armor. Brother Ash bows his head over the mourner's hands. "Let me take it away," he murmurs, "just for tonight." Then he looks up at you, and his face is full of an old and terrible tenderness. "No. You won't let me, will you?" The grey robe darkens and hardens; it is armor now, black plate grown over with thorns and inlaid with silver moths, and the petals of his cloak rise around him like ash in the wind. His lips glitter silver. "I am Sir Merrow Ashgrave," says the Sorrowkiss, setting down his helm. "And I am so very sorry for what I am about to do."

secrets.title: Guise: Amaranth as Notary Amar Thorne
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: A meticulous, soft-spoken notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows. They witness contracts, check wills, and explain fine print to frightened clients for very reasonable fees. Clients sometimes notice that the contract they signed is a little longer than they remember.
  • Tells:
  • They never lie, not even politely: "I can't say I love your hat, but it is certainly a hat."
  • The ink in their office blooms into tiny roses as it dries.
  • They refuse iron paperweights and use a polished river-stone instead.
  • Perception DC 14 in lamplight: the shadow of their head has antlers.
  • Everything smells faintly of roses and old paper.
  • Mirror reflection: An antlered herald in a dusk-colored coat, holding the vast red Book of Forfeit Names, and still smiling.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Dusk on Night 5. Amaranth reveals themself publicly, and with apologies, to begin collecting. 2. A PC signs anything Amaranth has notarized. 3. Someone finds a genuine loophole. Amaranth reveals themself out of sheer professional delight. 4. They are offered bread and salt as a guest. They must state their true name and nature before accepting.

Read-aloud: The Notary Closes the Ledger. Notary Thorne blots the last signature, examines it, and smiles that small, apologetic smile. "Thank you. That's everything in order." The lamps dim. The little office seems to grow taller, and so does the notary: antlers unfurl from their temples, threaded with roses; the drab clerk's coat flows into dusk-colored velvet embroidered with thorns. On the desk, the ledger swells into an enormous book bound in red leather, its pages whispering names. "I am Amaranth, Herald of the Dusk," they say gently. "Please don't be alarmed, darling. Everything you signed was perfectly legal. I made sure of it."

secrets.title: Guise: Queen Ilysse of the Hush as Madame Ilse Hush
secrets.html:
• Cover identity: A veiled, soft-voiced dream-reader who opened the Hush House in the Velvet Quarter this season. She reads dreams for a silver kiss and sells little blue bottles of sleep-tonic that give the sweetest dreams in Carnelia. Her clients sleep wonderfully, and some of them don't wake up for days.
  • Tells:
  • A powder like crushed moonlight on her fingertips and on the rim of every tonic bottle.
  • Candle flames lean toward her, and moths gather at her windows.
  • She speaks only in whispers, so clients must lean close.
  • She has iron candleholders replaced with glass.
  • Insight DC 16: she seems hungry when a client describes a beautiful dream.
  • Mirror reflection: Great wings of dusky violet and gold patterned like eyes, ink-dark eyes, and a gown spun from moonlight.
  • Triggers that drop the glamour: 1. Someone falls asleep in her presence. She cannot resist feeding, and the wings unfold. 2. A sudden gust of wind or a lantern thrust at her face. Moth instinct takes over. 3. Pipwhistle's dream-sugar trade is exposed in front of her. 4. A PC wins the Moth Waltz, or calls her by her true name and title.

Read-aloud: The Dream-Reader's Wings. Madame Hush leans across the little table, her veil stirring with each whispered word. "Tell me," she breathes, "what did you dream of last night?" Behind you, someone in the waiting room has nodded off, and the dream-reader's head turns toward them like a flower toward the sun. Her veil falls away. Behind her, two great shapes unfold and fill the room, wings of dusky violet and gold, each patterned with a staring eye. Every candle bends toward her. Silver dust drifts down like snow. "Forgive me," whispers Queen Ilysse of the Hush, and her eyes are pools of ink. "It has been such a long time since I had something sweet."

secrets.title: Branching & Endings (Part 7)
secrets.html:
The Shape of the Campaign

The mystery is a web, not a line. After the opening scene, the PCs choose where to go each night. Think of the campaign in three movements.

                         ACT I: THE BLACK KISS (Night 1)
              Murder at the Opera -> Warrant -> Question suspects at the scene
                                       |
        +------------------------------+-------------------------------+
        |                              |                               |
  THE CITY THREAD                THE COUNTRY THREAD            THE UNDERWORLD THREAD
  Sable Palazzo, Perfumery,      Side adventures 1-5           Drowned Market, Varo,
  Atelier, Crypt, Hall of Vows   (each = 1 night, 1 Keystone)  Hale, Saltgrave (Syndicate)
        |                              |                               |
        +---------------+--------------+---------------+---------------+
                        |                              |
              ACT II: THE UNRAVELLING (Nights 2-5)     |
          3+ Keystones -> confront Thessaly  <---------+
          Wrong accusation -> complications (see below)
                        |
              ACT III: THE SEVENTH BELL (Night 6-7)
          Council vote, Fae Duke's heralds, the choice of endings

Approach Orders (Three Sample Playthroughs)

  • The Detective's Road (city-first). Opera → Sable Palazzo (Riddle 1, journal) → Vos Perfumery (Riddle 3) → Atelier (suspicion) → Crypt (Riddle 4) → confront Thessaly on Night 4. Fast, cerebral, leaves time for one side adventure as the city burns.
  • The Rogue's Road (underworld-first). Flirt Varo into cooperating → Drowned Market (Riddle 5) → Saltgrave (blackmail archive) → Hale flips → Hall of Vows with Varo's key (Riddle 2). The PCs end up owing the Syndicate — or owning it.
  • The Wanderer's Road (country-first). Chase the vanished carpenter into the Thicketmoor → follow moth-dust to the Lanternwood → visit the Countess. The PCs arrive back in the city with allies, a witness, and two Keystones, but only two or three nights left.

If the PCs Accuse the Wrong Person

Accusation is a public act — made before the Opera Council and sealed with a kiss-oath by the accuser. A false accusation has consequences, but it doesn't end the game:

  • Seraphine is arrested; the Syndicate, fearing she'll talk, tries to assassinate her in her cell (Night +1). Saving her makes her a loyal ally.
  • Celestine is arrested; House Morrow withdraws its guard from the city and the Unravelling advances one extra step.
  • Hale is arrested; the Lantern Watch collapses and Lanternside riots (combat encounter).
  • Varo is arrested; he breaks out within a night and leaves the PCs a rude note — and the vault key.
  • In every case, Thessaly sends the PCs a gift: a beautiful mask, and a card reading "Well done, darlings." (She overplays her hand: the card smells of bloodrose — the false accusation itself becomes a clue.)

The Climax: The Seventh Bell

On the final night, the Opera Council convenes in the Velvet Opera to name a new Oathwarden before midnight. The Fae Duke's heralds attend, smiling. Candidates may include:

  • Thessaly / Isaveth — if her identity is proven, she is the rightful heir of founding blood.
  • Lady Celestine Morrow — House Morrow is also of founding blood (her ascension is legal but loveless; she'd do it to save the city).
  • The Syndicate's puppet — a minor noble bought by Mother Brine (or Lucan Vey, if he survived).
  • A PC — the Ledger can accept anyone who is freely kissed into office by a founding heir — a loophole the Veiled Sisters will reveal if asked (History DC 16 or a gift to the Hall).

Allies earned in side adventures show up here: ogres stomp in, sirens sing, a dragon lands on the Opera roof, the Countess casts her vote.

Possible Endings

Ending A — The Unmasking (Justice)

The PCs expose Thessaly before the Council with three or more Keystones. She does not deny it. The Ledger, sensing the truth, writes her true name across its blank pages in shining ink. She is arrested for murder — and in the same breath, legally recognized as Lady Isaveth Sable. Celestine (or another founding heir) is sworn in as Oathwarden. The city is saved, the law is upheld, and the PCs leave knowing that justice and fairness are not quite the same thing. Epilogue: Isaveth asks the PCs to visit her in the Tower of Penitence. She has made them each a mask.

Ending B — The Restored Name (Mercy)

The PCs gather the proof — and choose to present it not as a murder case, but as Aurelian's crime: the theft of a woman's identity through a corrupted oath. Under the Accord, a stolen vow voids everything built on it. With the Council's support (requires at least two allied votes: Countess Dusk, the blackmail archive, or Dame Ottoline), Isaveth is sworn in as Oathwarden. Her first act is to rewrite the Ledger so that no kiss-oath can ever take a person's self. Her second act, she insists, is to confess the murder publicly and accept exile to the Lanternwood once a successor is trained. Epilogue: the city wears no masks for one day each year: "Isaveth's Day."

Ending C — The Velvet Throne (Ambition)

The PCs seize the moment. With the vault key, the vow-page, and Thessaly's secret, they can force a bargain: a PC is kissed into the office of Oathwarden by a founding heir (Isaveth, Celestine, or — via blackmail — someone more reluctant who agrees to the deal; the kiss must still be freely given or the Ledger rejects it). The PC now controls every promise in Carnelia. Thessaly may be pardoned, exposed, or quietly sent away — the PC's choice. The Syndicate approaches with offers. The Fae Duke's heralds bow low and say, "We look forward to doing business with you." This ending opens a whole second campaign: ruling a city of secrets.

Ending D — The Seventh Bell Tolls (Failure)

If no Oathwarden is sworn by midnight on Night 7, the Accord fails. The Fae Duke arrives in a rain of rose petals and claims the founding bloodlines. Vesperine is drawn halfway into the Feywild — a city of eternal masquerade, where nobody can remove their mask. Not a game over: a dark new campaign begins, in which the PCs must journey into the Duke's court to win the city back.

handbook.title: Vesperine — Player Guide
handbook.lead: Everything the players may see: the content compass, the world of Carnelia, the City of Masks, maps, the opening scene, the session-zero checklist, names and rumors, and the faces you will meet.

sections.title: Content Compass
sections.html:
"In Vesperine, every promise is sealed with a kiss. Last night, one of those kisses killed a man."

Content compass: Mature fantasy intrigue — flirtation, seduction-as-strategy, scandal, vice, betrayal, and violence. Romance and sexual content are always suggestive, never explicit, and fade to black between consenting adults. Nothing romantic or sexual ever involves captives, coercion, or anyone underage. The ogress den is played as danger plus bawdy comedy, not titillation at a prisoner's expense. Use your table's preferred safety tools (Lines & Veils, an X-card, or a quick "too far? → cut to morning" agreement).

Recommended levels: Characters of levels 3–8. The central mystery works at any point in that range; the side adventures are tiered (see each one).

sections.title: The World: Carnelia
sections.html: Carnelia is a sun-drenched, wine-dark land of canals, vineyards, and old magic, ruled less by kings than by contracts. Five hundred years ago the founders of its greatest city struck a bargain with the Fae Duke of the Dusk — the Accord of Lips — which made any promise sealed with a kiss magically binding. The Accord made Carnelia rich: merchants, nobles, and lovers alike trust a kissed contract more than any gold. It also made Carnelia dangerous. A kiss here can be a love letter, a business deal, a marriage, a confession, a curse, or a death sentence.

sections.title: The Premise
sections.html:
Every kiss-oath sworn in Carnelia is recorded, in shimmering ink that writes itself, in the Ledger of Vows — a living book kept by a single magically appointed guardian, the Oathwarden. The Ledger is the spine of society: it settles disputes, proves marriages, enforces debts, and keeps the Fae Duke's ancient bargain intact.

At midnight on the Night of Unmasking — the final night of the city's month-long masquerade festival — the Oathwarden, Lord Aurelian Sable, was found dead in the Rosewater Gallery of the Velvet Opera, his lips stained black as ink, moments after kissing the city's most famous diva in front of a hundred masked witnesses.

Now the Ledger has no keeper. Each night that passes without a new Oathwarden, oaths begin to unravel. Marriages dissolve mid-dinner. Debts vanish — or double. Old curses wake. And on the seventh night, the Accord itself will fail, and the Fae Duke will come to collect what the city owes him.

The characters are handed a Red Ribbon Warrant — the Opera Council's sealed authority to question anyone, enter anywhere, and name the killer before the seventh bell.

sections.title: Tone & Themes
sections.html:
• Seductive intrigue. Flirtation is a weapon, a currency, and a lie detector. Everyone in Vesperine is flirting with someone, usually for a reason.
  • Masks and true faces. Who you pretend to be versus who you are — and what you'd give to be seen.
  • Promises and their price. A world where words literally bind makes every bargain a moral choice.
  • Decadence with teeth. Silk sheets, poisoned wine, velvet-gloved threats. Comedy and danger share the same bed (figuratively).
  • Consent matters here — in-world, too. The Accord of Lips cannot bind an unwilling kiss; a forced or stolen kiss creates no oath. This is a known, sacred law, and violators are reviled. (It's also a plot clue.)

sections.title: The Hub City: Vesperine, the City of Masks
sections.html:
Vesperine is built on a hundred islands knit together by bridges, gondola lanes, and gossip. Lanterns of colored glass hang over every canal, so the night city glows rose, amber, violet, and green. Masks are legal — even fashionable — everywhere, at all hours, and showing your bare face in a salon is considered either very brave or very forward.

At a glance
Population ~60,000 (humans, half-elves, tieflings, elves, halflings; a famous minority of satyrs and fauns in the theater district)
Government The Opera Council — seven patrons of the Velvet Opera who own most of the city's debt. Officially "advisory." Actually everything.
Law The Lantern Watch (underpaid, overdressed)
Currency Gold ducats and silver kisses (a coin stamped with lips — a joke that became official)
Notable vices Masquerades, card salons, wine of the Vinehold, dream-moth dust, duelling for love
What visitors notice The smell of rosewater and canal water; the music never stops; everyone touches your arm when they talk

Key districts of Vesperine

  1. The Gilded Crescent — Noble palazzos facing the Grand Canal. Balconies built for eavesdropping. Home of House Morrow and the shuttered Sable Palazzo.
  2. The Velvet Quarter — Theaters, salons, pleasure-gardens, and the Velvet Opera, a cathedral of red plush and gold leaf. The Rosewater Gallery (the murder scene) is on its second tier.
  3. Needle Row — Artisans' lanes: tailors, wigmakers, perfumers, and the Atelier of Madame Rook, the city's most beloved maskmaker.
  4. The Drowned Market — A half-sunken flea market under the old city, where the Thorn Syndicate sells anything, including secrets and people's debts.
  5. The Hall of Vows — A white-marble temple-library on its own island, where the Ledger of Vows rests on a lectern of living rose-thorn. Tended by the Veiled Sisters.
  6. Lanternside — Docks, taverns, sailors, and the Lantern Watch's leaning headquarters, "the Tilted House."

sections.title: The Velvet Marches: Surrounding Regions
sections.html:
Beyond the city stretch the Velvet Marches — the countryside Vesperine both depends on and pretends not to need.

Region Feel Who rules it Side adventure
The Thicketmoor Boggy forest of giant brambles, mud wallows, honey-wasps Nobody, officially. Unofficially, the ogresses of the Honeyhorn Clan The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons
The Lanternwood Night-forest where the trees glow; dream-moths, fey lights The Moth Court of Queen Ilysse The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court
The Saltgrave Coast Cliffs, shipwrecks, black-sand coves, sea caves The Drowned Choir (sirens) and smugglers The Song Beneath Saltgrave
The Duskvine Valley Terraced vineyards, sleepy villages, a château on the hill Countess Morwenna Dusk, vintner (and vampire) The Crimson Vintage
The Emberpeaks Volcanic hot springs, copper mines, sky-bridges The copper dragon Vexirra, "the Lonely Wyrm" A Hoard of Love Letters

sections.title: Pulled Through the Glass (read-aloud)
sections.html:
It's late. The room is quiet except for the hum of the ordinary world. You catch your reflection, in a mirror, a darkened window, a glass of something amber, and for a moment you don't recognize the face looking back. It looks like someone who never kept a promise. Then the reflection smiles, and you are not smiling.

[Gateway character's arrival — see "How they appear."]

The glass goes soft as warm wax. Cold silver closes over your fingers, your wrist, your heart. Every promise you ever whispered to a mirror plays back at once, in your own voice, a hundred times over. You fall upward through a forest of reflections: ballrooms, canals, candlelit faces in masks, a woman with a silver braid weeping over a hatbox, a man in midnight-blue falling and falling. Then rose-scented air, the roar of a crowd, and a floor of cool marble under your palms. Somewhere very close, a clock has stopped ticking. A voice in the dark says, almost fondly: "Ah. The oathless have arrived."

sections.title: Opening Scene
sections.html:
The Velvet Opera is a furnace of candlelight and perfume. A thousand masks turn toward the Rosewater balcony as the great clock above it — oddly silent tonight — is ignored in favor of the hand-bells. Midnight. The Oathwarden, Lord Aurelian Sable, sweeps the diva Seraphine Lark into his arms, and the whole house roars as their lips meet.

Then he staggers. His fingers claw at his golden mask. Black — black as spilled ink — spreads from beneath its edges, down his cheeks, across his lips. He falls. Someone screams "Poison!" and a hundred masked faces scatter like startled birds.

In the chaos, a tiny woman in crimson with a jeweled lorgnette taps your shoulder. "You," says Dame Ottoline Graves, "have no oaths in this city. How wonderfully useful. Come with me."

sections.title: Session Zero Checklist
sections.html:
• Confirm the content compass: suggestive, never explicit; fade to black; no captives, coercion, or minors in any romantic context.
  • Agree on Lines (never appears) and Veils (happens off-screen). Typical Veils for this campaign: graphic gore, torture.
  • Pick personal ties to suspects (Part 9).
  • Explain the fey etiquette rules to players (Part 6): never say "thank you," never give your full name, and refuse gifts graciously. Agree that enthralled characters cannot consent to romance.
  • If using the mirror prologue: each player writes the promise their character once made to their own reflection (Part 2), and you roll for the gateway character.
  • Decide: group, solo with GM, or GM-less solo.
  • Choose whether the Allure track is in use.

sections.title: Names & Rumors
sections.html:
Names: Benedetto Fiore (tenor), Allegra Vane (card-salon owner), Pim Gallowglass (gondolier), Sister Corvina (Veiled Sister), Teodor Graves (sleeping heir), Old Mother Brine (fence), Lorcan the Poet, Bel Okafor (first mate), Marta Ilic (innkeeper), Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand.

Rumors (d8): 1. "Aurelian was never really a Sable — I heard his grandmother sold eels." 2. "The diva poisoned him on the Syndicate's orders." 3. "The Countess of the Duskvine drinks the blood of virgins." 4. "Men are vanishing in the Thicketmoor and coming back fat and happy." 5. "Madame Rook has made Aurelian's mask every year for thirty years, and never charged him a coin." 6. "The Ledger is bleeding." 7. "A dragon is reading our mail." 8. "Captain Hale lost his own house in a card game."

End of guide. May all your oaths be kept — and all your masks come off at the right moment.

npcs_player.name: Lysander of the Silvered Glass
npcs_player.text: Tall and slender, with skin that carries a faint quicksilver sheen and hair like poured white silver tied back with a black ribbon. His eyes are polished steel that reflect you rather than having a color of their own. He wears a five-hundred-year-old doublet of silver brocade with a high lace collar, and he chimes faintly, like a wineglass, when he moves. Courtly, wistful, playful, and very lonely. He has watched every masquerade for five centuries and can describe each one, but he has not touched anyone in five hundred years.

npcs_player.name: Sabine Velour
npcs_player.text: A strikingly glamorous woman in her mid-fifties with warm brown skin, finger-waved black hair streaked with silver, and a long midnight-blue gown of beaded sequins with opera gloves to the elbow. She carries a jeweled cigarette holder she never lights and wears a single playing card, the Queen of Hearts, tucked into her beaded clutch. Her voice is smoke and honey. Worldly, warm, funny, and deeply homesick. She calls everyone "sugar" or "kid." Underneath the sparkle she carries thirty years of guilt.

npcs_player.name: Cael Rosier
npcs_player.text: A charming rose merchant and high-stakes gambler, a regular at The Blue Hour.
npcs_player.revealedText: Unearthly tall, with skin the soft violet of twilight, golden eyes, and graceful antlers twined with climbing red roses. He wears a long high-collared coat of rose-petal-red velvet stitched with thorns, a crown of briar, and an expression of permanent private amusement. He smells of summer nights. Languid, charming, mischievous, and very old.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Cael sighs, the way a man sighs when a card game has gone on too long, and sets down his glass. "I did so enjoy being ordinary," he says. Every rose in the room opens at once. The red coat lengthens into rose-petal velvet stitched with thorns; his skin deepens to the violet of the last minute before night; and from his dark curls rise antlers twined with climbing roses, brushing the chandelier, which chimes. His eyes are molten gold. "Prince Caelum of the Dusk," he says, bowing, "and still, I promise, your friend. I simply wasn't allowed to say so until now."

npcs_player.name: Marisol Tidewhisper
npcs_player.text: A merfolk siren who can take a two-legged shape on land. Sea-green scales shimmer along her cheekbones, collarbones, and forearms. Her long black hair is braided with sea-glass and tiny bells, and her eyes are the color of moonlit surf. She wears a fitted bodice of pearl and abalone shell, a sweeping wrap-skirt of sea-silk, and a gauzy sea-silk shawl. She is always slightly damp and grinning. Wild, reckless, gleefully rule-breaking, with a laugh like a breaking wave. She is impatient with old traditions and with her elders.

npcs_player.name: Sir Valentin Dusk
npcs_player.text: Pale as candle wax, with tousled raven hair, a small beauty mark beneath one heavy-lidded dark eye, and a rakish half-smile. He dresses in a black velvet coat with garnet buttons, a ruffled cravat, and gloves of oxblood leather. He is a vampire, so in mirrors he is invisible except for his clothes. Decadent, sardonic, romantic, and very tired of eternity. He is witty to the point of self-mockery and kinder than he pretends.

npcs_player.name: Seraphine Lark
npcs_player.text: Human, early 30s, a cascade of copper hair, emerald silk gown, a voice that could melt candle wax. Black-stained lips she refuses to wash ("Let them look"). Dramatic, quick-witted, exhausted by her own legend. Funny when she forgets to perform.

npcs_player.name: Lady Celestine Morrow
npcs_player.text: Half-elf, 28, platinum hair in a severe crown braid, ice-blue gown with a high collar, a single sapphire at her throat. Moves like a duelist. Cold, cutting, brilliant. Treats conversation as fencing and keeps score.

npcs_player.name: Captain Dorian Hale
npcs_player.text: Human, mid-40s, broad shoulders, a scar along his jaw, Lantern Watch coat with the top buttons perpetually undone. Smells of pipe smoke and rain. Tired, gruff, decent at heart, ashamed of what he's become. Dry humor.

npcs_player.name: Ezren Vos
npcs_player.text: Tiefling, 30s, lavender skin, gold rings on curling horns, a loose silk robe over an embroidered vest. Speaks softly and leans in close to smell you. Sensual, curious, theatrical, a little amoral, genuinely brilliant.

npcs_player.name: Varo Kestrel
npcs_player.text: Half-elf, late 20s, dark curls, crooked grin, a rose-thorn earring, a thorn-green domino mask. Dresses better than he can afford. Shameless, charming, cheerful even when caught. Loyal to his friends, nobody else.

npcs_player.name: Madame Thessaly Rook
npcs_player.text: Human, about 60, a long silver braid pinned with gold, laugh lines, magnificent dark eyes, fingertips flecked with gold leaf. Always a lavender shawl. Never wears a mask herself. Warm, wicked, hilarious, everybody's favorite aunt who has stories.

npcs_player.name: Lord Aurelian Sable
npcs_player.text: Age 58. Silver at the temples, a dimpled smile that has ended three marriages (none of them his), always in midnight-blue velvet. Aurelian was beloved in public — generous, witty, the best dancer at any ball — and feared in private, because the man who keeps the Ledger knows every promise everyone has ever broken. He was engaged to Lady Celestine Morrow, kept the diva Seraphine Lark as his "muse," and had held the office of Oathwarden for thirty years.

npcs_player.name: Dame Ottoline Graves
npcs_player.text: The Opera Council's spokesperson: an elderly, terrifyingly polite patron with a lorgnette.

npcs_player.name: Big Mother Hulga Tenderbone
npcs_player.text: Clan matriarch, 10 feet tall, braids woven with bones and dried roses, an apron reading (in crude Common) KISS THE COOK. Loud, sentimental, quick to weep and quicker to smash.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: Brunhilde "Bru"
npcs_player.text: Hulga's eldest daughter. Bodybuilder energy. Flirts by arm-wrestling and lifting people over her head. Respects anyone who beats her at anything.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: Little Gretch
npcs_player.text: The "small" one, only eight feet. Romantic, shy, reads stolen chapbook romances. Most likely to help the PCs.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: Granny Moss
npcs_player.text: Ancient, blind, sharp-tongued, the only one who remembers exactly what the hag said. Will trade information for gossip.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: Auntie Sallowmere
npcs_player.text: A green hag who lives beneath the bog. Petty, vain, hilarious, and still sulking after forty years.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: The Captives
npcs_player.text: Pell Ambrose (nervous, sweet), Rufus the carter (has accepted his fate and is enjoying the cake), Watchmen Dobbs and Pirelli (in denial), and Lorcan the poet (who's frankly having the time of his life and is technically a willing guest — he walked in on purpose).
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 1 · The Courting Moot of the Honeyhorn Matrons

npcs_player.name: Madame Ilse Hush
npcs_player.text: A veiled dream-reader who sells sleep-tonics at the Hush House in the Velvet Quarter.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 2 · The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court
npcs_player.revealedText: Wings of dusky violet and gold, eyes like wet ink, a gown that seems spun of moonlight. Speaks in a near-whisper so you must lean close. Seductive in the manner of something ancient and amused. Collects compliments, dances, and truths.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Madame Hush leans across the little table, her veil stirring with each whispered word. "Tell me," she breathes, "what did you dream of last night?" Behind you, someone in the waiting room has nodded off, and the dream-reader's head turns toward them like a flower toward the sun. Her veil falls away. Behind her, two great shapes unfold and fill the room, wings of dusky violet and gold, each patterned with a staring eye. Every candle bends toward her. Silver dust drifts down like snow. "Forgive me," whispers Queen Ilysse of the Hush, and her eyes are pools of ink. "It has been such a long time since I had something sweet."

npcs_player.name: Sir Fennic Ashwing
npcs_player.text: Her champion and consort, jealous, theatrical, a skilled duelist who challenges anyone the Queen smiles at.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 2 · The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court

npcs_player.name: The Dust-Maidens
npcs_player.text: Attendants who scatter sleep-pollen and giggle a lot.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 2 · The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court

npcs_player.name: Teodor Graves
npcs_player.text: A sleeping young nobleman wrapped in silk in the Library, dreaming of being a famous sailor.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 2 · The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court

npcs_player.name: Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa
npcs_player.text: Choir leader, silver-scaled, hair like kelp in moonlight, voice now a hoarse whisper. Proud, furious, irresistibly charismatic even voiceless.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 3 · The Song Beneath Saltgrave

npcs_player.name: Captain Morven "Saltlick" Kray
npcs_player.text: Human, one eye, tattooed knuckles reading SALT / LICK, a grin full of gold teeth. Flirts by insulting you.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 3 · The Song Beneath Saltgrave

npcs_player.name: Quill-Fin
npcs_player.text: A young merfolk siren who'll guide the PCs through the underwater ways in exchange for a kiss on the cheek (she's an adult and does this to everyone as a dare; it seals a small oath of guidance under the Accord).
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 3 · The Song Beneath Saltgrave

npcs_player.name: The Wreckers
npcs_player.text: Bandits and thugs with lanterns and hooked poles.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 3 · The Song Beneath Saltgrave

npcs_player.name: Countess Morwenna Dusk
npcs_player.text: Tall, raven-haired, gown of black and wine-red velvet, lips like a fresh cut. Witty, melancholy, devastatingly flirtatious in a slow, old-world way. She flirts with everyone but feeds only on the willing — and says so, crisply, to anyone who assumes otherwise.

npcs_player.name: Lucan Vey
npcs_player.text: Her steward. Handsome, golden, polite to a fault. Ambitious beyond reason.

npcs_player.name: Marta Ilic
npcs_player.text: A sharp-eyed village innkeeper whose son vanished; she's the PCs' contact.

npcs_player.name: The Donors
npcs_player.text: Well-dressed adults who attend the masquerade willingly and boast about it like a spa visit.

npcs_player.name: Vexirra
npcs_player.text: A young copper dragon with scales like a new penny, a talent for impressions, and terrible taste in jokes. Insists she is an "adult" dragon. Desperately romantic, prickly when embarrassed.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 5 · A Hoard of Love Letters

npcs_player.name: Scribbletail
npcs_player.text: The kobold chief poet. Writes appalling sonnets. Jealous of anyone the dragon likes.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 5 · A Hoard of Love Letters

npcs_player.name: Forewoman Brannagh Copperhand
npcs_player.text: Dwarven guild boss: grizzled, practical.
npcs_player.group: Side Adventure 5 · A Hoard of Love Letters

npcs_player.name: Pip Dewley
npcs_player.text: A bubbly, full-size barmaid at The Gilded Thimble tavern on Needle Row.
npcs_player.revealedText: A pixie the size of a hand, with dandelion-fluff hair, freckles of pollen, iridescent dragonfly wings, and a dress of overlapping rose petals with a thimble for a hat. She glows faintly pink when pleased and faintly green when plotting. Giddy, nosy, sentimental, and a compulsive collector of shiny buttons, gossip, and tiny promises.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Pip leans across the bar, beaming, a tray of steaming teacups balanced on one hand. "Now, sweet thing, a little kiss on the nose for luck, and you'll owe me just one teensy song—" Someone drops a pouch of shiny brass buttons on the counter. Pip's eyes go enormous. There is a sound like a cork leaving a bottle, a puff of pink glitter, and the teacups crash down onto an empty floor. Something the size of your hand zips up out of the wreckage on dragonfly wings, clutching a button like a shield, glowing bright, delighted pink. "Ohhh, those are lovely," squeaks Pipwhistle Dewlace. "Oops. Um. Surprise?"

npcs_player.name: Dina Mire
npcs_player.text: A laughing bath-attendant at the Lilywater Baths in Lanternside.
npcs_player.revealedText: A river nymph with green-gold skin, long hair the color of wet willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, and dark eyes that ripple. She wears a flowing gown of layered green silk that seems to drip without ever soaking anything, plus a necklace of river-pearls. Frogs sing when she laughs. Teasing, sunny, petty, and timeless. She forgets that mortals age.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Dina is mid-giggle, a braid of somebody's hair half-finished in her fingers, when the bucket of cold water hits her. She shrieks, and the shriek turns into a laugh like a brook in spring. The freckles slide off her like wet paint. Her skin is green-gold now, her hair a cascade of willow leaves threaded with water-lilies, her eyes dark and rippling. Every frog in the drains begins to sing. "Well, that was rude," says Ondine Mirewillow, wringing out a lily. "And I was being so good. Mostly. Does anyone want their shoes back?"

npcs_player.name: Master Orrin Mintleaf
npcs_player.text: Dance master and fiddler who leads the revel-band at the Velvet Opera's after-parties.
npcs_player.revealedText: A handsome satyr with curling ram's horns gilded at the tips, chestnut curls, a goatee, and twinkling amber eyes. He wears an open-throated poet's shirt under a waistcoat of patchwork velvet and carries panpipes on a ribbon. He has goat legs, of course, and he dances on them as if they were a happy accident.
npcs_player.revealTitle: The Dance Master Kicks Off His Boots
npcs_player.revealHTML: The music is too good to stop. Master Mintleaf whoops, kicks one boot clean across the ballroom, then the other, and his hat goes sailing after them. Where his feet should be, polished hooves strike sparks from the marble. Gilded ram's horns curl from his chestnut hair; his trousers are suddenly fur from the hips down. The dancers scream, then laugh, then don't stop dancing. "No point hiding it now!" bellows Rillo Fennamint, pipes at his lips. "Who's coming to the after-party? The forest's only a short walk, and the moon's out!"

npcs_player.name: Madame Noor Vesperelle
npcs_player.text: A wealthy foreign widow who hosts the Black Fan, the most exclusive masked salon in the Gilded Crescent.
npcs_player.revealedText: Impossibly beautiful in a way that is slightly wrong: no two witnesses describe her the same way. Her true form, revealed under true seeing, a broken glamour, or the Oathless Glass, has bone-white skin, black lips, eyes like starless night, and black hair woven with dead roses. She wears a high-collared gown of black velvet and spider-silk lace, long gloves, and a choker set with a single dark sapphire. Patient, elegant, cruel in the gentlest possible voice. She enjoys being adored but cares only about control.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Madame Vesperelle laughs, that low, warm laugh that has made half of Vesperine fall in love with her, and snaps her black lace fan shut. "Darling," she says, "you've been looking at the wrong face all evening." Behind her, the crepe slithers from the great mirror like a shed skin. In the glass stands someone else: skin white as a bone in moonlight, lips black as Ledger ink, eyes with no stars in them at all. The candles gutter. When you turn back from the mirror, the widow is gone and only the other one remains, smiling exactly the same smile. "There," says Lady Nocturne Vesh. "Isn't that better? Now we can stop pretending you weren't already mine."

npcs_player.name: Brother Ash
npcs_player.text: A grey-robed mourning friar who sits with the grieving at Lanternside wakes.
npcs_player.revealedText: A tall, sorrowful, beautiful knight in black thorned plate inlaid with silver moths. He keeps his helm under his arm to show a pale face, grey eyes that always seem about to cry, and silver hair. A cloak of grey petals sheds and regrows as he walks, and his lips are dusted faintly with silver glimmer. Melancholy, courteous, and honest about being a monster. He believes he offers mercy: relief from pain.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Brother Ash bows his head over the mourner's hands. "Let me take it away," he murmurs, "just for tonight." Then he looks up at you, and his face is full of an old and terrible tenderness. "No. You won't let me, will you?" The grey robe darkens and hardens; it is armor now, black plate grown over with thorns and inlaid with silver moths, and the petals of his cloak rise around him like ash in the wind. His lips glitter silver. "I am Sir Merrow Ashgrave," says the Sorrowkiss, setting down his helm. "And I am so very sorry for what I am about to do."

npcs_player.name: Notary Amar Thorne
npcs_player.text: A soft-spoken contract notary with a tiny office on the bridge to the Hall of Vows.
npcs_player.revealedText: Androgynous and serene, with elegant antlers threaded with roses and a long, high-collared, dusk-colored coat embroidered with thorns. They carry an enormous book bound in red leather, the Book of Forfeit Names, and they always smile, even when sad. Polite, punctilious, and almost apologetic. A bureaucrat of doom with impeccable manners.
npcs_player.revealHTML: Notary Thorne blots the last signature, examines it, and smiles that small, apologetic smile. "Thank you. That's everything in order." The lamps dim. The little office seems to grow taller, and so does the notary: antlers unfurl from their temples, threaded with roses; the drab clerk's coat flows into dusk-colored velvet embroidered with thorns. On the desk, the ledger swells into an enormous book bound in red leather, its pages whispering names. "I am Amaranth, Herald of the Dusk," they say gently. "Please don't be alarmed, darling. Everything you signed was perfectly legal. I made sure of it."

solo.title: Through the Oathless Glass
solo.subtitle: Five Solo Entry Adventures for Vesperine & the Velvet Marches (D&D 2024 rules, levels 1–3)

intro.html: Everyone has kissed a mirror once. Tonight, one of them kisses back.

intro.title: How to Use This Book
intro.html:
These are five solo gamebook adventures, one for each gateway character of the Oathless Glass (world guide, Part 2). Each pulls a single adventurer out of their own world, through a mirror, and into Carnelia on the Night of Unmasking, the night Lord Aurelian Sable dies. Each one ends by handing your character into the main murder mystery (The Black Kiss) or into that gateway character's side adventure, carrying a clue, an ally, or a complication.

Pick your door. Choose the gateway character who intrigues you most, or roll a d6: 1 Lysander, 2 Sabine, 3 Caelum, 4 Marisol, 5 Valentin, 6 the Glass chooses (roll again, and start with one Anchor already owed to that character).

Content compass. These adventures are flirtatious and full of intrigue: suggestive, never explicit. Romance between consenting adults fades to black. A character under enthrallment (stage 2+) can't consent, and the Accord itself voids any vow sealed that way. Anything that crosses your personal lines can simply be skipped.

intro.title: What You Need
intro.html:
• A 1st- to 3rd-level character (any class), dice, and a notebook.
  • The world guide's Allure track (Part 8) and Enthrallment track (Part 6). A quick reference is below.
  • A Glass Sheet: write down your Mirror-Promise, Allure (0–4) with your gateway character, Enthrallment (0–5, per fey), Anchors (kiss-bound promises you've made), Clues, and Favors.

intro.title: Reading the Gamebook
intro.html: Each mission is a set of numbered scenes. Read a scene, make your choice, and follow the link, for example → go to 4. Ability checks list DCs as L1 / L2–3 where they scale. Combat stat blocks are 5e SRD creatures, scaled for one hero (see below).

intro.title: Quick Reference: Allure & Enthrallment
intro.html:
Track 1 2 3 4
Allure (their feelings for you) Intrigued: one honest answer Charmed: reveals a secret if asked Smitten: volunteers help Devoted: an ally who takes risks for you; romance possible (fade to black)
Enthrallment (their hold on you) Smitten: you daydream of them Beguiled: can't consent; disadvantage on Insight vs. them Enthralled: charmed; follow one suggestion a day Bound: forged vows (stage 5, Nameless, can't happen in these entry adventures)

Resist-or-yield scenes are marked 🌹. Each offers a temptation. Yield and you usually gain something (Allure, a gift, a boon) at the price of Enthrallment or an Anchor. Resist and you keep your head, but the moment may pass. Neither choice is wrong. Counter-charms from Part 6 work here: cold iron, refusing gifts graciously three times, never saying "thank you," and cold water.

intro.title: Solo Rules for the Entry Adventures
intro.html:
The Oracle (d20). When you're unsure what happens, ask a yes/no question and roll: 1–3 No, and… · 4–8 No · 9–11 No, but… · 12–14 Yes, but… · 15–18 Yes · 19–20 Yes, and… Shift the result by ±3 for likely or unlikely questions. Each adventure adds its own d6 oracle prompts for colour.

Gateway Aid. Your gateway character can help you three times per adventure (each adventure says how they help). Mark a box each time. Some aid costs Allure or adds an Anchor, as noted.

Scaling for one hero.

Your level Enemy hit points Enemy numbers Extras
1 Halve non-boss HP 1 enemy per listed "slot" Gateway Aid can also heal 1d8 + 2 once
2 ¾ HP As listed —
3 Full HP Add 1 minion to the largest fight Hero's Surge: once per combat, take an extra action

Death's Door. When you drop to 0 HP, you may instead stay at 1 HP and take a Scar (a lasting complication noted in each adventure's consequence table). Once per adventure.

Arrival ties. Whichever door you choose, you arrive on Night 1. Your entry adventure takes most of that night, and the Unravelling clock (world guide, Part 4) starts at dawn.

intro.title: Mirror-Promise Prompts (d12)
intro.html:
Before you begin, decide (or roll) what your character once promised their reflection. The Glass heard it.

d12 "I promised my reflection…"
1 "…that I'd stop being afraid of being seen."
2 "…that I'd find someone who'd choose me first."
3 "…that I would never go back to them."
4 "…that I'd finally do something brave."
5 "…that I'd find out the truth about what happened."
6 "…that I'd stop pretending to be someone I'm not."
7 "…that I'd make them pay."
8 "…that I'd go somewhere nobody knows my name."
9 "…that I'd forgive myself."
10 "…that I'd fall in love properly, just once."
11 "…that I'd protect someone who couldn't protect themselves."
12 "…that I'd stop wasting my life."

Your promise matters at the end of every adventure. Keeping it is part of the way home (world guide, Part 2).

adventures.title: The Glass Remembers

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
You live an ordinary life somewhere that is not Carnelia. Roll or choose:

d6 Your life tonight
1 Closing up an antique shop alone. The oldest mirror in the back has been fogging from the inside.
2 Getting ready for a party you don't want to go to, staring at yourself in the hallway mirror.
3 Home late after a breakup, brushing your teeth, refusing to cry at your own face.
4 Working a night shift; the restroom mirror flickers under the bad lighting.
5 Packing to leave a life you've outgrown, with one last look in the dressing-table glass.
6 Sleepless at 3 a.m., talking to your reflection the way you did as a teenager.

The call. You whisper your Mirror-Promise to the glass again, maybe without meaning to. This time your reflection smiles before you do.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html: Your reflection smiles, slowly and fondly, the way someone smiles at an old friend. Then it steps aside, and someone else is standing behind you in the glass: a tall man with skin like moonlight on water, white-silver hair tied with a black ribbon, a doublet of silver brocade five hundred years out of fashion. His eyes are polished steel, and in them you see yourself, very small. "Forgive the intrusion," he says, and his voice echoes as if from the end of a long hall. "A man is about to die, and I need someone who can't be accused of loving or hating him. You'll do beautifully." He holds out his hand. When you touch the glass, it is warm. Then cold. Then gone. You fall upward through a thousand candlelit reflections, and land on your hands and knees on marble that smells of roses, just as a hundred masked strangers begin to scream.

sections.title: Meeting Lysander
sections.html:
• His approach: He mirrors you, copying your posture, your accent, the way you push your hair back, and tells you exactly what you need to hear: "You've always been braver than you let yourself be." He speaks from any reflective surface nearby: mirrors, windows, a polished goblet, a pool of spilled wine.
  • What he offers: Guidance out of a very dangerous room, his eyewitness memory of the murder, and five hundred years of knowledge about Vesperine.
  • What he hides: He was trapped in the Glass by a kiss-sealed promise to his lover, Lady Oriane Sable. He can only leave if someone honestly agrees to trade places with him, and he's been rehearsing ways to ask. He also knows the killer is of Oriane's blood, and he's not sure he wants her caught.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • Reflected Warning: reroll one failed Perception or Insight check.
  • Mirror Step: in a room with mirrors, teleport 30 feet between two reflective surfaces.
  • Glass Shield: impose disadvantage on one attack against you.

The third use costs 1 Allure, because he finds it frightening to care.

Oracle prompts (d6), to ask whenever you're stuck:

  1. Is a guard looking your way?
  2. Did Lysander see this happen, too?
  3. Is there a mirror within reach?
  4. Does someone recognize you as "the stranger from the mirror"?
  5. Is Madame Rook nearby?
  6. Has the Watch noticed the body's been moved?

sections.title: The Entry Mission: Out of the Gallery, Into the Truth
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: The Witness. You walk into The Black Kiss already holding a Keystone clue and Lysander's trust (Allure 2+). He can speak to you through any mirror in the city, once per night, for the rest of the campaign. Complication: Thessaly knows the mirror-stranger was in the Gallery. If you wore her mask, she knows everything you've said.

Ending B: A Night in the Glass. You spend Night 1 as a reflection, watching Vesperine from every mirror. Lysander spends it as a man: he weeps at sunrise, eats a peach, and kisses your reflection's hand. At dawn the Glass trades you back, as the honest bargain promised. You gain Lysander, Devoted (Allure 4), and you can scry through any one mirror per day, as he can. You also saw something from inside the mirrors in Needle Row: Madame Rook, weeping over an old wedding mask (a strong lead). Complication: advance the Unravelling clock by one step; the city went a night without its judge.

Ending C: The Kept Secret. You enter the mystery without the testimony, but with Lysander's devotion and a burning hint about the clock (the gallery clock's riddle, Riddle 6, is your best first lead). Lysander will lie for you once to anyone who questions you near a mirror. Complication: if you later accuse Thessaly without telling him first, he'll feel betrayed (–2 Allure).

sections.title: Rewards & Consequences
sections.html:
Result Effect in the campaign
Clue: The Cut Ribbon Counts as the "Original Mask" Keystone in The Black Kiss.
Clue: The Vow Page Points straight to the Drowned Market and Mother Brine.
Clue: Rook's Pause / Thorn Card Advantage on your first Insight check against Thessaly / an easy introduction to the Syndicate.
Vault Key Opens the Vault of Broken Vows in the Hall of Vows (Riddle 2 still applies).
Favor: Hale or Varo One free "under pressure" reveal from that suspect.
Anchor: "Walk Beside Me" Must be honestly resolved before you can go home.
Listening Mask (worn) Thessaly hears what you hear until you discover it (Arcana DC 16, or Ezren Vos).
Scar: Suspect The Lantern Watch has your description; disadvantage on Charisma checks with Watchmen until cleared.

entries.title: The Rosewater Gallery
entries.html:
Chaos. A silver-haired man in midnight-blue lies dead beside a velvet chaise, black ink staining his lips. A copper-haired diva in emerald stares at her own hands. Watchmen with lanterns are sealing the doors. A woman points at you: "That one came out of the mirror!" Behind you, Lysander's reflection whispers: "The mirror wall has a door. Or you could be bold."

  • To stand your ground and declare yourself a witness: → go to 2.
  • To slip through the secret door behind the mirror wall: → go to 3.
  • To vanish into the panicking crowd: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 11 / 13. Success → go to 4. Failure → go to 2.

entries.title: Captain Hale's Questions
entries.html:
A scarred captain with his coat half-unbuttoned steers you into an alcove. "Captain Hale, Lantern Watch. You fell out of a mirror, friend. Talk." He's exhausted, frightened, and hiding something (Insight DC 12: he keeps glancing at the Dressing Gallery corridor he left unguarded).

  • Tell the plain truth (Persuasion DC 12 / 14; advantage if you mention his empty corridor, which rattles him). Success: he lets you go with a warning and a whispered "Find me if you learn anything." Note Favor: Hale. → go to 5.
  • Lie smoothly (Deception DC 14 / 15). Success → go to 5. Failure: he locks you in the Dressing Gallery under guard ("until I decide what you are") → go to 3.
  • Flirt to disarm him: he's flustered but not stupid. Charisma (Persuasion) DC 13. Success: +1 Allure with Hale (track him separately) and → go to 5. Failure → go to 3.
