entries.title: The Dressing Gallery 🌹
entries.html:
Racks of costumes, wig-stands, and a long table covered in feathers and gold leaf. A silver-haired woman in a lavender shawl is calming weeping chorus girls. She turns, and her face lights up. "Oh, darling, you poor thing, you're white as a sheet. Madame Rook. I make the masks." She presses a cup of warm wine into your hands, adjusts your collar, calls you "pet," and is wonderful company. Then she offers you a gift: an exquisite half-mask of midnight lace. "For you. You'll need to blend in tonight."

Resist or yield:

  • Yield: accept the mask. +1 Allure with Thessaly, and you'll pass for a guest anywhere in the Opera (advantage on Stealth here). Secretly it's a listening mask: she hears everything you hear while you wear it. Note it.
  • Resist: decline graciously (Charisma DC 12; three polite refusals and she laughs and stops offering). She approves, a little warily.

Either way, while she fusses, you notice a costume trunk that's been disturbed (Investigation DC 11 / 13).

  • If you search the trunk: you find a golden festival mask whose ribbon has been cut clean, not frayed (the original mask of the dead man). Gain Clue: The Cut Ribbon. Lysander's reflection, in a dressing mirror, goes very still. → go to 5.
  • If you ask Madame Rook where she was at quarter to midnight: "Right here, darling, all evening." Insight DC 15 / 16: a flicker of something grieving and fierce. Gain Clue: Rook's Pause. → go to 5.
  • If you hear running footsteps above: → go to 4.

entries.title: The Catwalks (Chase)
entries.html:
A half-elf in a thorn-green domino mask sprints across the rigging high above the stage, a ring of keys in his fist. He sees you and grins. "Oh, you're the mirror one. Lovely. Can't stop!" Two stagehands-turned-Syndicate-heavies (thugs: one slot at L1, two at L2–3) come after both of you.

Chase rules (solo): Run three rounds. Each round, pick one: Dash (Athletics DC 12), Swing on a rope (Acrobatics DC 13), or Drop a sandbag on a pursuer (Dexterity attack, +4 if proficient; it deals 2d6 bludgeoning). Two successes and you catch Varo on the roof. Two failures and the thugs corner you: fight them (thug, scaled), then continue.

  • Caught Varo: → go to 6.
  • Lost him: Varo is gone, but he dropped a playing card stamped with a thorn (the Syndicate's sign). Gain Clue: Thorn Card. → go to 5.

entries.title: The Glass Door Riddle
entries.html:
You find yourself before the great central pane of the mirror wall, the Oathless Glass. Lysander presses his palm to the inside. "There's a way through the reflections, where no Watchman can follow. But the Glass only opens for those who understand it." Words of light write themselves across the surface:

I show you the world, but I keep none of it;
I give you your face, but I've never worn it.
Look into me and I look back true —
I am you, and I am not you.

  • Answer "a mirror" or "a reflection": the glass softens like warm wax. → go to 7.
  • Wrong or no answer: Lysander sighs, then helps (uses 1 Gateway Aid, or roll Intelligence DC 12 for a hint: "What are you standing in front of?"). If you still can't answer, the Watch arrives and you must talk your way out (Persuasion DC 13 / 15; failure means a night in a cell: the Suspect Scar). → go to 8.

entries.title: Rooftop Bargain (Combat or Talk)
entries.html:
On the Opera roof, above a sea of colored lanterns, Varo is cornered against a gargoyle, twirling a brass key. "Fine, you caught me. I nicked the Oathwarden's vault key from his coat. Didn't kill anyone. Ask the man in the mirror if you don't believe me."

  • Fight him (bandit stats at L1; spy at L2–3). If you win, take the Vault Key. Varo escapes over the rooftops, cursing you fondly. → go to 5.
  • Bargain (Persuasion DC 12 / 13): he trades information for silence: "Six months back I stole an old wedding-vow page from Sable's desk. Aurel Fenn and Isaveth Sable. Sold it in the Drowned Market. Some lady in a grey veil bought it." Gain Clue: The Vow Page and Favor: Varo. → go to 5.
  • Let him go with a wink and a "you owe me": +1 Allure with Varo, and he slips you the thorn card. Gain Clue: Thorn Card. → go to 5.

entries.title: Inside the Glass 🌹 (Moral Choice)
entries.html:
You step into a world of silver: endless corridors of reflections, every masquerade the Opera has ever held, frozen and shining. Lysander walks beside you, fully real for the first time. He takes your hand, and his fingers are cool and trembling. "Five hundred years," he says softly. "You're the first warm thing I've touched."

Resist or yield: He stops before a mirror showing a moonlit balcony. "Would you let me walk beside you, just once, out there? Say yes and I'll show you everything I saw tonight."

  • Yield: say yes without asking what it means. +1 Allure. Note Anchor: "Walk Beside Me." (It's ambiguous: the Glass reads it as a possible place-trade. Because you didn't understand, the Glass will refuse any actual swap, but Lysander will ask again, honestly, someday.)
  • Resist: ask exactly what "walk beside you" means. He flushes silver and tells you the truth: he means trading places. +1 Allure anyway, for honesty. No Anchor.

Then he shows you the memory: at 11:47, through the secret door, a silver braid, a lavender shawl, a golden mask swapped in a heartbeat, a clock pendulum knocked still. Madame Rook. "She has Oriane's eyes," he whispers. "She is the last of the house I swore to protect. Must you tell them?"

The moral choice:

  • Promise to tell the truth, whatever it costs her. Gain Keystone Clue: Lysander's Testimony (it counts as one of the three Keystones for the accusation). Lysander grieves, but respects you. → go to 8 and take Ending A.
  • Promise to keep his secret, and find another way to the truth. +1 Allure (he's Smitten). Gain Clue: "Ask about the clock." → go to 8 and take Ending C.
  • Offer to trade places honestly, for one night, so he can see the city. The Glass accepts an honest offer. → go to 8 and take Ending B.

entries.title: Through the Looking-Glass and Out
entries.html: Wherever you came from, you step out of a tall mirror into a quiet corridor of the Opera as dawn grays the windows. Dame Ottoline Graves, tiny, terrifying, crimson-gowned, is waiting with a lorgnette. "There you are. The oathless one. Come along. You have a murder to solve and a city to save." Choose your ending below (or, if no ending was assigned, take Ending A if you hold two or more Clues and Ending C otherwise).

adventures.pitch:
Pitch: You tumble out of a mirror into a murder scene ten seconds after the victim drops. A silver man who lives in the glass is the only witness, and he'll only tell what he saw if you promise to set him free.

Leads into: The Black Kiss (main mystery), right at the scene of the crime.

adventures.title: The Blue Hour

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
d6 Your life tonight
1 Last call at a dive bar. A song you haven't heard since childhood starts playing, with no jukebox in sight.
2 Playing poker with friends. You keep drawing the Queen of Hearts.
3 Home with a glass of wine and an old record, dancing alone in the dark.
4 Waiting tables at a lounge; the mirror behind the bar shows a crowd that isn't there.
5 On the late train, your face in the dark window, someone singing in the reflection.
6 At a wedding reception, hiding in the restroom from people who ask when you'll settle down.

The call. You catch your reflection and murmur your Mirror-Promise. A trumpet answers, faint and far away, and then a woman's voice, singing your song.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html: The song gets louder until it fills your head: a smoky, honeyed voice wrapping itself around a melody from your own world, a song nobody in this room should know. In the glass, the room behind you has changed. Blue light. Cigarette smoke curling through it. A woman in midnight sequins leans on a grand piano, silver streaks in her finger-waved hair, opera gloves to the elbow. She looks straight at you and lifts one gloved hand out of the mirror, holding a playing card between two fingers: the Queen of Hearts. "Pick a card, sugar," she says. "Any card. They all go to the same place." You take it. The glass ripples like a curtain, and you step through into blue smoke, piano music, and the clink of chips, while somewhere far away a hundred people begin to scream.

sections.title: Meeting Sabine
sections.html:
• Her approach: Old-world glamour. She pours you something amber, calls you "kid," and asks greedily about home: songs, slang, what coffee tastes like now. She dances you three steps across the floor before you know what's happening.
  • What she offers: Shelter, a drink, a crash course in Vesperine, and a seat at her table.
  • What she hides: Thirty years ago she was the last oathless judge, and she endorsed the Oathwarden who just died. She owes the Thorn Syndicate a fortune. Tonight she promised to deliver you to Mother Brine's collector, Gristle Pike, in exchange for a ticket home. She is hating herself for it.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • House Always Wins: force one reroll of an enemy's attack or check.
  • Torch Song: one enemy within 30 feet makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or is charmed until the end of its next turn.
  • Card Up the Sleeve: advantage on one Sleight of Hand or Deception check.

Oracle prompts (d6):

  1. Is Gristle Pike already here?
  2. Is anyone at the table cheating besides Sabine?
  3. Does Sabine glance at the clock?
  4. Is the Watch outside?
  5. Does someone recognize you're "oathless" (your lagging reflection)?
  6. Is the shard in Sabine's clutch right now?

sections.title: The Entry Mission: A Hand of Hearts
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: Absolution. You keep the Queen's Shard, and with it, once per day, you can scry through any mirror in Vesperine for 1 minute. Sabine becomes your ally (Allure 2+) and introduces you to Varo Kestrel, who owes her a favor (he gives up the vow-page lead at once: "Aurel Fenn and Isaveth Sable, sold to a grey-veiled lady"). Complication: the Syndicate wants the shard, and Gristle Pike (if he lived) is hunting you.

Ending B: The Syndicate's Ticket. Sabine is free of debt and grateful, but guilty. Mother Brine now holds a shard and will try to decide who passes through the Glass on Night 7. Sabine, ashamed, becomes your informant inside the Syndicate: once per night she'll tell you one true thing Brine is planning. Complication: on Night 7, Brine can block one person from going home unless you recover the shard.

Ending C: Burned Bridges. You escape the market with Sabine and the shard, but Brine's guards saw your faces, so the Thorn Syndicate is openly hostile (Varo is told to avoid you, and Hale is ordered to arrest you on sight). Sabine hides in your company. She is a constant, fragile companion, and she gives you a Torch Song use every long rest. Complication: start The Black Kiss with the Hunted Scar.

sections.title: Rewards & Consequences
sections.html:
Result Effect in the campaign
The Queen's Shard Scry through any Vesperine mirror 1/day. A Glass shard (reveals fey true forms; part of the way home).
Hale's Marker Hale cooperates fully ("under pressure" reveals for free).
Clue: Debtors' Page Proves Hale's Syndicate debt. Leads to Mother Brine's books.
Clue: Brine Wants the Shard Advance warning of the Syndicate's Night 7 plan.
Anchor: Cael's Favor Prince Caelum (in disguise) is owed a small favor. He'll collect at the worst moment.
Anchor: Sabine's Luck You owe Sabine one honest favor before going home.
Brine's Grudge The Syndicate raises its price for everything and sends an assassin on Night 3.
Scar: Hunted Syndicate heavies appear in one scene per night (oracle: "Are they here?").

entries.title: The Back Room 🌹
entries.html:
The Blue Hour's back room: velvet booths, a piano, a mirror in a gilded frame. Sabine sits close, her knee almost touching yours, and asks you to describe the last song you danced to. Then, quietly: "A man's coming for you tonight, kid. I made a promise I shouldn't have. Play along, and I'll get you out the other side."

Resist or yield: She takes your hand. "Sing me something from home first. Please. Just a verse."

  • Yield: sing, or describe a song lovingly. (Performance DC 10, or automatic if you, the player, actually hum or quote a song.) +1 Allure. She closes her eyes and, for a moment, looks thirty years younger.
  • Resist: "Who's coming, and why?" Insight DC 12: she's ashamed, not cruel. You learn Gristle Pike works for Mother Brine. She smiles ruefully. No Allure, but no illusions either.

Then:

  • To play along and join her card game while she stalls: → go to 2.
  • To refuse and slip out the kitchen before Gristle arrives: → go to 3.
  • To demand she tell you everything: Persuasion DC 13 / 14. Success: she confesses the deal and asks you to help her break it. Gain +1 Allure and → go to 4. Failure: she clams up, so → go to 2.

entries.title: The High-Stakes Table
entries.html:
At the green-baize table sit a scarred Watch captain drinking too fast (Captain Hale), a dazzling rose merchant in red velvet (Cael Rosier, really Prince Caelum in disguise; Insight DC 17 to sense he's more than he seems), and a sweating noble. Hale is about to bet his marker, a signed IOU to the Syndicate.

The game: Play three hands. Each hand, choose Play Straight (Wisdom (Insight) DC 13: read the table) or Cheat (Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) DC 14; Sabine can help with Card Up the Sleeve). Win two of three hands to take the pot, including Hale's Marker. If you're caught cheating (a failed Cheat roll), the noble shouts. Cael Rosier laughs delightedly, says "Oh, well done," and smooths it over, and you now owe him a small favor (note Anchor: Cael's Favor).

  • Afterward, Cael leans close and murmurs: "You don't belong here. How marvelous. Never thank me." (If you say "thank you" anyway, gain 1 Enthrallment with Caelum.)
  • Then the door opens on a huge man with a hook for a hand: Gristle Pike. → go to 5.
entries.imgAlt: Prince Caelum in his guise as Cael Rosier

entries.title: The Kitchen and the Canal
entries.html:
You slip past steaming pots and a startled cook into a moonlit alley that ends at a canal. A gondola bobs there, untended. Behind you, heavy boots and a voice like gravel: "There's the goods. Get 'em."

  • To take the gondola: → go to 5 (start the chase with one success already).
  • To hide and wait (Stealth DC 13 / 14): success, and you overhear Gristle saying "Brine wants the singer's mirror and the mark. Both or neither." Gain Clue: Brine Wants the Shard, and → go to 4. Failure → go to 5.

entries.title: Sabine's Safe (Riddle)
entries.html:
Sabine leads you to her dressing room upstairs. Behind a painting of a city with lights you recognize (your world, painted from memory) sits a small safe with a brass dial engraved with card suits. "I set the riddle myself, years ago, so I'd never forget why I came here," she says. "I'm too nervous to think straight. You do it."

I've a face but no head, a crown but no throne;
I've lovers and fools and a king of my own.
Shuffle my fortunes, I'll never complain —
and fifty-one sisters will share in my reign.

  • Answer "a playing card" (or "a deck of cards"; "the Queen of Hearts" earns a smile and +1 Allure): the safe clicks open. Inside lies a small silver hand-mirror, a shard of the Oathless Glass. Sabine presses it into your hands. "If I give it to Brine, the Syndicate decides who goes home. Keep it for me tonight." Gain The Queen's Shard. → go to 6.
  • If you can't solve it, Sabine opens it herself with shaking hands, but Gristle's men are on the stairs: → go to 5, then 6.

entries.title: Chase Through the Drowned Market
entries.html:
Gristle Pike and his crew (thugs: one slot at L1, two at L2–3; Gristle himself is a bandit captain at L3 only, or a thug with 40 HP at L1–2) pursue you down the Gull Steps into the half-sunken market: lantern-lit stalls on stilts, ankle-deep water, traders shrieking.

Chase (three rounds). Each round choose:

  • Leap stalls (Acrobatics DC 12)
  • Shove through the crowd (Athletics DC 13)
  • Topple a stall of glass bottles into their path (Dexterity DC 12; the pursuers lose a round)
  • Sabine sings (spend a Gateway Aid: automatic success)

Two successes: you lose them, and you can → go to 6. Two failures: Gristle corners you, so fight (scaled). If you win, he gasps "Brine'll have your eyes for this" and drops a ledger page listing Syndicate debtors, including Capt. D. Hale, 2,000 ducats. Gain Clue: Debtors' Page. → go to 6.

entries.title: Mother Brine's Offer (Moral Choice)
entries.html:
All roads lead to a stall called Things That Shouldn't Be Sold. Old Mother Brine, a tiny, toothless fence wrapped in shawls with eyes like wet pebbles, smiles up at you. Sabine stands at your shoulder, pale. "Here's the sum of it, dearie," says Brine. "Give me the singer's little mirror, and her debts vanish, and I'll see she goes home when the Glass opens. Keep it, and she owes me more than she can ever pay. I'm patient. I'm very patient."

  • Hand over the shard. Sabine's debts are cleared, and she weeps with relief and shame. The Syndicate now controls a shard (and a say in who passes through the Glass). → go to 7, then Ending B.
  • Refuse, and keep the shard for Sabine. Brine shrugs. "Your funeral, dearie." Sabine squeezes your hand so hard it hurts. → go to 7, then Ending A.
  • Threaten Brine with Hale's Marker or the Debtors' Page: "The Watch would love to see this." (Intimidation DC 14; advantage with both items.) Success: Brine cancels Sabine's debt and lets you keep the shard, but you've made a dangerous enemy. → go to 7, then Ending A plus the Brine's Grudge consequence. Failure: Brine's guards move in, and you flee with Sabine. → go to 7, then Ending C.

entries.title: Rooftop at Dawn 🌹
entries.html:
(Read before any ending.) On the roof of the Blue Hour, as the colored lanterns pale into dawn, Sabine lights a cigarette she never smokes. "Thirty years ago a boy with a dimpled smile asked me to kiss him into office. I did. Tonight somebody killed him." She looks at you. "Don't make my mistakes, kid."

Resist or yield: She leans in, close enough that you smell gardenias. "Kiss me for luck? Just luck. Nothing sealed."

  • Yield (both adults, both willing): a soft, smoky kiss as the sun comes up. Fade to black on the rooftop. In Vesperine even a "luck" kiss is a small promise, so note Anchor: Sabine's Luck (you owe her one honest favor). +1 Allure.
  • Resist kindly: "Ask me again when you're not afraid." +1 Allure. She laughs, really laughs, for the first time tonight.

adventures.pitch:
Pitch: A torch singer from another world deals you into a high-stakes card game in a smoky salon. Tonight she has promised to hand you over to the Syndicate, and she would very much rather not.

Leads into: The Black Kiss via the underworld thread (Drowned Market, Varo, Captain Hale), or the Syndicate's hold on the Glass.

adventures.title: A Rose Before Midnight

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
d6 Your life tonight
1 Pressing flowers from a funeral in a heavy book. A petal is still damp when you open it.
2 Up late with a fantasy novel, wishing, not for the first time, that you lived in one.
3 Leaving a florist's shop at closing. Every rose in the bucket has turned to face you.
4 Watching the sun set from a rooftop. It doesn't quite finish setting.
5 In a bridal-shop fitting room, for someone else's wedding. The mirror has three of you, then four.
6 Bored. Terribly, beautifully bored, the kind that aches.

The call. You speak your Mirror-Promise aloud, half as a joke. Rose petals drift out of the glass and settle on your shoes.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html: The glass fogs over as though someone on the other side has breathed on it. A finger draws a heart in the fog, then crosses it out and draws a rose instead, with a flourish. Then a long violet hand slides through the surface with no ripple at all, a thorned ring on every finger, holding a single red rose out to you, stem first, thorns carefully removed. "Come and see something beautiful," says a voice like warm honey poured over gravel, "before it ends." You take the rose. The world folds like a love letter. You are standing in tall, cool grass under trees that glow soft blue from within, and moths the size of cats drift overhead like slow lanterns. The sky is the violet of the last minute before night, and it stays that way.

sections.title: Meeting Caelum
sections.html:
• His approach: He makes bargains sound like love poems, and he tests you constantly. He offers a gift, then watches to see if you notice the string. Saying "thank you" in the fey manner is a small debt, and he'll wince on your behalf and teach you not to ("Say instead, 'You honor me.' Never thank us. We collect.").
  • What he offers: Safe passage through the Lanternwood, his protection from lesser fey, and "anything that fits in your two hands," in exchange for one dance at the seventh bell.
  • What he hides: He is the Fae Duke's son, sent to see the Accord fail. He wants Vesperine for himself, and (Insight DC 18) he's lonely in a way that frightens him. The token he wants back is a rose he gave Queen Ilysse two hundred years ago. While she holds it, she can always find him and can tell his father where he is.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • Thorned Word: one fey creature must stop and parley for 1 round.
  • Rose Ward: gain temporary hit points equal to 2 × your level.
  • Princely Command: a lesser fey (CR 1 or less) obeys one short command.

Using all three in one adventure makes you a "favored guest," so add +1 Enthrallment (Caelum's tally).

Oracle prompts (d6):

  1. Is a fey watching from the trees?
  2. Does Caelum tell the truth this time?
  3. Is the twilight darkening (one step closer to sunset)?
  4. Is someone dreaming nearby?
  5. Does Pipwhistle have something you need?
  6. Has Ilysse already sensed Caelum?

The Sunset Clock. The Lanternwood is stuck at twilight, but tonight the sun is finally setting, and at sunset Caelum's glamour fails. Start with 6 Twilight. Each scene costs 1. Scenes marked ⏳ cost 2. At 0, go straight to 7.

sections.title: The Entry Mission: The Thief of Roses
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: The Prince's Favor. Caelum owes you (or you owe him) a dance, and he is genuinely fond of you. He escorts you to Vesperine by dawn, gives you a thornless rose that keeps you hidden from lesser fey once, and murmurs as he goes: "Ask me sometime what I really want. On the right night, I'll answer." You start The Black Kiss with a powerful, unreliable fey ally. Leash variant: he can't refuse to come when you call him through the rose, and he resents it, charmingly.

Ending B: The Queen's Confidant. Ilysse names you a "friend of the Hush." She lets you view one cocoon in the Silk Library: a dream of a young silver-haired bride and a dimpled groom at an altar of white roses, the wedding of Isaveth Sable and Aurel Fenn (a Keystone clue for The Black Kiss). Complication: Caelum is wounded and sulky (–1 Allure with him), and the Moth Court will expect you back for The Dreamthieves.

Ending C: Thornwake's Pawn. Brother Ash delivers the rose to Lady Nocturne Vesh, who now knows where Caelum is at every moment and can expose him to the Duke on Night 7. You have money, a cold conscience, and (Insight DC 14, or the oracle) the impression that Brother Ash smiled with too many teeth. You start the campaign knowing the Thornwake exists, with a contact inside it who wants to use you again. Complication: +1 Enthrallment (Nocturne). Caelum, when he learns, will be heartbroken and dangerous.

sections.title: Rewards & Consequences
sections.html:
Result Effect in the campaign
Anchor: One Dance at the Seventh Bell You must be where Caelum is at midnight on Night 7 (see Part 2). Released freely if he truly loves you.
Clue: The Silver-Haired Woman's Dream Points to Thessaly / Isaveth buying Widow's Sigh. Keystone clue once viewed.
Ally: Rillo Advantage on the Dimming path in Side Adventure 2. Can lead you to Nocturne's revels.
Thornless rose Hides you from lesser fey once.
Queen's Fury Ilysse's court is hostile at the start of Side Adventure 2 (DCs +2).
Leash You can summon Caelum once per night; his Allure caps at 3 until you give it back.
Pip's Shiny Thing Pip pesters you until you deliver a trinket. Fail to, and he steals something important on Night 3.
+1 Enthrallment (Nocturne) Nocturne's first temptation scene starts one step deeper.

entries.title: The Rose Offer 🌹
entries.html:
Caelum circles you slowly, delighted. "An oathless one. Your promises go everywhere." He plucks a petal from his own antlers and lets it fall. "I need something stolen, and I can't steal it myself. There is a rose in the Cocoon Palace, mine once. Bring it back, and I'll owe you a dance at the seventh bell. Or you owe me one. I can never remember which way it goes." He smiles. "Seal it?" He offers his cheek, or his hand, or his lips: your choice.

Resist or yield:

  • Yield: seal it with a kiss (cheek, hand, or lips). Gain the Anchor: One Dance at the Seventh Bell, +1 Allure, and advantage on the next Charisma check against any fey in this adventure (they can smell his favor on you).
  • Out-bargain him. Make an opposed Persuasion or Deception check (you vs. his +4 at L1, or +6 at L2–3). Success: you rephrase it as "you owe me the dance, and I choose the night," and he laughs aloud. Gain +2 Allure and no Anchor. Failure: you owe the dance anyway (Anchor), with no Allure.
  • Refuse wittily ("Roses wilt, Your Highness; I'd prefer something evergreen."). +1 Allure. He'll help anyway, because he's curious.
  • Say "thank you." Gain +1 Enthrallment (Caelum). He sighs. "Oh, darling. We'll work on that."

Then:

  • To take the moonlit path past a talkative hedge-sprite: → go to 2.
  • To follow the floating lights toward music: → go to 3.

entries.title: Pipwhistle's Pocket Bargain
entries.html:
A tiny, mossy, button-eyed sprite in a thimble hat drops onto your shoulder: Pipwhistle Dewlace, a hedgefolk thief of trinkets. "Ooooh, a Glass-walker! Got any buttons? Promises? I'll trade you a secret for a button." Caelum rolls his eyes.

  • Trade a button (or any small object from your own world): Pip whispers, "The Moth Queen's library's guarded by her knight, Sir Fennic, but he falls asleep if you hum to him." You gain advantage on the Stealth or Performance check in 5.
  • Trade a promise ("I'll bring you a shiny thing tomorrow"): Pip gives you the secret and a silver needle (it cuts silk like butter, so you automatically succeed at opening one cocoon). You gain a minor Anchor: Pip's Shiny Thing.
  • Shoo him away: he steals one item from your pack (oracle: your choice of something trivial or useful) and skips off cackling.

→ go to 4.

entries.title: The Lure of the Lights (Chase) ⏳
entries.html:
The lights are will-o'-wisps, and the music is a fey reveler's pipes echoing off the water. A laughing voice calls from a lily-choked pond: "Rest a moment, lovely. Just a moment." A green-gold nymph lounges among the lilies (Ondine Mirewillow). She wants your shoes, and the hours of your life that go with them.

  • Resist her lure: Wisdom save, DC 12 at L1 or DC 13 at L2–3. Failure: you "rest a moment," lose 2 Twilight, and wake barefoot.
  • Then flee the wisps (one will-o'-wisp at L2–3; at L1 the lights only harry you). Chase, 3 rounds:
  • Run (Athletics DC 12)
  • Close your eyes and follow Caelum's voice (Wisdom DC 12)
  • Splash the pond (cold water breaks fey glamour: Ondine shrieks, and the lights scatter)

Two successes: you escape, and → go to 4. Two failures: 1d6 lightning damage per failure (L1: 1d4), and you arrive at 4 with 1 fewer Twilight.

entries.title: The Garden Gate (Riddle)
entries.html:
The Cocoon Palace rises ahead, a towering tree of pale silk, glowing from within like a paper lantern. The only door is a gate of woven moth-wings with a pair of painted eyes that open and speak:

I wear a hundred eyes and never once have seen;
I dance with my own shadow, in gowns of dust and sheen.
I fly to the one thing that will burn me clean —
Say my name, and enter, guest of the Queen.

  • Answer "a moth": the gate parts like curtains. → go to 5.
  • Answer wrong: the gate sighs dream-dust on you (Constitution save DC 12, or fall asleep for 1 Twilight). Try again, or have Caelum whisper it (costs 1 Allure, because he hates being useful), and → go to 5.
  • Rillo's way in: if you hear piping inside, you can join the revel at the back of the palace instead (go to 5, revel option).

entries.title: The Revel and the Silk Library ⏳
entries.html:
Inside, dreamers float asleep in silken cocoons along spiraling galleries, smiling. Far below, a goat-legged piper (Rillo Fennamint) plays for a revel of pale moth-fey. On a balcony of moonlight, Queen Ilysse of the Hush watches, her wings patterned like eyes. Caelum, invisible in the doorway, hisses: "The rose is in the Silk Library, her cocoon-room. Don't let her see you. She will see me."

Choose your approach:

  • The Dimming (stealth): Creep along the galleries (Stealth DC 13 at L1, 14 at L2–3; advantage with Pip's secret). Success: you reach the Silk Library unseen. Find the rose: a crystal rose inside a cocoon labeled in moth-script, beside other cocoons of traded dreams. One reads "Wedding Day — a silver-haired woman — paid for one sigh of orchid." (Gain Clue: The Silver-Haired Woman's Dream.) Take the rose and → go to 6. Failure: → go to 6, alarm raised.
  • The Revel (social): Join Rillo's dance. Performance or Acrobatics DC 12 keeps up; failure means you dance for an hour (–1 Twilight). Charm him with a dance or a joke (Persuasion DC 13) and he'll tell you the Queen keeps a "silver-haired woman's wedding" in her library and gladly lead you there (as above, plus the clue). He can also be turned as a future ally (Ally: Rillo).
  • The Audience (bold): Present yourself to the Queen. → go to 5a.

entries.title: The Queen's Whisper 🌹
entries.html:
Ilysse beckons you close, closer, until you must lean in to hear her. "You smell of his roses." Her antennae brush your cheek. "Tell me a dream you've never told anyone, and I'll give you whatever he's sent you to steal."

Resist or yield:

  • Yield: tell her a true dream (the player describes one; any honest answer). She tastes it with a shiver. +1 Allure with Ilysse, but you lose that dream: you will never dream it again. She gives you the rose freely: "Tell him I'm done with it." She adds, almost tenderly, "And come back. I'll show you a wedding." (Clue: The Silver-Haired Woman's Dream, offered for later.) → go to 7.
  • Resist: Wisdom save, DC 13 at L1 or DC 14 at L2–3, against her drowsy charm. Success: you step back. "Not tonight, Majesty." She laughs softly and lets you go empty-handed. → go to 5 (another approach, with –1 Twilight). Failure: +1 Enthrallment (Ilysse), and you sleep in a cocoon for 1 Twilight before Caelum drags you out. → go to 6.

entries.title: Moth-Guard Chase
entries.html:
The alarm sounds as a thousand wings beat at once. Sir Fennic, the Queen's moth-knight, and his guards pursue you down the spiraling silk. Use giant moths (giant bat stats with a sleep-dust bite, Constitution DC 11): one at L1, two at L2, and two plus Sir Fennic (scout with flying) at L3.

Chase, 3 rounds:

  • Slide down the silk (Acrobatics DC 13)
  • Cut a cocoon free to block them (silver needle = automatic success, otherwise Strength DC 13). The dreamer wakes, groggy and grateful.
  • Hum (Fennic yawns; Performance DC 12, advantage with Pip's secret)
  • Fight at the gate (scaled encounter)

Escape with two successes, or defeat the pursuers: → go to 7. Two failures: you're cornered, and Caelum steps out of the shadows. "Fennic. Old friend." Fennic lowers his spear in bewildered loyalty; you escape, but Ilysse now knows Caelum sent you (consequence Queen's Fury). → go to 7.

entries.title: Sunset: The Seventh Bell 🌹 (Moral Choice)
entries.html:
At the forest's edge, the sun finally sets. Caelum's glamour peels away like a dropped silk: the antlers dim, the thorns lengthen, and his golden eyes are, for a moment, terribly young. "There," he says softly. "Now you've seen me." He holds out his hand for the rose.

If you have the Anchor: One Dance, or simply wish to, he asks: "Dance with me, before the bell?" (Yield: a slow dance under the moth-lanterns. Fade to black on a forest that hums with light, +1 Allure. Resist: "When I choose the night." He bows, delighted, +1 Allure.)

A hooded monk steps from the trees: Brother Ash, whose robes smell of ash and roses (he's one of Lady Nocturne Vesh's agents in a human guise; Insight DC 15 to sense the glamour). "I'll pay well for that rose, traveler. Enough to buy any bargain he's tricked you into."

What do you do with the rose?

  • Give it to Caelum. He holds it to his lips, and the rose dissolves into him. "Free of her," he breathes. Then, more quietly: "...and of my father's eyes, for a while." Take Ending A.
  • Return it to Ilysse (if you're on speaking terms, or go back secretly). The Queen is moved that a mortal would choose her over a prince. Take Ending B.
  • Keep it. Whoever holds the rose can always find Caelum. He looks at you with new, wary respect. "Clever. Cruel. I like you." Take Ending A with the Leash complication.
  • Sell it to Brother Ash. Gain 50 gp × your level, and a sinking feeling. Take Ending C.

adventures.pitch:
Pitch: A rose-crowned fey prince offers you anything that fits in your two hands for a single dance. His first gift is a burglary: steal back his love-token from the Moth Queen who still hates him, before sunset strips his glamour bare.

Leads into: The Dreamthieves of the Moth Court (Side Adventure 2) and the Fae endgame. One ending carries a Keystone clue for The Black Kiss.

adventures.title: Hold Your Breath

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
d6 Your life tonight
1 In a long hot bath after a terrible week, singing badly to the tiles.
2 Swimming laps alone in a hotel pool at midnight. Something brushes your ankle.
3 Washing dishes. The water in the sink is suddenly very deep.
4 Walking a rainy pier, staring at the puddles. One of them laughs.
5 Pouring a glass of wine. Your reflection on its surface winks.
6 Seasick on a ferry, leaning over the rail, as someone below the waves calls your name.

The call. You murmur your Mirror-Promise to the water. A song you feel in your teeth rises from beneath the surface.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html: The water goes still as glass, and beneath it a face looks up at you, laughing, upside down: sea-green scales along her cheekbones, black hair drifting with sea-glass and tiny bells, eyes the color of moonlit surf. A cool, wet, webbed hand closes around your wrist. "Hold your breath, darling," she says, and her voice comes up through the water in bubbles. She pulls. You go down and down through warm water that turns cold, through dark that turns blue, through a rush of salt and bells, and you surface gasping in a moonlit sea cave with the roar of surf all around you. The water is at your waist. It's rising. She surfaces beside you, shakes out her hair, and grins. "Welcome to Saltgrave. Can you swim? Say yes."

sections.title: Meeting Marisol
sections.html:
• Her approach: Dares. She splashes you, challenges you to cliff-dive, holds your gaze a beat too long, and laughs at everything, especially danger.
  • What she offers: A crew, an adventure, her protection under the sea, a luck-kiss that lets you breathe water, and (if you're interested) a sweetheart who will race you to the bottom of the sea.
  • What she hides: She gave the Pearl Heart to Captain Kray. She wanted to break Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa's rule over the Drowned Choir; Kray betrayed her and enslaved her sisters with it. She wants you to recover the Heart and give it to her, making her the Choir's new Mother.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • Undertow: pull you 30 feet through water or away from an enemy (no opportunity attacks).
  • Siren's Laugh: one enemy makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or is distracted (disadvantage on its next attack).
  • Breath of the Deep: grant water breathing for 10 minutes, or restore it if her kiss has worn off.

Oracle prompts (d6):

  1. Has the tide risen another level?
  2. Is a wrecker patrol near?
  3. Is Marisol lying right now?
  4. Are the sirens singing (Wisdom DC 12 or move toward the water)?
  5. Is Bel Okafor alone?
  6. Is there something valuable in the wreckage?

The Tide Clock. Start at Low. It rises one level after each scene: Low → Waist → Chest → Flooded. When it's Flooded, any check made underwater without water breathing has disadvantage and costs 1d4 cold damage.

sections.title: The Entry Mission: The Wreckers' Night
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: Marisol's Champion. Marisol takes the Heart, sings, and breaks the chains of the Choir; her sisters rise singing. She is the new, reckless, joyful Mother of the Drowned Choir, and she owes you everything (Allure +2). Nerissa slips away into the deep, humiliated and plotting. You gain Marisol's Song of Calling for Night 7 (allies get advantage on saves against charm). Complication: when Nerissa returns in Side Adventure 3, she brings an army, and she knows your name.

Ending B: Nerissa's Truth. Nerissa takes the Pearl Heart, and her voice returns like a storm. The Choir is freed, and the old order restored. Marisol is cast out to the shallows, furious and heartbroken. She may become a rival, or (if your Allure with her is 3+) a chastened friend who meets you later in Vesperine. You gain the Choir's eternal friendship and Nerissa's blessing (once, the sea will carry you anywhere along the coast). Complication: Marisol's Anchor is unresolved, and she will hold you to it.

Ending C: Kray's Ledger. You hold the Heart (or the archive). With Bel's testimony and Varo's report in hand, you head for Vesperine knowing the vow-page was sold to "a grey-veiled lady on Needle Row" (supporting clue for The Black Kiss), and holding Hale's Syndicate debts (he'll cooperate fully). The Choir remains chained until you return the Heart, and Kray swears revenge. Complication: Side Adventure 3 begins with the Choir still enslaved, and Kray expecting you.

sections.title: Rewards & Consequences
sections.html:
Result Effect in the campaign
Anchor: Marisol's Luck You've promised to see her quest through. Release it only with her blessing.
Ally: Bel Okafor First mate's testimony and inside help. Advantage on Charm/Stealth paths in Side Adventure 3.
Pearl Heart Whoever holds it commands the Choir's voices (huge leverage).
Blackmail archive Hale cooperates. One free Opera Council vote. Varo's report clue.
Sea-glass whistle Summon Marisol once anywhere on the coast.
Song of Calling Advantage on saves against charm for all allies on Night 7.
Wrecked ship If you ignored the beacon: –1 Allure with Marisol, and the merchant's grieving family appears on Night 2.
Kray's Revenge Kray hires wreckers to ambush you in the Drowned Market on Night 3.

entries.title: The Rising Cave 🌹
entries.html:
Marisol floats on her back, watching you. "Here's the trouble, darling. Smugglers have stolen something of my family's: a pearl, big as your fist. Help me get it back and I'll make you rich and famous, and probably wet." Her grin widens. "But first, you'll need to breathe down here." She swims close enough that the bells in her hair chime against your cheek. "Kiss me for luck?"

Resist or yield:

  • Yield: kiss her for luck (both adults, both willing). She tastes of salt and laughter. You gain water breathing for 1 hour and the Anchor: Marisol's Luck (in Carnelia, a kiss is a small promise; this one means "I'll see your quest through"). +1 Allure.
  • Counter-dare ("Race me to the far wall first."): Athletics DC 12 / 13. Win, and she laughs and gives you the breath with a simple hand-squeeze instead (no Anchor; water breathing for 30 minutes; +1 Allure). Lose, and you kiss her anyway or go without.
  • Refuse: she shrugs, unoffended. "Hold your breath, then." You have no water breathing (holding breath: Con DC 12 every 2 minutes underwater).

Then:

  • To swim the tide tunnels toward the warehouse: → go to 2.
  • To climb the cliff path to the false lighthouse: → go to 3.

entries.title: The Tide Tunnels and the Shipwreck Riddle
entries.html:
The tunnels open onto a shipwreck wedged in the rock, its figurehead a weeping woman. Carved into its hull, in old sailor's script, is a riddle guarding the captain's hidden lockbox:

I'm caught in nets but never fished, I'm owed by all at sea;
I steal the sand and give it back, and twice a day I'm free.
I keep no clock but keep the time, the moon's my only master —
wait on me, and I'll come home; fight me, I come faster.

  • Answer "the tide": the figurehead's hand opens. Inside are a sea-glass whistle (summons Marisol once from anywhere along the coast) and an old map of the grotto. Gain advantage on your next Stealth check. → go to 4.
  • Answer wrong: the wreck shifts and groans. Con DC 12 or take 1d6 bludgeoning damage, and the tide rises one level. → go to 4.

entries.title: The False Lighthouse
entries.html:
On the cliff stands the Wreckers' Beacon, a fake lighthouse luring ships onto the rocks. Two bandits stand watch at L1 (three at L2, four at L3). A merchant cog is on course for the rocks right now.

  • Douse the beacon (Stealth DC 13, then Sleight of Hand DC 12): the ship turns away in time. +1 Hero point (advantage on one roll later). → go to 4.
  • Fight (scaled): win, and you douse it. You find a wrecker's lantern with a password scratched into it, "Salt and Lick."
  • Ignore it and hurry on: the ship wrecks. Marisol goes quiet. "Not their fault," she mutters. "None of this is their fault." → go to 4.

entries.title: The Syndicate Warehouse
entries.html:
Crates of wrecked cargo, rum, and silk. Thugs playing dice by lantern-light: two at L1, three at L2, four at L3. Above them, on a catwalk, stands Bel Okafor, Kray's first mate, a tall woman with a shaved head, a scar through one eyebrow, and a look of profound disgust at her own crew.

  • Bluff your way in ("Kray sent us." Deception DC 13; automatic success with the "Salt and Lick" password): the thugs let you pass. → go to 5.
  • Sneak along the catwalks (Stealth DC 13): you reach Bel alone. → go to 5.
  • Start a fight (scaled thugs): Bel watches, arms folded, and doesn't join in. Afterward she says, "Finally. Someone with nerve." → go to 5.

entries.title: Bel Okafor 🌹
entries.html:
Bel pours you a rum without asking. "Kray's got the Pearl Heart in his strongroom. He's making the Choir sing ships onto the rocks. I've had enough of it." She studies Marisol coolly. "Funny thing is, she's the one who gave it to him."

Marisol goes pale beneath her scales. (If you have Allure 2+ with Marisol, she says, very quietly, "...It's true.")

Resist or yield (Bel): Bel is lonely, clever, and looking for an excuse to walk out. She looks at you a long moment. "I could use someone to talk me into it."

  • Yield (both adults, both willing): you share the rum, a long talk, and more. Fade to black among the silk bales. She wakes with a plan: Kray's strongroom key, a back way out, and a promise to testify. Gain Ally: Bel Okafor.
  • Resist, and persuade her with words (Persuasion DC 13 / 14, advantage if you doused the beacon): she gives you the key and the back way, and agrees to testify if you survive.
  • Intimidate her (Intimidation DC 15): she gives you the key, but she'll warn Kray if things go badly.

With or without Bel's help, you slip into Kray's strongroom. In the iron box lies the Pearl Heart, pulsing with stolen song. In a sea-chest sits Kray's blackmail archive, including a crumpled report in Varo's handwriting: "'Aurel Fenn & Isaveth Sable' — sold by Brine to grey-veil lady, Needle Row." You can grab one: the Heart, or the archive (unless you have Bel's help, which lets you take both). → go to 6.

entries.title: Chase up the Tidepool Stair
entries.html:
Bells clang. Captain Morven "Saltlick" Kray roars from the dark: "THIEVES!" The tide is rising (check the clock). Kray and his wreckers pursue you up a slick, winding, half-flooded stair. At L1 use two bandits and a thug; at L2–3 add Kray himself (bandit captain; +10 HP at L3).

Chase, 3 rounds:

  • Climb (Athletics DC 13)
  • Dive and swim (water breathing = automatic success; otherwise Con DC 12)
  • Knock loose the old barrels (Strength DC 12)
  • Marisol's Siren's Laugh (Gateway Aid)

Two successes: you burst out into the moonlit surf and escape, and → go to 7. Two failures: Kray corners you on a ledge. Fight, or try Bargain: offer to keep his skimming secret from Mother Brine (Persuasion DC 15 / 16). If you win or bargain, → go to 7.

entries.title: On the Rocks (Moral Choice)
entries.html:
On a moon-washed reef, Marisol holds out her hand for the Pearl Heart. Her eyes are bright. "Give it to me. Nerissa's ruled the Choir for six hundred years. She'd have drowned us all for tradition. With the Heart, I can free my sisters and change everything." Behind her in the surf, an old, silver-scaled siren rises from the water: Mother-of-Pearl Nerissa, her voice a hoarse whisper. "Child," she breathes. "What have you done?"

(If you took the archive instead of the Heart, this scene is about the truth. Marisol begs you not to tell. Choose to keep her secret or tell Nerissa, then use the matching ending.)

  • Give the Heart to Marisol (or keep her secret): take Ending A.
  • Give the Heart to Nerissa and tell her the truth: take Ending B.
  • Keep the Heart yourself as leverage, or bargain it to Kray / Bel for the archive: take Ending C.

adventures.pitch:
Pitch: A grinning siren drags you through your bathwater into a sea cave as the tide comes in. She dares you to kiss her for luck, rob a smugglers' warehouse, and outrun the wreckers, then hopes you never learn she's the one who sold her sisters out.

Leads into: The Song Beneath Saltgrave (Side Adventure 3). One ending carries Varo's report, a supporting clue for The Black Kiss.

adventures.title: May I Come In?

sections.title: Your Side of the Glass
sections.html:
d6 Your life tonight
1 Alone at a candlelit dinner after being stood up. The empty chair across from you is only empty in the mirror.
2 Up past midnight watching an old vampire film, laughing at it, a little.
3 Locking up a wine bar; one glass on the bar is still half full and moving.
4 At a costume party, in a mask. You came alone and nobody's asked you to dance.
5 Unable to sleep, writing a letter to someone you'll never send it to.
6 Standing by the window at night, wishing someone would ask before they assumed.

The call. You whisper your Mirror-Promise. In the mirror, the empty armchair behind you is no longer empty.

sections.title: The Pull-Through
sections.html:
The room in the mirror is your room, perfectly ordinary. Except: in the reflection, a black velvet coat with garnet buttons sits in your armchair with no one inside it. A ruffled cravat. Oxblood gloves, one resting on the arm of the chair. A wineglass lifts itself in a toast. "Please don't scream," says a voice, warm and dry and amused at itself. "I've had a very long century. I'm going to ask you something, and you're allowed to say no. That's rather the point." The glove turns, palm up. "May I come in? You do have to say yes." If you say yes, the coat stands, bows, and offers you its arm, and as you take it the mirror's surface gives like velvet. You step through into candlelight and the scent of crushed grapes, and a masked orchestra in the next room strikes up a waltz.

If the PC says no: Valentin sighs. "Of course. Thank you for answering honestly." The glass stays still. Roll again on the d6 door table in How to Use This Book (or, if you'd still like to play this adventure, he asks again three nights later, very politely).

sections.title: Meeting Valentin
sections.html:
• His approach: He asks permission for everything, and makes asking the most seductive thing in the room. "May I take your hand on the stairs?" "May I tell you that your pulse just quickened? I'm flattered." He describes warmth and sunlight like a man describing a lost love.
  • What he offers: An invitation to the Harvest Masquerade at Château Dusk, a borrowed mask, wit, protection from the house's hungrier residents, and a way to Vesperine.
  • What he hides: He was Countess Morwenna Dusk's consort for a century, until her steward Lucan Vey framed him for a murder. He's exiled and forbidden from the house, so he needs you to be seen with him. And: he plans to go through the Oathless Glass to a world without the Accord in hopes of walking in sunlight, with or without your blessing.

Gateway Aid (3):

  • Shadow Step: move 30 feet through darkness unseen.
  • Gentleman's Grip: grapple or restrain one enemy for 1 round (he has the strength of the dead).
  • Mesmeric Glance: a humanoid thrall or guard makes a DC 13 Wisdom save or forgets the last minute.

He will never use Mesmeric Glance on you, and he says so.

Oracle prompts (d6):

  1. Has Lucan noticed you?
  2. Is Morwenna watching Valentin?
  3. Are the servants afraid?
  4. Is a vampire spawn in this room?
  5. Does Valentin want to tell you something?
  6. How long until dawn (1–3 close, 4–6 far)?

sections.title: The Entry Mission: The Harvest Masquerade
Endings
sections.html:
Ending A: The Reunion. You hand Morwenna the Proof. She reads it twice. Then she looks at Valentin for a long, long moment and says only, "You should have made me listen." Lucan is seized (or flees, wounded, into the Duskvine, to return in Side Adventure 4). Morwenna pledges her Council vote to whatever you champion on Night 7 and gives you her card. Then, quietly: "There was a maskmaker at my party last spring — silver hair, steady hands. I knew her once as a child. Isaveth. Isaveth Sable. I couldn't place her then." (Keystone lead for The Black Kiss, confirmed when she meets Thessaly.) Valentin is forgiven, or nearly. Complication: forgiveness is fragile, and he still plans to go through the Glass.

Ending B: Hunted. You free the villagers and flee with them up through the vineyards under a thin moon. Marta Ilic, the village innkeeper, embraces her son, who was among them, and becomes your ally. But Lucan survived, and he's burned the Proof. He tells Morwenna that you and Valentin attacked her household. Start Side Adventure 4 early with Marta as ally and Morwenna hostile (DCs +2 with her) until you prove the truth. You gain the villagers' undying gratitude (free food, shelter, and lies to the Watch in the Duskvine).

Ending C: Pact in the Dark. You give Lucan the Proof. He bows, and in that moment Valentin vanishes into shadow without a word. You leave Château Dusk with a promise of Syndicate patronage, a purse of 100 gp × your level, and a seat at Lucan's side on Night 7. Complication: Lucan will betray you on Night 7, and Valentin, who once asked so politely, will no longer ask anything of you. (A redemption path: return the villagers' freedom and Valentin's name before Night 5, and he may forgive you.)

sections.title: Rewards & Consequences
sections.html:
Result Effect in the campaign
The Proof Clears Valentin's name and implicates Lucan and the Syndicate. Morwenna's trust.
Morwenna's vote One Opera Council vote on Night 7.
Keystone lead: Isaveth Sable Morwenna can identify Thessaly as Isaveth Sable.
Invitation A private salon with Morwenna in Side Adventure 4 (fade to black, both willing).
Ally: Marta Ilic A village network in the Duskvine. Starts Side Adventure 4 early.
Anka freed If you freed her compulsion, she smuggles you a servants' key in Side Adventure 4.
Lucan's Grudge Lucan sends spawn after you on Night 4.
Valentin's Wound If you refused his request and failed the chase, he begins the campaign at half strength.
Pact with Lucan A Corruption mark: you're on the Syndicate path, and Lucan betrays you on Night 7.

entries.title: The Side Gallery 🌹
entries.html:
You step out of a tall gilded mirror into a dim side gallery hung with portraits whose eyes have been painted over. Valentin (his clothes visible in the mirror, but not him) adjusts your mask with careful fingers. "May I tell you what we're doing? I'd like you to know before you agree to it." He explains: proof of Lucan's crimes is in the steward's study; the Countess believes Valentin a murderer; and if she sees him, she might set him on fire. "So I'll need you to be the charming one."

Resist or yield: He offers his gloved hand. "May I hold your hand as we walk in? It will help with the story that we're merely lovers sneaking into a party. It will also help me."

  • Yield: take his hand. It's cold, and then, strangely, less cold. +1 Allure. He looks at your joined hands as if they were a sunrise.
  • Resist, gently: "Let's keep it to an arm." He smiles. "Of course." +1 Allure (he respects candor above all).
  • Ask why it would help him (Insight DC 13): "Because I haven't been touched without fear in thirty years." +1 Allure, and you understand him better (advantage on your next Insight check about him).

→ go to 2.

entries.title: The Grand Tasting Hall 🌹
entries.html:
Candlelight, musicians, masked donors boasting about it like a spa visit. On a velvet divan sits Countess Morwenna Dusk, raven-haired, lips like a fresh cut, receiving admirers. Her eyes find you through the crowd and linger. Valentin goes very still behind his mask.

She beckons. "A new face. How delicious. And I say that as a figure of speech, darling, unless you'd like otherwise. Everyone here has said yes in writing." She pats the divan beside her.

Resist or yield (Morwenna):

  • Yield: flirt with her as an equal (Persuasion DC 14 / 15). She's fascinated. She offers you a glass of the Crimson Vintage (just wine), tells you she's lonely, and invites you to her private salon "later, if you're still interested; I'll ask again then." +1 Allure (Morwenna). Note the Invitation (it can lead to a fade-to-black scene in Side Adventure 4, if both are willing).
  • Resist gracefully: "I'm spoken for this evening." She glances at your masked companion, and her smile flickers. "Oh. Oh. I'd know that cravat anywhere." Valentin is exposed: she gives you until dawn to "make your case, or I make mine." → go to 3.
  • Ask her about the disappearances: Insight DC 15 reveals that the servants fear Lucan, not her. She frowns and says, "Lucan handles the help." Gain the clue Servants' Fear.

Then: → go to 3.

entries.title: The Frightened Maid
entries.html:
In a servants' corridor, you find a maid weeping into her apron, with two small puncture marks on her wrist and a glassy look in her eyes: a thrall of Lucan's. Her name is Anka, and she's twenty-three. She whispers that people from the village are being taken "downstairs," and that Lucan's study is "the room with the red seal on the door."

(Valentin's hands curl into fists. "She hasn't said yes to anything. Not really.")

  • Comfort her and promise to help (Persuasion DC 12 / 13; or use Valentin's Mesmeric Glance to lift Lucan's compulsion for one hour, if she agrees): she leads you to the study by the servants' stair. → go to 4.
  • Press her for information (Intimidation DC 12): she gives directions but runs straight to Lucan afterward (oracle question 1 is automatically "yes" from now on). → go to 4.
  • Leave her and find the study yourself (Investigation DC 14; failure: → go to 5 first).

entries.title: Lucan's Study (Riddle)
entries.html:
The study door is locked with a seal of red wax, magically bound. Its brass plate reads:

I was poured to seal a lie, red as blood and twice as dry;
I keep a secret, keep a name, I bear a crest but feel no shame.
I'm warm when I'm made and cold when I'm kept —
break me, and the truth runs free.

  • Answer "sealing wax" (or "a seal"): the lock melts like a candle. Inside, among neat ledgers, you find the Proof, a letter in Lucan's hand to the Thorn Syndicate: "The consort will hang for Count Aurelio's death as planned; with Valentin gone, Her Ladyship's vote is mine to deliver." You also find a ledger page listing villagers delivered to the "cellar chapel." → go to 5.
  • Wrong answer: the seal burns. Take 1d6 fire damage (L1: 1d4), and a bell rings in the cellars, so spawn are coming. Valentin can force the door (Gentleman's Grip, Gateway Aid). Take the Proof and → go to 5.

entries.title: The Barrel Labyrinth (Chase)
entries.html:
Down a stair into a maze of thousand-year-old casks. The lights go out one by one. From the dark, a polite golden voice: "Guests are not permitted in the cellars." It's Lucan Vey, and his newly turned spawn are hunting you. Use one vampire spawn at 40 HP at L1, the same at full HP at L2, and two spawn at L3.

Chase, 3 rounds:

  • Run toward the smell of fresh, not aged, blood (Perception DC 13)
  • Navigate by the casks' vintages (Survival DC 14)
  • Roll a barrel down an aisle (Strength DC 12)
  • Valentin's Shadow Step (Gateway Aid)

Two successes: you lose them in the dark and find the crypt-chapel, so → go to 6. Two failures: a spawn catches you. Fight (scaled), then → go to 6. If you drop to 0 HP, Valentin carries you out (Death's Door; see How to Use This Book).

entries.title: The Crypt-Chapel (Moral Choice)
entries.html:
A deconsecrated chapel. In iron cages, a dozen villagers sit pale and dazed but alive. An altar stands at one end, and Lucan's coffin rests behind it. You hear him coming.

Valentin is wounded and grey-faced from the chase (or from fending off spawn so you could escape). He sinks against a pillar. "There's no time for everything. You'll have to choose."

The choice:

  • Free the villagers (Sleight of Hand DC 13, or smash the locks, Strength DC 14): it takes time. Lucan arrives, but you'll have witnesses. Any proof you didn't already take stays upstairs.
  • Take the Proof to Morwenna now, before Lucan can burn it, leaving the villagers for later. They might not survive the night (oracle: 1–3, some are turned before you return).
  • Both is possible only if you already have the Proof from scene 4, in which case you simply have to hold off Lucan while the cages open.

Valentin's request. Before you decide, he asks, very quietly and without looking at you: "I can keep going. But I'd be quicker, and you'd be safer, if I fed. Only a little. Only from your wrist. And only if you truly want to. Saying no will not change a single thing between us."

  • Agree (an enthusiastic yes, non-sexual): a careful sip from your wrist. Take 1d6 necrotic damage (it can't reduce you below 1 HP). Valentin regains his full strength for the rest of the adventure (refresh 1 Gateway Aid) and +1 Allure. He bandages your wrist with his cravat.
  • Refuse: "Thank you for answering." He means it. +1 Allure. He fights on, slower (–1 Gateway Aid).

Then → go to 7.

entries.title: Lucan's Confrontation
entries.html:
Lucan appears in the chapel doorway, golden and smiling. "Ah. The exile and his little pet. Hand me the letter, and I'll let one of you live."

  • Fight (scaled: Lucan is a vampire spawn with 60 HP at L1 and 80 at L2, or 110 HP with Legendary Resistance 1/day at L3; plus remaining spawn). He flees if reduced to half HP: "This isn't over, exile." → Ending A or B (A if you have the Proof, B if you freed the villagers; both if both).
  • Stall until Morwenna arrives (Persuasion or Deception DC 14 for 2 rounds, or if you have her Invitation, she arrives automatically): the Countess steps out of the dark like a swallowed candle. "Lucan. Explain." → Ending A.
  • Accept Lucan's bargain: he offers a share in the coming "new order" and the Council vote if you hand him the Proof and Valentin. Valentin only watches you, not even surprised. → Ending C.

adventures.pitch:
Pitch: An exiled vampire gentleman has to ask your permission to enter your mirror, and everything after that. Tonight he needs you to walk into his ex-lover's masquerade and find proof that her steward framed him, before dawn and before the steward finds the cages you just opened.

Leads into: The Crimson Vintage (Side Adventure 4). One ending carries a Keystone lead for The Black Kiss (Morwenna recognizes Isaveth Sable).

solo.note: Written as "D&D 5e" gamebooks; DM Atlas runs them with the 2024 rules (SRD 5.2.1). Endings and riddle answers are DM-only when you run this for a group (use Group table mode).

partyHint: Solo or 3–5 players, levels 3–8 (solo entry adventures: levels 1–3)
